issue.title: Fresh install issue (1.0.5)

issue.body:
Sonarr/Radarr are able to use indexers with movies/shows because the consequences for getting the wrong movie or show is relatively low. However, with gaming being actual executable files that you are trusting, the consequences for getting a malicious file are high. I feel like because of this, it doesn't make sense to use indexers in the traditional sense. There is just too high of a risk to get a virus.

I just wanted to reach out and suggest an alternative. [Hydra Launcher](https://hydralauncher.gg/) is a game launcher that has automatic downloads similar to questarr. They have a system where instead of relying on indexers, they rely on user defined lists form where to look for to match games with torrent links. Websites like [this](https://library.hydra.wiki/) exist now where they provide a constant url for trusted sites where you can map games to their respective magnet link. For example, [this link](https://hydralinks.pages.dev/sources/fitgirl.json) maps all fitgirl downloads with a magnet link.

Incorporating something like this into questarr would alleviate the risk of downloading a virus. If this isn't a possibility, then I would suggest some sort of filter for the indexers. For example, at https://1337x.to/user/FitGirl/, you can see all of fitgirls repacks so that you wont have to walk the site blindly and trust some random person.

Ok I think I see the problem. My mistake was to think running the image alone was enough but it doesn't contain the DB so you would need to spin up a postgresql db yourself around it.

comments.body:
So today, the files you see when searching for a game depend only on the categories you use on your indexers. That means ROMs would be available if they are on the indexers and the categories are right. 
Then it's the matter of being able to add ROM specialized websites (with no API) as indexers.

Regarding the "downloading" part, since it is handled by the downloader you configure, it could be possible to configure it directly to handle the ROMs and saving it in the folder you want. But I think we'll need to set-up some download rule engine to e.G say if download comes from indexer X, it should be added with label Y

I had actually started following this project under the assumption it did support ROMs but I use Deluge as my downloader and was going to submit an enhancement request for that. However, seeing this, I think it's more important this be addressed first.

My expectations are as @SpaceFrags suggested. Similar to how Radarr or Sonarr work, we should be able to add games to our library and either manually search for them across indexers or have Questarr do the searching for us. Then Questarr would automatically import the ROM into the proper folder depending on the game console/system.

I use the Romm project to manage my library and play ROMs currently so having something like this to download the ROMs I'm missing and load them into the proper folder for Romm to pick up would really complement the existing system.
Working on this in #363

I'll need some testers for this branch because I don't use RomM myself so I'd benefit from real users. let me know here if you're interested and I'll let you know when you can build off the branch.
I'd recommend creating a separate questarr instance since this branch creates changes in the BDB.

I also do not use RomM, but I do use my roms on my server with streaming via Wolf and Steam (RetroArch) and need a way to manage, download, auto-import them and so on that is not just a file browser. 

I would love to test this out, so count me in!
I can definitely help with testing. I don't have an instance running yet, but I can build one when you have it ready and test it out. Happy to test out the Romm integration as well.

### Testing Request — `romm-integration` branch

This branch introduces the **RomM integration** and an import pipeline. I need your help validating it.

---

#### ⚠️ Important — Use a fresh instance

**Do NOT point this at your existing Questarr database.** This would break your database when upgrading later.

---

#### Recommended Setup

1.  Create a dedicated folder for this test instance — **do not reuse your existing Questarr folder**:

```bash
mkdir questarr-romm-test && cd questarr-romm-test
```

2. Create a `docker-compose.yml` in that folder with the following content. Make sure to update the mounts as needed. It can also be simplified to a single volume mount if everything can be found under it.

```yaml
services:
  app:
    image: ghcr.io/doezer/questarr:romm-testing
    ports:
      - "5001:5000"        # Different port to avoid conflicts with your main instance
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - SQLITE_DB_PATH=/app/data/sqlite.db
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
      # Downloader output path
      - /srv/downloads:/downloads
      # RomM library root (if testing RomM imports)
      - /srv/romm/library/roms:/romm/library/roms
    restart: unless-stopped
```

3. Then start:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

---

#### Where to focus in the UI

| Location | What to check |
|---|---|
| **Settings → Import → General Config tab** | Enable/disable post-processing master switch; all sub-options grey out correctly when disabled |
| **Settings → Import → RomM tab** | Library root path, platform routing mode, move mode (hardlink/copy/move), conflict policy, folder naming template, platform bindings and aliases editors |
| **Settings → Import → Path Mappings tab** | Add/edit/delete path mappings; file browser opens and resolves correctly |
| **Settings → Import → RomM → Platform Mappings section** | Add/delete IGDB platform → RomM platform name mappings |
| **Dashboard → Pending Manual Imports card** | Appears when imports need review; amber warning card with per-item Review button |
| **Pending Imports → Review modal** | Opens correctly per item, allows approving/rejecting the import |
| **Settings → Downloaders** | Download path field present for relevant clients |
| **File browser (path fields)** | Clicking browse opens the file browser; navigation works; path is applied on select |

---

### Test Scenarios

- Configure settings according to your structure
- Check that when a rom file is downloaded, it is imported to RomM library correctly (with correct slug)
- Check that when redownloading a file that already exists in library, while making sure settings are configured so no overwrite is authorized
- Check that when slug doesn't exist for the downloaded rom platform, the review pop-up is displayed (you can remove it from the settings)

---

#### Reporting issues

Please report any unexpected behaviour as a comment on this issue/PR, including:
- Which test scenario failed
- What you expected vs. what happened
- Any error messages from the browser console or Docker logs (`docker compose logs -f`)

issue.body:
It would be beneficial to update the package release pattern to include `:latest` and `:dev` tags. This would improve the user experience, provide clearer versioning guidance, and encourage wider adoption of the project.

A commonly adopted approach is:

- **`:latest`** – released on major and minor version updates (x.y in `x.y.z`, e.g., 1.0.4) to provide stable releases for most users.
- **`:dev`** – released on all versions (x, y, and z) to allow users to access the most recent changes and improvements.

Versioning should follow a clear ruleset based on [Semantic Versioning (SemVer)](https://semver.org/):

- **X** – major overhauls or breaking, non-backwards-compatible changes
- **Y** – new features
- **Z** – bug fixes or minor improvements

Any change to a previous version resets the next number as appropriate (e.g., `1.2.3` → `1.3.0` or `1.2.3` → `2.0.0`). Pre-release tags (e.g., `1.2.3-beta.1`) can also be used for experimental versions.

Automations can be set up to handle these releases automatically using CI/CD pipelines such as GitHub Actions

Additionally, [Tracarr](https://github.com/connorgallopo/Tracearr) provides a useful example with a `:supervised` Docker image, which includes the database and dependencies for one-click setup. This approach could be considered as a future enhancement to simplify onboarding for new users.

Okay i fixed it:

Problem: Questarr sends multi-word game titles (e.g. "Alabaster Dawn") directly as the Newznab q parameter. Games-focused indexers like G4u.to store releases under Scene names that use dots instead of spaces (Alabaster.Dawn.v0.1.0.6...). The indexer's tokenized search can't match the space-separated title against the dot-separated release name, returning 0 results.

Fix: In src/server/newznab.js, line ~72, replace spaces with dots in the query before sending it to the indexer:

Before:
url.searchParams.set("q", params.query);

After:
url.searchParams.set("q", params.query.replace(/ /g, "."));

This aligns the search query with how Scene releases are actually named on games-focused Newznab indexers. Single-word queries are unaffected.
You can check image questarr:v1.4.0-rc1 to verify correct implementation.

issue.body:
Just wanted to give some constructive feedback for the use of your product. It seems like you are caught up in adding a bunch of features without streamlining the installation process or even building a proper version management process. Right now users build their own docker container instead of pulling it from a registry with proper tags. There is no way for a user to understand the versioning of your product this way unless they look into each commit on the repository. This means that one user downloading one day might get a completely different experience the next day (since there is daily commits on the main branch). 

 feel like you need to take a step back and evaluate the use of docker in general in this product. The general method for deployment is to build containers and update them to registry's with tags. So you would use a "latest" tag for users to download. Then you would have a "testing" tag or something similar where you can play around and develop a new feature or fix a bug, and when you are ready to push it, you can update which image the "latest" tag points too. 

I feel like the above suggestions would fix alot of the day to day issues that pop up, because it seems like you have a alot of them in the github issues page.

Your docker compose example is also just needlessly complicated. I feel like the use of an environment file here is just not warranted. Docker compose files already have options for this that I feel like is being under utilized, especially with only a few variables to choose from.

Overall I love the product and your work with it and I don't really want to come off rude with this criticism; I just want to see this succeed. I just feel like people can't use it in its current state.

issue.body:
Ajout d’un filtre "Completed" pour la liste de téléchargements et ajout de badges indiquant la vitesse, l’ETA et le ratio. Le rendu des badges est conditionnel selon la disponibilité des données. Tests ajoutés pour la logique de rendu et le filtre.

Modifications attendues

- UI : nouveau filtre "Completed" dans la vue Downloads.
- UI : badges pour speed, ETA et ratio affichés sur chaque téléchargement.
- Rendu conditionnel : chaque badge s’affiche uniquement si la donnée correspondante est disponible/valide.
- Tests : unitaires/intégration pour couvrir le filtre et les cas de rendu (présence/absence de données).

Critères d’acceptation

- Le filtre "Completed" est visible et affiche uniquement les téléchargements complétés.
- Les badges speed / ETA / ratio apparaissent pour les éléments qui possèdent les données correspondantes.
- Les badges sont masqués quand les valeurs sont manquantes ou non calculables.
- Tests associés passent dans la CI.

Comment vérifier (manual)

1. Ouvrir la page Downloads.
2. Activer le filtre "Completed" → vérifier que seuls les téléchargements terminés sont listés.
3. Pour chaque élément terminé :
   - Vérifier que la vitesse s’affiche si > 0.
   - Vérifier que l’ETA s’affiche si calculable.
   - Vérifier que le ratio s’affiche si seeds/leechers sont connus.
4. Tester cas limites : éléments sans données (aucun badge), valeurs extrêmes, et accessibilité des badges (aria-label).

Notes d’implémentation

- Rendu conditionnel au niveau du composant affichant les métadonnées du téléchargement.
- Penser à ajouter des tests couvrant : présence/absence de données, format d’affichage, et filtrage côté UI.
- Mettre à jour les libellés/traductions si nécessaire.

Both Apprise API and CLI deliveries now include an absolute context URL when APP_URL is configured. Release-date notifications open the game's details page; actionable in-app notifications retain their download dialog.

- Preserve deployment subpaths, settings tabs and anchors; convert game-modal commands into navigable URLs for Apprise.
- Preserve the destination through login, including a reload of the login page, with local-path validation and rejection of login/setup destinations.
- Correct missing or generic destinations for download, import and Steam wishlist notifications; reject generated URLs escaping the instance origin or configured subpath.

## Description

Fixes #1280

With **Settings → Appearance → Platforms** set to several consoles including PS3 (e.g. Game Boy, GBC, GBA, GameCube, Wii, Wii U, PlayStation, PS2, PS3), the manual download dialog showed only PS3 releases. Everything else was hidden without a message, even releases whose platform `parseReleaseMetadata` detects correctly (e.g. `Wii`). `/api/search` returned the items; the dialog stayed empty.

**Cause.** `IGDB_ID_TO_CANONICAL_PLATFORM` in `shared/platforms.ts` listed only PC, PS3, PS4, PS5, Switch, Xbox Series, Xbox, Mac and Linux. `canonicalPlatformsForIgdbIds` drops every other selected id, so the selection above became `["PS3"]`. The `labels.length === 0` safeguard only covers a selection with *no* mappable platform, not a mixed one.

**Fix.**
- Build `IGDB_ID_TO_CANONICAL_PLATFORM` from `PLATFORM_CATALOG`, which already carries the IGDB ids for every label the release parser can emit (GB, GBC, GBA, GameCube, Wii, Wii U, PS1, PS2, N64, NDS, 3DS, PSP, …). The legacy `11 → "Xbox"` umbrella override is kept.
- In `matchesSelectedIgdbPlatform`, keep releases with no detected platform when part of the selection has no release label (e.g. Switch 2 + Switch). This extends the existing "the filter stays out of the way" rule to mixed selections.

Unchanged on purpose: with a selection whose platforms all have labels and no PC (e.g. only consoles), untagged releases are still hidden, as before.

## Screenshots

Shared-module change only (`shared/platforms.ts`); no `client/src/**` files touched.

- the nine-console selection above keeps GB, GBC, GBA, GameCube, Wii, Wii U, PS1, PS2 and PS3 releases and still drops PC and Switch;

pr.body:
Partially addresses #1276 (client side).

## Problem
The game download dialog sent a release search after every 300 ms pause in typing. Superseded searches were never cancelled, because the default React Query `queryFn` didn't pass the query's `signal` to `fetch`. Every partial query (`E`, `Examp`, `Example G`, …) therefore went out to all enabled indexers. Behind Prowlarr these requests queued up, hit timeouts and pushed the shared indexers into backoff.

## Changes
- `client/src/lib/queryClient.ts`: the default `getQueryFn` now passes React Query's abort `signal` to `apiFetch`/`fetch`. When the search text changes, the old query loses its observer and React Query aborts its HTTP request instead of leaving it to run alongside the new one. This applies to all default queries, which is the standard React Query behaviour for queries that become unobserved mid-fetch.
- `client/src/components/GameDownloadDialog.tsx`: the release-search debounce goes from 300 ms to 1000 ms (`SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS`). Typing at normal speed now leads to one search per pause rather than one per word fragment, in line with the 1–1.5 s suggested in the issue.
- Added a unit test checking that `getQueryFn` passes the abort signal to `fetch`.

## Not included
This PR does not cover the server-side suggestions:
- aborting indexer requests when the client disconnects
- per-indexer concurrency limits and de-duplication of identical in-flight queries
- a configurable Torznab timeout

Each of these changes `searchAllIndexers`, the Torznab/Newznab clients and `safeFetch`, and would be better as a separate PR. As a result, a cancelled browser request stops waiting for its response, but the server's request to the indexer still runs to completion. The longer debounce is what actually reduces the number of searches reaching the indexers.

I couldn't run the test suite in my environment, so the new test is unverified.

Fixes #1276

---
_Happy to adjust anything or close it if it isn't a fit._

pr.body:
## Description
Settings → Integrations now previews the linked account's owned Steam games and imports an explicit selection (up to 50) as Owned. This includes played free-to-play games and uses Steam's official GetOwnedGames API and exact Steam App ID → IGDB mappings, with Questarr's content filters and duplicate checks. It neither starts downloads nor touches files; existing statuses, ratings and progress stay unchanged. Exact IGDB matches may gain a missing Steam App ID so future previews recognize them. Normal account automation can apply to new Owned games afterward.

The server rechecks Steam ownership at import time, caps selection sizes, batches IGDB metadata and reads the library once per import, serializes same-account imports, preserves successful rows when others fail, and never accepts client-supplied Steam identities, credentials or mappings. Steam requests use safeFetch over HTTPS with a timeout; URLs/provider errors containing API keys are not logged. Responses are not cached. No new dependencies or schema migration.

## Differentiation rationale
This is the first increment toward a server-native view connecting storefront ownership, the backlog and local acquisition/import workflows. Questarr's PRD explicitly identifies the library centralizer and owned-library sync. Playnite offers broad library unification but requires Windows; Gameyfin emphasizes local-file scanning and browser delivery; ROMarr emphasizes acquisition and DAT verification. Steam import alone is not unique: the potential advantage is the combined workflow on a NAS/server without a running desktop launcher. Research, sources, prerequisites and limits are in [docs/STEAM_LIBRARY.md](https://github.com/Doezer/Questarr/blob/codex/monthly-differentiator-2026-10/docs/STEAM_LIBRARY.md).

This initial version is manual, separate from wishlist sync. GOG, periodic ownership reconciliation, license removal and multi-source provenance remain follow-ups.

## Screenshots
Captured from the running dev:test app. Steam responses are mocked for browser tests; no live Steam/IGDB credentials were available.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcTLuiRpTEvYjqjALStWY5Kw?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcTLuiRpTEvYjqjALStWY5Kw)_

Refs Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#60. Builds on #1270 (merged); the base is `main`.

Before: each install learned alone. The only way to give verified labels back to the model shipped with Questarr was to attach a CSV to an issue by hand.

After: in the "Release classification review" card, a "Share verified labels" block lets a user opt in.

- The switch **"Share my verified labels automatically"** is off by default. It is not an environment variable on purpose (consent is a UI choice) and is saved with the other classification settings (`shareLabels`).
- While it is ticked, a task "Label sharing" (every 6 hours, listed in System Tasks) sends the labels verified since the last run. A failure is logged, shown as a failed run, and retried at the next run.
- **"See what will be sent"** opens a dialog listing the exact rows and the address. **Send now** sends them without waiting; it is bound to the previewed batch (a batch id), so rows that changed since the preview are never sent unseen (409, preview again).

![Switch, off by default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/cf380a3be082f22b57b9492eed72489d543245fa/.github/pr-assets/label-sharing/switch-off.png)
![Preview dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/cf380a3be082f22b57b9492eed72489d543245fa/.github/pr-assets/label-sharing/preview.png)
![Preview dialog on a phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/cf380a3be082f22b57b9492eed72489d543245fa/.github/pr-assets/label-sharing/preview-mobile.png)

How: `server/classification/share.ts` builds the batch from rows with status `verified`, a known label and a game title, 200 rows at most, lengths capped. Each row carries four fields and nothing else: `releaseName`, `gameTitle`, `label`, `modelVersion`. The body is `{ "labels": [...] }`, posted with `redirect: "error"` and a 10 s timeout to a fixed address (`SHARE_URL`, no API key, no configurable URL). Sent rows are remembered as short hashes (release, game and label) in the system config (`classification.shared`, no migration), kept only for candidates still in the list, so a sent row is never offered again while it is queued and the list stays bounded. A corrected label is offered again. Selecting, posting and recording run one at a time, and consent is rechecked before every automatic batch. A failed or refused send remembers nothing. Routes: `GET /api/classification-candidates/share/preview` and `POST /api/classification-candidates/share` (needs the `batchId`). README and `docs/RELEASE_CLASSIFICATION.md` now say that labels stay on the server "unless you tick Share my verified labels automatically".

Open point: `SHARE_URL` is `https://labels.questarr.app/v1/labels`, a placeholder. The collector (Cloudflare Worker + D1) is in Iroise-IA/questarr-label-collector (merged, not deployed). Until it is deployed the task fails cleanly and keeps the rows.

Tests (`classification_share.test.ts`, both dialects): off by default, preview carries only verified rows with exactly four fields, no network call while off, one POST with `redirect: "error"` and the exact body, no repeat after success, rows kept after a refusal, batch binding, fingerprint retention, corrected labels, overlapping sends, the scheduled run, row cap.

pr.body:
Before: active learning only flagged a disagreement between the rules and the local model. When the cloud model contradicted the local model's best guess, nothing marked the release as a good example to label. Nothing told the user that releases were waiting in the review card either, so nobody went to look.

After: a release gets the reason `model_disagreement` ("Local and cloud models disagree") and a higher review priority when the cloud model names a different class than the local model's best guess. An expansion counts as a DLC, an update as a patch, a repack as a full game, and `unknown` never conflicts.

![Review card with the new reason](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/ca13583c9a882d22dd2a352f867b4a2bc7f15695/.github/pr-assets/model-disagreement/review.png)

Each time the waiting list reaches a multiple of 25 releases, every user also gets one notification, "Releases need your review". Clicking it opens Settings > Discovery & Downloads and scrolls to the review card.

![The notification in the bell](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/b6ecfbe2/.github/pr-assets/review-notification/bell.png)

![The review card after clicking it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/b6ecfbe2/.github/pr-assets/review-notification/review.png)

How: in `hybrid` mode the cloud is only asked when the local model abstained, so the comparison costs no extra request (`assessCandidate`). The "Ask the cloud model" button, still opt-in and one paid call per press, adds the same reason when its answer differs from the stored local guess (`disagreementUpdate`), and the reason is derived again when the release is seen again. The reasons are stored as JSON, so there is no migration. The notification is sent from `collectCandidate` when a new candidate brings the pending count to a multiple of 25 (`notifyReviewBacklog`). The settings page now reads `?tab=` to choose its tab, and the card has an `id` for the `#classification-review` anchor. Tests cover both disagreement paths, the class equivalences, the repeated button press and the notification threshold; the docs list the new reason and the notification.

pr.body:
### 💡 What
Replaced `.filter(...).length` array operations with a manual `for...of` counter inside a `useMemo` block in `client/src/components/CollectionDialog.tsx` and `client/src/components/GameJournalTab.tsx`.

### 🎯 Why
Using `.filter(...).length` for counting iterates through the entire array and allocates an intermediate array in memory containing the matched items, only to discard the array immediately after reading its `.length`. In heavily re-rendered components, this generates unnecessary garbage collection pressure and CPU overhead. By manually counting matches in a single pass, we achieve the same result with zero intermediate allocations.

### 📊 Impact
- Reduces memory allocations during render cycles for collections and achievements.
- Flattens array iteration complexity.
- Helps avoid frontend jank on large datasets.

### 🔬 Measurement
Run `npm run test` and observe that the logic produces identical counts with improved memory efficiency.

Before: in `cloud` mode every search called the TypeSafe model again for the same release names (top 15 results), and each call is paid. The hybrid/local pipeline already had an in-memory cache, the cloud path had none.

After: `typesafeClient.analyzeRelease` keeps a 24 h in-memory cache (2,000 entries). A repeated name, size and platform is served from memory. The key includes the provider settings revision and the model id, so changing the key, URL or model never serves old answers. A failed call is not cached and is retried next time.

How: cache map inside `server/typesafe.ts`, three tests in `typesafe.test.ts` (repeat, settings change, failed call), one line in `docs/RELEASE_CLASSIFICATION.md`. Nothing survives a restart; the persistent cache for every pipeline is tracked in Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#59.

Does not touch `client/src/**`.

pr.body:
Before: releases the classifier was unsure about were decided (or passed through as `unknown`) and forgotten, so there was no cheap way to turn them into training examples.

After: with `ACTIVE_LEARNING_COLLECT=true` (default off), unsure releases are kept and can be labeled in Settings, exported in the existing dataset format, and merged into the labeled CSV before a manual retrain. With the flags off nothing is collected, no request is made and the card does not render.

Refs Questarr-mgmt#36 (ADR-001 task 6).

## How

- **Collection** (`server/classification/active-learning.ts`, hooked in the auto-download check in `server/cron.ts`): local/hybrid mode only, never when a layer failed. Reasons: `unresolved`, `low_confidence` (< 85 %), `disagreement` (rules vs the local model's best guess, via the new `LocalTfidfClassifier.guess`). One row per release and game (normalized key), `seenCount` on repeats, cap 5,000. A reviewed row is never reset to pending.
- **Four kinds of label stay apart**: rule output and local guess are stored as signals; a cloud suggestion is stored with model, confidence and time and shown as "not verified"; only a label the user gives (`status = verified`, `humanLabel`) is exportable.
- **Table** `classification_candidates` on SQLite and Postgres (migrations `0053` / `0017`, parity types, `TABLE_ORDER`, `server/db/tables.ts`, both storage implementations).
- **API** `/api/classification-candidates` (behind the existing `/api` auth gate): list (ranked: unresolved/disagreement first, bonus for classes with few verified examples), review (`accept` / `correct` / `ambiguous` / `reject`), `suggest` (403 unless `ACTIVE_LEARNING_CLOUD_SUGGEST=true`, one paid call per press, provider failure leaves the row untouched), CSV export of verified rows only, delete (all or by status).
- **UI**: "Release classification review" card in Settings > Discovery & Downloads, rendered only when collection is on or candidates exist.
- **Dataset**: `scripts/release-benchmark/merge-candidates.ts` appends exported rows without duplicates, reports label conflicts without overwriting, and skips games present in a separate held-out file. No automatic retrain or deploy.
- **Docs**: `docs/RELEASE_CLASSIFICATION.md` (new section incl. export, merge, re-evaluate, retrain, delete) and `.env.example`.

Desktop:

![Review card, desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/9ae3bb559f9e285b322da1b0d5b0c3fbaf50254b/.github/pr-assets/active-learning/card-desktop.png)

## Description

Fixes #1253 (image ~373 MB compressed).

- **Prune in a build stage.** New `prod-deps` stage runs `npm prune --omit=dev`; the production stage copies `node_modules` from it. Before, the full dev tree was copied (169 MB layer) and only hidden by a later prune layer.

Expected size is ~200 MB compressed per the issue's estimate. **Not built locally** (no Docker daemon in my environment), so the size gain and PUID/PGID startup are unverified: please check the CI Docker build and run the image once.

Sourced from node-forge's changelog.

1.4.1 - 2026-10-27

Notes

  • This release involved coordinating many security reports from many groups, people, and robots over too long period of time. Thank you for your reports and patience.
  • Claude Code was used to help organize, track, untangle, merge, test, validate, fix, and improve it all. Further verification of fixes would be welcome.

Security

  • HIGH: Signature forgery in RSA-PKCS due to ASN.1 extra field in DigestAlgorithm.
    • RSASSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts forged signatures for low public exponent keys (e=3). The fix for CVE-2026-33894 only checked the element count of the outer DigestInfo. Attackers can add "garbage" elements inside the nested DigestAlgorithm SEQUENCE in order to construct a signature that passes verification, enabling Bleichenbacher style forgery.
    • Reported by Geo (@​geo-chen).
    • CVE ID: CVE-2026-85393
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-2g46-22mc-6gwp
  • HIGH: Signature forgery in RSA-PKCS due to non-canonical DigestInfo encoding.
    • RSASSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts non-canonical DigestInfo encodings, such as NULL parameters with content, non-minimal length encodings, and non-canonical OIDs. These provide attackers space to construct forged signatures for low public exponent keys (e=3), similar to CVE-2026-33894 and CVE-2026-85393.
    • Reported by Oren Yomtov (Fireblocks), Bronson Yen (Calif.io, in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research), Kamil Hałajda, @​pzartech, @​antonlissone, and @​Brechard.
    • CVE ID: CVE-TBD
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-6qrw-m8cv-hcxf
  • HIGH: ASN.1 resource exhaustion via BIT STRING decoding.
    • An Uncontrolled Recursion (CWE-674) and Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (CWE-400) vulnerability in node-forge versions 1.4.0 and below enables remote, unauthenticated attackers to exhaust CPU and memory with small crafted DER or PEM inputs (certificates, keys, and other structures parsed with asn1.fromDer()). By default fromDer() attempts to decode BIT STRING contents as ASN.1. That decode ignored the global asn1.maxDepth and the per-call maxDepth option, and BIT STRINGs nested in decoded BIT STRINGs were decoded too, with each level keeping a full copy of its decoded contents. Memory use grew quadratically with the nesting depth and can terminate the process from heap exhaustion. The maxDepth bypass is an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-66031.

pr.body:
Before: release classification was Jev-only. Without a TypeSafe key, nothing checked whether an unattended download was a patch, a DLC or a crack. The deterministic rules layer existed but was not wired.

After: an orchestrator runs rules, then a local tf-idf model, then the cloud provider, selected by `CLASSIFICATION_MODE`. The default is `hybrid`: it needs no key, and asks the cloud only when the local model abstains, fails or is not installed. `local` never leaves the server. `cloud` is the legacy Jev-only check, unchanged. A release no layer can classify stays `unknown` and is never turned into `full_game`.

Refs Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#35 (ADR-001 task 5), parent #1.

## What changes

- `shared/release-tfidf.ts`: pure-TypeScript tf-idf + logistic regression inference and a validated model file format, shared with the benchmark trainer (a test checks that the exported file scores identically to the trained model).
- `server/classification/`: local layer, cloud adapter over the existing TypeSafe client (Jev stays the default cloud model; another compatible model is a `typesafe.model` setting), pipeline with bounded timeouts, structured logs, model/version metadata and a 24 h cache keyed by pipeline, mode and model versions. Failures and timeouts are not cached.
- `server/cron.ts`: in `local` and `hybrid` mode the auto-download hold uses the pipeline. It holds patch/dlc/expansion and the crack_only, demo, soundtrack and other_artifact flags. `cloud` mode runs the previous code path untouched.
- `scripts/release-benchmark/export-model.ts`: trains on the private dataset and writes the model file. The model is not committed; users generate it and drop it in `<database folder>/models/` (or `CLASSIFIER_MODEL_PATH`).
- `docs/RELEASE_CLASSIFICATION.md`: modes, install steps, operations, compatibility.

## Behaviour changes

- **The default mode is now `hybrid`** (decided by the project owner: the cloud mode needs a paid key, so it cannot be the default). Without a key and without a model file only the rules run, so a release the rules identify as a patch, DLC, crack, demo or soundtrack is held for review before an unattended download. Before, nothing was checked without a key. `CLASSIFICATION_MODE=cloud` restores the previous behaviour.
- `CLASSIFICATION_HOLD_UNKNOWN=true` holds releases no layer could classify. Off by default, so `unknown` goes through as today.
- Search-result AI badges still use Jev only.

## Testing

- New tests: model round trip and validation, local threshold and abstention, cloud mapping, every mode and fallback (hang, throw, abstain, no layer), degraded results and cache rules, production wiring, and the cron hold.
- `npm run lint`, `tsc`, `npm run build` and the full `vitest run` are green.

No `client/src` change, so no screenshot. No Dockerfile, database or API change.

pr.body:
## Description

ADR-001 Task 4 (Questarr-mgmt #34): training and evaluation scripts that compare local classifiers for release classification, and the measured model-selection record. Before: only a pure-TypeScript TF-IDF baseline and Jev numbers existed. After: `scripts/release-classifier-training/` compares TF-IDF + logistic regression, MiniLM (frozen and fine-tuned), DistilBERT and an int8 ONNX export on the benchmark's own game-grouped split, with calibration, abstention thresholds and CPU measurements.

The recommendation (in `DECISION.md`) is to ship the pure-TypeScript TF-IDF + logistic regression path first (80.7% test accuracy, 175 KB as JSON, under 1 ms, no new dependency). A fine-tuned MiniLM-L6 in int8 ONNX (23 MB) measured 2 to 5 points higher, inside the noise of an 88-row test part, and needs `onnxruntime-web` or `onnxruntime-node`: that is the task's approval gate and is not taken here.

- No runtime code, dependency or Docker change. The Python dependencies are training-only (`requirements-train.txt`).
- No dataset and no model file is committed. `export-splits.ts` reads the private CSV and writes the split JSON locally.
- Laya was not measured (installing its package was not authorized); see `DECISION.md`.

How: `export-splits.ts` reuses `groupedSplit` and `importDataset` from the benchmark so Python scores the same rows. Metrics mirror `metrics.ts`. Hyperparameters, epochs, temperature and thresholds use validation (or out-of-fold predictions of train+validation) only; the test part is scored once.

Not applicable: no `client/src/**` change.

Release notes

Sourced from semgrep's releases.

Release v1.181.0

1.181.0 - 2026-10-14

### Changed

  • semgrep scan now uses the same asynchronous configuration generation and retries as semgrep ci when fetching platform scan configurations. (CODE-9930)

  • Python only: Supply Chain now reports every package declared in a requirements.txt, not only the ones pinned with ==. A requirement with a version range (requests>=2.0, numpy~=1.26, django==2.2.*, requests (>=2.0)) is reported with the declared specifier as its version, and a bare name (flask) is reported with an empty version, so they appear in the dependency inventory and SBOM instead of being dropped with a "not pinned to an exact version" parse error. These dependencies have no definitive installed version, so for now they produce no Supply Chain findings. When there is no requirements.in manifest to consult, a range or bare-name line is reported as a direct dependency, since it was declared by hand rather than written by a resolver; exact pins keep their previous unknown transitivity. Local path and URL lines are no longer reported as parse errors, while a line whose leading token is not a valid package name (requests$foo>=1) is now reported as a parse error instead of being dropped silently. Other ecosystems and other Python manifest formats are unchanged. (SC-3487)

  • pro: Various performance improvements for historical secrets scanning. (SCRT-983-historical-performance)

  • go grammar update (v0.23.4):

    • Go target parsing now supports composite type-set constraints and shorthand union constraints on type parameters, preserving underlying-type markers and all union members. Literal generic rule-pattern syntax remains unchanged.
    • Go target parsing now supports embedded generic struct fields, including pointer and package-qualified embeddings, while retaining their type arguments.
    • Go target parsing now supports standalone generic function instantiations with multiple or composite type arguments, such as Pair[int, string] and Identity[[]int], including qualified function names.
    • Go target parsing now accepts Unicode decimal digits after the first character of an identifier, including Arabic-Indic and Devanagari digits.

    (go-v0.23.4)

  • Hack grammar update:

    • Hack target parsing now supports capability lists on functions, methods, function types, lambdas, and anonymous functions, including empty lists and context-dependent capabilities.
    • Hack target parsing now supports context constants with capability bounds or initializers, preserving the distinction between super bounds, as bounds, and assigned capabilities. Unbounded abstract context constants retain their existing representation limitation.
    • Hack target parsing now supports concrete and abstract enum classes with typed members, plus qualified and unqualified enum class labels.
    • Hack target parsing now supports function and static-method references with empty or explicit type arguments, such as foo<> and MyClass::bar.
    • Hack target parsing now preserves type arguments on calls and constructors such as foo(), $obj->bar(...), and new MyClass(...), matching other languages' typed-call representation.
    • Hack target parsing now supports expression-tree literals such as Example1 + 2, preserving the visitor and body text. Embedded DSL bodies remain opaque rather than being parsed as Hack expressions.
    • Hack target parsing now supports file-level attributes such as <<file: SomeAttribute(...)>>, preserving attribute names and arguments.
    • Hack target parsing now supports internal visibility on methods and properties, keeping it distinct from public, protected, and private visibility.
    • Hack target parsing now accepts namespace-relative names such as namespace\run() and include/require member names in piped expressions.

    (hack-1a7ded90288189746c54861ac144ede97df95081)

### Fixed

  • pro: Historical secrets scanning no longer aborts when preparatory git gc fails. (SCRT-982-historical-gc-nonfatal)
  • Supply Chain: lockfileless Gradle resolution now tells the dependency graph plugin where to write its report, so builds that relocate their build directory resolve instead of failing. When the plugin writes no report, the scan reports a resolution error that includes the Gradle log instead of crashing on the missing file. (code-9953)
  • Supply Chain: lockfileless Gradle and Maven scans now report incomplete dependency resolution when dependencies or transitive metadata cannot be resolved. Registry HTTP failures include the affected URL when available. (sc-3358)

### Infra/Release Changes

  • Forward optional job context when registering CLI scans. (SMS-3333)

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcSqrboZQNcGhhqTuApSgfvE)_

## Summary
Implements Questarr-mgmt #52: one "can I grab this safely?" verdict per search result, assembled only from signals that already exist.

- `shared/release-trust.ts`: pure `deriveReleaseTrust(evaluation, signals)` returns `trusted | unverified | risky` plus the list of reasons. Computed from rejection codes and facts, not from the score, so overriding built-in rule weights cannot turn a nuked release into a trusted one.
- Download dialog: new `ReleaseTrustBadge` before the score badge, popover lists each reason.
- Auto-search: the "Auto-downloaded result" log now carries the trust level and reason codes.

## Rules
- **risky**: nuked on xREL, executable payload, non-game media, blacklisted.
- **trusted**: accepted, clear title match, no xREL size mismatch, and hard-to-fake evidence: an xREL listing whose size matches (±25%), or a preferred group when xREL could be checked.
- **unverified**: everything else, including whenever xREL could not be checked.

## Reliability fixes found while reviewing the signals
- A release name on xREL alone is no longer enough for "trusted" (anyone can reuse a scene name). The xREL size is now carried through and compared; a size mismatch blocks `trusted` even for a preferred group.
- New `xrel: "unavailable"` evaluation state (slow or failed lookup), shown as "xREL?" instead of looking like "not on xREL". Previously the result was silent.
- An xREL reply with neither release list is now an error, not "no releases" (it was cached and marked everything not found).

## Not in this PR
Antivirus is not a signal of this badge (decided with Vincent: it will not be used), and crack status stays per game, so neither feeds the per-result verdict. Blacklisted results are still removed from manual search, so that reason only matters if they are shown later. Auto-search still grabs after one deferred cycle when xREL stays down; it is now visible in the log as unavailable.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run check`, `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run test:run` (4304 passed; the badge uses text only because the GameDownloadDialog suite mocks lucide-react)
- [x] New tests: `shared/__tests__/release-trust.test.ts`, xREL size conversion, empty xREL reply

## Visual evidence
The component is rendered by the real code (Vite dev server, harness page with the real `evaluateRelease` + `deriveReleaseTrust`), not the full dialog behind a seeded indexer.

![unverified reasons](``https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/6239ef81709b16e1249ecd4c483fe302c5070bf1/.github/pr-assets/trust-badge/unverified-reasons-mobile.png``)

Bumps the npm_and_yarn group with 2 updates in the / directory: [fast-uri](https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri) and [ip-address](https://github.com/beaugunderson/ip-address). Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.8 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

## Summary

Two independent fixes that unblock the failing Dependabot PRs.

- **#1245 (production group)**: `js-yaml` 5.5.0 pulls in `argparse@3.0.4`, which declares `PSF-2.0` instead of `Python-2.0` (same license, new SPDX id), so the `license-checker --onlyAllow` step of `sca-scan` failed. `PSF-2.0` is added to the allow-list in `ci.yml`, `deploy.yml` and `docs/VULNERABILITY_MANAGEMENT.md`.
- **#1244 (dev-dependencies)**: vitest 5.0.5 throws when code reads an export that a `vi.mock` factory does not define. The `node:net` mock in `api_routes.test.ts` only exposed `Socket`, so `isSafeUrl` (which calls `isIP`) made 13 route tests return 500 (reproduced locally: `No "isIP" export is defined on the "node:net" mock`). The mock now spreads the original module.

## Test plan

- [x] `api_routes.test.ts` passes with vitest 5.0.5 (375/375); it failed 13 tests before the change.
- [x] On the #1245 tree, `check:overrides` and `audit-prod` pass; only the license step failed. License check passes on main with the extended list.
- [ ] After merge, `·@·d·ependabot r·ebase` on #1244 and #1245; #1238 should rebase cleanly once #1244 is in.

v6.0.0

6.0.0 (2026-10-19)

Features

  • effect-ts: support Effect v4 (#880) (a5ab308), closes #878

BREAKING CHANGES

  • effect-ts: the effect-ts resolver now requires effect@^4.0.0; Effect v3 is no longer supported. Schemas must be migrated to the Effect v4 Schema API (e.g. Schema.nonEmptyString() -> .check(Schema.isNonEmpty()), Schema.Union(a, b) -> Schema.Union([a, b]), Schema.transform -> Schema.decodeTo). Error type values follow Effect v4 issue tags: Type -> InvalidType, Missing -> MissingKey, Refinement -> Filter, Unexpected -> UnexpectedKey, plus new AnyOf and InvalidValue. Default error messages now come from Effect v4 (e.g. is missing -> Missing key, and the received value is no longer included).

Release notes

v30.1.3

  • Improved performance of getComputedStyle() and computed CSS property reads, including with stylesheets containing attribute selectors. (@​scttcper, @​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed slowdowns when focusing elements and running interaction tests, which regressed in v30.1.2. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed XMLHttpRequest reusing credentials supplied to xhr.open() after cross-origin redirects, including in response to authentication challenges from the destination.
  • Fixed XMLHttpRequest incorrectly sending and accepting cookies after cross-origin redirects back to the document's origin when xhr.withCredentials is false.
  • Fixed exceptions from malformed CSS math functions, such as calc(0px - @submenu_space), while parsing documents, stylesheets, and style declarations. (@​rnavarro)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() ignoring style rules nested inside multiple @media rules.
  • Fixed CSS shorthands overwriting longhands with higher priority or specificity during style computation, including declarations containing CSS variables.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() returning unresolved or inconsistent shorthand values, including for 'background', 'border', 'flex', 'font', 'margin', and 'padding', and incorrect shorthand defaults and inheritance.
  • Fixed computed background positions to resolve font-relative lengths using the final font size and handle multiple image layers correctly.
  • Fixed computed 'color' values depending on property read order, including unresolved color-mix() results, which regressed in v29.0.2.
  • Fixed currentcolor border colors incorrectly becoming transparent when 'color' uses light-dark() or relative color syntax.
  • Fixed CSS calculations that reduce to a percentage incorrectly producing pixel values, which regressed in v30.0.0.
  • Fixed numeric font weights in the 'font' shorthand incorrectly setting 'line-height'.
  • Fixed selector matching involving XML namespaces, and selectors such as [data-a|=""] failing to match empty values and values beginning with -. (@​asamuzaK)

pr.body:
Before: the deterministic classifier (#1226) and Jev could not be compared. There was no way to measure how often a classifier is right, how often it stays silent, or what it costs.

After: `npm run bench:releases -- --dataset <file>` imports a human-labeled dataset, validates it, splits it by game and scores every classifier on the same parts, writing `results.json` and `report.md`. The 298 labeled releases are not in this repo: they live in the private `Doezer/Questarr-mgmt` repository (Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#50), and `--dataset` points at them.

What it does: the split is by game, so no game has releases in two parts. Trained classifiers fit on `train` only and every classifier is scored on `validation` and `test`. Accuracy, per-class precision/recall/F1, macro F1, confusion matrix, abstention rate, precision of the non-`unknown` answers, latency (p50/p95) and, when a provider reports it, tokens and cost. A value a provider did not report prints as `n/a`, never 0. `expansion` is folded into `dlc` (labels and classifier answers), as decided with the dataset owner.

How: `scripts/release-benchmark/` only. It is not imported by the server or client, adds no dependency, and does not touch the production runtime. Classifiers: the deterministic rules, a pure-TypeScript character n-gram TF-IDF + logistic regression baseline (name only, and with the game title as context), Jev through the System One contract, and any OpenRouter chat model. Cloud classifiers run only when named in `--classifiers` with their key set, and each stops at `--max-calls`. The OpenRouter key is only sent to an `https://openrouter.ai` URL. The Jev OpenRouter route was exercised by the labeling run, not by this PR's tests, which mock `fetch`.

Measured offline on the real dataset (seed 42, 57 test releases from a split by game, so differences of a few points are noise):

| Classifier | Accuracy | Macro F1 | Abstention | Auto-accept precision |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| deterministic | 73.7% | 68.3% | 59.6% | 91.3% |
| tfidf | 78.9% | 75.9% | 38.6% | 71.4% |
| tfidf-title | 84.2% | 81.4% | 38.6% | 77.1% |

Jev and OpenRouter models were not run here (no credentials in this environment). Their results come from running the command above.

pr.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcWqbgFptvo6YQTTdzBT3ZVN)_

## Summary

A user reported that Library Import does not discover Switch games correctly. Typical dumps are flat files such as `Game [0100F2C0115B6000][v0].nsp`, with the update and each DLC as separate files. Three things went wrong:

- **Polluted IGDB query.** `cleanReleaseName` kept the hex title id (`[0100F2C0115B6000]` is not a numeric or known tag), so the search was `Game 0100F2C0115B6000` and nothing matched. `.nsz`/`.xcz` were not stripped either, and `(UPD)` stayed in the name.
- **No platform hint.** Switch files were searched against all IGDB games.
- **Updates and DLC treated as unrelated games.** Each file was its own candidate, categorized by name only (a "Complete Edition" base game read as DLC, an update read as main), and a DLC named differently from its base game ended up in Needs Review.

## Changes

- `shared/title-utils.ts`: strip Switch title ids, add `nsz`, `xcz`, `upd` to the release tags, and add `parseSwitchTitleId()` (base, update or DLC, plus a family key shared by a game, its update and its DLC).
- `server/library-scanner.ts`:
  - searches IGDB with the Switch platform (130) first when a title id is present, falling back to an unfiltered search;
  - files with a title id get their category from it (main / update / dlc);
  - candidates are processed base first, and updates/DLC attach to the base game found in the same scan (or an already linked one) through the title id family;
  - nothing changes for non-Switch names.
- Tests: scanner end to end on `.nsp` files (base, update, DLC attach to one game, platform hint, no Needs Review entry) and title utils.

No schema change, no client change. `npm run check`, eslint and the full Vitest run pass.

## Not included

Still one candidate per top-level file, so a Switch DLC without a matching base file in the same root goes to Needs Review as before. May conflict textually with #1239 (same file, different area).

pr.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc2jumTXqNCEJiuhx57fENCj)_

## Summary

Implements Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#47 (requested in #1204): a non-game folder in Needs Review (e.g. Proton builds next to games in a Steam folder) can now be ignored for good.

- **Ignore** button on each Needs Review card. The folder leaves the list immediately and later scans skip it (no IGDB lookup either).
- New **Ignored Folders** list on the Library Import page with a **Restore** action. Restoring queues a rescan of that root folder so the folder returns to Needs Review.
- New table `library_scan_ignored (id, root_folder_id → root_folders ON DELETE CASCADE, folder_name, created_at)` with a unique index on `(root_folder_id, folder_name)`.
  - SQLite: `migrations/0052_library_scan_ignored.sql`
  - Postgres mirror: `shared/schema.pg.ts`, `shared/schema-parity.ts` + parity test, `migrations-pg/0016_library_scan_ignored.sql`, `TABLE_ORDER` in `scripts/sqlite-to-pg.ts`, `server/db/tables.ts`
- API: `POST /api/library/scan/unmatched/ignore` (resolved against the server-side queued entry like `match`, never joined onto a path), `GET /api/library/scan/ignored`, `DELETE /api/library/scan/ignored/:id`.
- Already linked folders are unaffected (the linked check runs before the ignore check).
- Not included: the optional default ignore patterns (`Proton*`, `Steam Linux Runtime*`) toggle from the issue.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check`, `npm run lint`
- [x] Vitest: scanner (ignored folder skipped, ignore persists + leaves review, refuses unqueued names), routes, storage (incl. cascade on root folder removal), schema parity, `RootFolderDiscovery` component
- [x] Manual run on `dev:test` with a real root folder: ignore → rescan keeps it out → restore brings it back (screenshots below)

Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.8 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

# Pull Request

## Description

User report on NZBGet: setting a default unpack (archive) password makes sending a download fail with a "not over HTTPS" error, even with the unencrypted-traffic option ("Allow insecure LAN") ticked. A second report from the same user: a download that fails in NZBGet on a missing/wrong archive password is marked failed with no reason, and is not restored after fixing the password and re-running post-processing in NZBGet.

Causes and fixes:

- **HTTPS refusal.** `resolveArchivePassword()` (`shared/archive-password.ts`) only looked at the URL scheme and ignored `allowInsecureLan`; NZBGet also forced `requireHttps` on the password-bearing `append` call even when the request started on HTTP. The guard now honours `allowInsecureLan` (NZBGet and SABnzbd), and the redirect pin only applies when the request itself is HTTPS (same approach as qBittorrent/Deluge). Without the opt-in, plain HTTP is still refused, with a message that now mentions the option.
- **No failure reason.** NZBGet history failures now set `error` from the `<overall>/<detail>` status (`FAILURE/PASSWORD`, `UNPACK`, `PAR`, `HEALTH`, `BAD`, `DISK`, ...), instead of "Aborted by downloader (no details provided)".
- **No restore.** New `storage.getRecentFailedUsenetDownloads()` plus `recoverFailedUsenetDownloads()` in `server/cron.ts`: usenet rows marked failed in the last 14 days are re-checked against the client; if it no longer reports an error (downloading, repairing, unpacking, completed), the row goes back to `downloading` and the normal tracker/import takes over. Rows still reported as failed stay failed.

Backend-only change, no UI touched.

## Summary

Part of #1204 (point "remember what was matched after a manual review").

The library scanner rebuilt its Needs Review list from scratch on every scan and re-queried IGDB for every folder. A folder matched by hand could therefore come back in Needs Review on the next rescan whenever its folder name scored below the auto-match threshold.

Now `runScan` loads the `libraryPath` of existing games once. A candidate whose path is already linked to a game:
- is not scored against IGDB and never lands in Needs Review;
- still gets new files recorded (`assignFilesToGame` already skips known paths).

No schema change, no client change.

Scheduled/automatic rescans, a persistent "ignore this folder" action, and better IGDB matching are larger and need verification, so they are separate backlog issues.

pr.body:
Before: nothing in Questarr tells a full game from a patch, a DLC or an expansion; scoring only reasons about the title match.

After: `classifyReleaseByRules` returns a class (`full_game`, `expansion`, `patch`, `dlc`, or internal `unknown`) with the rule ids that fired. It is not wired into search or auto-download yet; this is the rules layer of the hybrid pipeline in ADR-001 (Questarr-mgmt #31 to #36).

It never defaults to `full_game`: a bare title only counts as a full game when it exactly matches the known game title, otherwise the answer is `unknown` (`unknown.no-evidence`), and conflicting evidence gives `unknown.conflict`. Soundtracks, other artifacts, demos and crack-only releases are `unknown` with a flag; repacks are flagged from the raw title. `confidence` is null for rules, so a later model can fill it in without changing the shape.

How: `shared/release-classification.ts` (pure, shared client/server), a `ReleaseClassifier` interface and rules adapter in `server/classification/types.ts`, and 35 unit tests in `shared/__tests__/release-classification.test.ts`. No UI change, no schema change, no behavior change in search.

Tests: new unit tests pass; `tsc` and ESLint clean.

pr.body:
_Requested by **Vincent** · follow-up to #1198 (Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#22). Stacked on #1221, which is stacked on #1198: merge those first, then retarget this one to `main`._

## Description

Before: the SeerrNG provider answered the v2 core routes only. `catalog/games/{igdbId}/editions` and `catalog/discover` did not exist, and a request carrying `selection` was refused with a 400.

After: the three v2.1 items of the QuestarrNG contract are implemented and advertised in the handshake (`editions`, `discover`).

- **Editions**: `GET catalog/games/{igdbId}/editions` lists the editions IGDB links with `version_parent`, the content linked to each edition, and the standalone add-ons of the base game, with `owned` from the library. Content IGDB does not describe stays unknown (`storyContent: null`, `contentKnown: false`). Updates (IGDB type 14) are never listed.
- **Discovery**: `GET catalog/discover` filters on IGDB theme, mode, perspective, genre and language ids (include = any, exclude = none of), `q`, `minYear`, `maxHoursToBeat` and an offset cursor, with the content filters of the account applied.
- **Selection** on `POST requests`: `edition` makes Questarr acquire that edition as the game; `missing-selected` requests the base game and adds each selected add-on to the library as a wanted game. The ledger keeps the selection (`integration_requests.selection`, SQLite 0051, Postgres 0015) and the request state gets the `content` block (`mode`, `pending`, `acquiredCount`). Unknown edition or add-on ids, or a selection without `igdbId`, are a 400; replaying an id with another selection is a 409. Cancelling also shelves the add-ons that are still wanted.

Decisions taken (easy to change): add-ons are plain library games, so retry and asset delivery follow the base game only; discovery treats every id list as "any of"; `wantedContent` is not advertised. Details are in `docs/SEERRNG.md`.

Not run against the live IGDB API or a real SeerrNG build: the queries follow IGDB's documented syntax and are covered by Questarr's own tests (50 in `seerrng_provider`).

Backend only, no UI change.

pr.body:
Before: a new release profile started with no custom formats, so crack-only, demo, trainer and similar releases scored like the game itself until the user wrote their own rules.

After: new profiles are seeded with six recommended formats, and existing users get an "Add recommended formats" button in Settings > Release Scoring that installs the missing ones (matched by name, idempotent, serialized per user).

![Recommended formats](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/eaba7b3d/.github/pr-assets/default-formats/recommended-formats.png)

(The screenshot predates one rename: "Pre-installed or portable" is now "Pre-installed".)

| Format | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Crack, fix or NoCD only (explicit forms such as "crack only", "crackfix", "nocd") | -300 |
| Demo, playtest or trial | -150 |
| Trainer, keygen or activator | -500, rejects |
| Pre-installed | -40 |
| Includes updates and DLC | +25 |
| Trusted repackers (FitGirl, DODI, ElAmigos, KaOsKrew, GOG) | +20 |

Updates and DLC are searched for too, so nothing penalizes a release for being one, and a full game shipped "+ Crack" is not penalized. Matching is whole-word, case-insensitive, on the title (RE2, no lookarounds); the formats are ordinary custom formats the user can edit, disable or delete. The trusted-repackers list is opinionated and optional.

How: `shared/default-custom-formats.ts` holds the list, `createInitialConfig` seeds it, `POST /api/custom-formats/install-defaults` installs the missing ones. Existing profiles are not changed unless the user clicks the button.

Tests: unit tests for the regexes (valid, whole-word, reject, near-misses) and for seeding, installing and overlapping installs on SQLite and Postgres; existing service and route tests updated for the seeded formats.

pr.body:
## Description

**Empty platform/genre lists were cached for a day.** `/api/igdb/platforms` and `/api/igdb/genres` always send `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`. Before IGDB is configured, both return `[]`. If Settings → Platforms was opened before IGDB was set up, the browser keeps that empty response and shows "IGDB returned no platforms. Try again in a few seconds." for up to 24 hours, without contacting the server again. The Retry button doesn't help because it only appears on errors. These routes now send `no-store` when the list is empty and keep the 24-hour cache for non-empty lists.

**The primary platforms query matched nothing.** `getPlatforms()` filtered on `category = (1, 5, 6)`, but IGDB has deprecated `category` on platforms in favour of `platform_type` and the old filter now returns no rows. Every call fell through to the unfiltered `name != null` query, so the picker listed every platform. It now filters on `platform_type = (1, 4, 5, 6)`: console, operating system, portable console and computer. Type 4 is included because IGDB files PC (Microsoft Windows), Mac and Linux there, and PC is the first entry in `FALLBACK_PLATFORMS`.

Tests:
- `api_routes.test.ts`: a non-empty platform list keeps the 24-hour cache; an empty one gets `no-store` (fails on `main`).
- `igdb_extended.test.ts`: the primary platforms query uses `platform_type` and not `category` (fails on `main`).

## Screenshots

Backend-only change.

# Pull Request _Template_

## Description

Suivi de #1198, empilé sur sa branche (la table `integration_requests` n'est pas encore sur `main` : fusionner #1198 d'abord, la base de cette PR passera alors sur `main`).

Aujourd'hui seul le code (file d'attente par utilisateur + `attachExistingGameLocked`) empêche deux demandes actives sur le même jeu. Cette PR ajoute la garantie côté base : un index unique **partiel** `integration_requests_live_game_idx` sur `(user_id, provider, game_id)`, limité aux lignes où `game_id` n'est pas nul et `status <> 'cancelled'`.

Pourquoi partiel : une demande annulée garde son `game_id` jusqu'à ce qu'une nouvelle demande reprenne le jeu, donc elle ne doit pas bloquer la reprise. Les demandes sans jeu (échec avant l'ajout, jeu supprimé) ne sont pas concernées.

- Migrations : SQLite `0047_groovy_shadowcat` et Postgres `0011_magical_kate_bishop` (numéros à revérifier avant fusion, #1199 et #1198 en utilisent aussi).
- Test : `server/__tests__/integration_requests_index.test.ts` applique les migrations SQLite et vérifie qu'un second doublon vivant est refusé, qu'un détenteur annulé et les lignes sans jeu sont acceptés.
- Aucun changement de comportement attendu : le code évite déjà ce cas, l'index ne fait que le rendre impossible.

pr.body:
Bumps [express](https://github.com/expressjs/express) and [@types/express](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/tree/HEAD/types/express). These dependencies needed to be updated together. Updates `express` from 4.22.3 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

... (truncated)

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.2 to 4.38.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026

No user facing changes.

4.37.7 - 13 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.3. #4085

4.37.6 - 04 Aug 2026

  • Changed the default filepath for the new remote file address format that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 / 3.37.0 to .github/codeql-config.yml to align it with the suggested path that is used elsewhere. #4070

Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.64.0

🧰 WebMCP

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });
const page = await browser.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com');

for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools())
console.log(tool.name, tool.description);


const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 });
console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42"

Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool>. Pass --no-webmcp to opt out.

playwright-cli exposes them as well:

playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'

🎬 Better videos

Videos can now be recorded at a custom frame rate, and the decorations for actions are styled with plain CSS:

pr.body:
## Description

Auto-search asks every indexer for 10 results (`AUTO_SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE`), newest first, and only fetches a second page when the global release-name blacklist hides the whole first page. For a game with many update releases, the first page can be nothing but updates, so the base release never reaches the auto-download step and the game is marked as having no results.

Real example, Jackett and NZBHydra both return ~10 `<Game> Update vX.Y.Z <Platform>-<ReleaseGroup>` releases before `<Game> <Platform>-<ReleaseGroup>`. The first Usenet page also has a PC release (`<Game>.v1.0.0L-ReleaseGroup>`), which counts as a main release but is dropped later by the platform filter. Auto-search logged `gamesWithResults: 0` even though a manual search shows the release.

**Change** (`server/cron.ts`, backend only):

- For **wanted** games, `searchAndCategorizeItemsForGame` keeps fetching pages (still capped at `AUTO_SEARCH_MAX_PAGES`) until there is a main release for the game's effective platform. That is the same `resolveGamePlatformPreference` + `applyPreferredPlatformFilter` check the auto-download step applies afterwards, so a main release for another platform doesn't stop the search.
- Eligible releases from every fetched page are kept. Before, only the last page's were kept, which was fine when earlier pages were fully blacklisted.
- The per-game release blacklist is loaded before the loop, so a blacklisted main release doesn't count as "found".
- **Owned**-game update searches don't pass a platform and behave as before.
- Existing paging for a fully blacklisted page is unchanged.

Out of scope: auto-download still only triggers when exactly one main candidate remains, so the same release on a Usenet and a torrent indexer still produces "Multiple Results Found" rather than a grab.

## Screenshots

Not applicable (backend-only change).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Description

Automatic imports without a platform token in the release title were skipped when games stored normal IGDB platform names, even if that platform was selected. Resolve stored names through the shared platform catalog and accept any selected platform in the game's list, while preserving legacy ID formats.

Resolve detected release platforms and destination folders through the same catalog so release-title precedence and library placement also hold for PS4, PS5, Xbox, Linux, and Mac. Preserve existing legacy folder names. Add the supported Game Gear platform (ID 35) to the shared catalog. For untagged multi-platform games, use the same selected platform for both eligibility and destination folders, including naming previews and manual-import plans.

Adds 44 regression cases, including `platforms: ["PC (Microsoft Windows)"]` with selected ID `6` and a release title without a platform suffix, plus acceptance and rejection checks for the additional release platforms.

Fixes #1210.
