_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcKDxjoskUNaQoUyGbMSvpUD)_

Before: clicking a game opened a small modal with 8 tabs. It was cramped, could not be opened in a new tab, and Discover/Library/Roulette each embedded their own copy.

After: every game has its own page at `/games/:id` (and `/games/igdb-<id>` for Discover results). Cards are real links, so middle-click, ctrl/cmd-click and "open in new tab" work. The tab title is the game's name. The details are laid out as sections on one page, with a sticky jump bar, instead of tabs.

**Layout**
- Hero: cover, title, year and developers, status/score/source badges, and the Download / Hide / Remove actions (full-width row on phones).
- Main column: Overview (summary, crack status), Downloads, Journal, Media, DLC, Mods, Files on disk.
- Side column (after Downloads on phones): Facts, Your game (rating, download target, installed version), Scores and Time to Beat, Links.
- Files on disk only scans the library folder once the section nears the viewport.

**How**
- `GameDetailsModal` becomes `GameDetails` (same queries and mutations, no Dialog/Tabs), rendered by the lazy route `pages/game-details.tsx`. It loads a library game from the new `GET /api/games/:id` (owner-checked, UUID-validated) or a Discover game from `/api/igdb/game/:id`. Cards pass the game along in navigation state so the page paints instantly; a direct visit fetches it.
- `useGameDetailsLink` gives cards the path, a ctrl/cmd/shift-click and middle-click that open a new tab; titles are wouter `<Link>`s.
- `BacklogRoulette` "View game" navigates to the page. Back returns to where you came from, or to the library when the page was opened in a fresh tab.
- Tests updated (unit, server route, e2e for details, playing journal, roulette, discover, DLC). `npm run lint`, `tsc`, the full Vitest run and the touched Playwright specs pass. The Impeccable detector reports no findings on the new files.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcQ98TQYEEPXVFkc2gjAwcxu?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcQ98TQYEEPXVFkc2gjAwcxu)_

Closes Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#15 and Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#4

Before: Questarr had no RomM support. Imports went to readable platform folders ("SNES", "PS2", "PC"), which RomM does not recognise, and nothing in the app explained how to feed RomM or any other frontend.

After: Settings → Import has a RomM card.
- **RomM platform folders** (works without the API): imports go to `<library root>/<RomM slug>/<game>` (`snes`, `ps2`, `win`…). Point the library root at RomM's `roms` folder. A platform without a known slug keeps its readable folder.
- **API connection** (URL + token): Questarr asks RomM to rescan after each import, and can mark wishlist games already in RomM as owned.
- The Import help gets a "Feeding RomM (or ES-DE, Playnite)" setup, and the Library Root field shows the resulting path (`<root>/PC/Game Name`).

No migration: everything is stored in `system_config` (`romm.*`), all of it off by default, so existing deployments are unchanged. The token is encrypted like other credentials.

## How

- `shared/romm-platforms.ts`: IGDB platform id → RomM slug table and slug validation (lowercase, no `/`, no `..`). `ImportManager.resolvePlatformFolder` uses it when the option is on (release platform, then the game's chosen target platform, then its listed platforms); the existing containment checks still apply.
- `server/romm.ts`: settings, a small client (platforms, paged ROM list, `POST /api/tasks/scan` with a fallback to `/api/tasks/run/scan_library` for older RomM) over the SSRF-safe fetch, with redirects refused so the bearer token never follows one. The rescan runs detached after an import, so a RomM outage never fails or delays it.
- `server/romm-sync.ts`: pull sync, by IGDB id, then by normalized title only for ROMs without an IGDB id (ambiguous titles and a different target platform are ignored). Only `wanted` games become `owned`; playing, shelved, completed and already-owned games are never touched. Games RomM has and Questarr does not are only counted. Runs every 6 h when enabled, or on demand ("Sync now").
- Routes `GET/POST /api/settings/romm`, `POST /test` (the saved token is only sent to the saved URL), `POST /sync` (strict schema, token masked, test and sync rate-limited).
- Tests: platform table and folder routing, client, paging, sync matching and no-downgrade, routes, and the settings UI. Exercised against a fake RomM server for the screenshots.
- Not in this PR: creating missing games from RomM, a custom slug→folder binding map, the optional LLM ROM-name cleanup.

## Credits

Rewritten from `origin/romm-integration-clean` (`41fa5a02`, Doezer), as extended and tested in [snapetech/QuestarrNG](https://github.com/snapetech/QuestarrNG) (`3bb07f02`, `9f9ff39b`), and from the RomM API sync of Jeremy Stover's retro fork ([Kadajett/Questarr](https://github.com/Kadajett/Questarr), `romm.ts`, `romm-sync.ts`, both GPL-3.0). The code is new rather than copied.

The naming-template PR (#1197) is merged; this branch has been brought up to date with main.

## Description

Implements Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#3 (Custom collections, milestone 1.5.1).

Before: games could only be grouped by status, and there was no way to keep a personal list such as "Co-op night" or "every highly rated shooter".

After: a new **Collections** page (sidebar, under Library) lets the user create two kinds of collections:

- **Manual**: the user picks games from their library ("Manage games" dialog).
- **Smart**: filter rules kept up to date automatically. Rules (all set rules must match, list values match on any one): status, genre, platform, minimum IGDB rating, minimum personal rating, release year range, title contains. The create/edit dialog shows how many games match right now.

Scope kept deliberately small: single-user (single tenant), collections are not exposed in the Integration API, and games cannot yet be added to a collection from the game card or the library toolbar (only from the collection's own page). Smart collections store only their rules; membership is computed on read, so it never goes stale. The user's content filters (adult / age-restricted) and hidden games are applied to collection contents.

How: two new tables, `collections` (id, user, name, description, type, JSON rules) and `collection_games` (unique per collection/game, cascade on delete), mirrored in `shared/schema.pg.ts` with parity guards, `TABLE_ORDER` and migrations for both dialects (`migrations/0045`, `migrations-pg/0009`). Rule evaluation is a pure function in `shared/collection-rules.ts`, used by the server for membership and by the dialog for the live match count. <!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcJwgNh3MJkuPWfKpedp5va5)_

## Description

Before: every integration API key could call every `/api/integration` route forever, Questarr could not act as a provider for a request app, and nothing explained how to show imported games in Gameyfin.

After: keys have a scope and an optional expiry, SeerrNG can use Questarr as its PC game provider, and a short guide covers Gameyfin. One branch, one commit per issue, so it can be reviewed commit by commit (the second depends on the first):

1. **Scoped and expiring API keys** (Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#14). `api_keys.scope` and `expires_at`. Scopes are named after what they allow: `all`, `read` (read the library), `library:write` (sync the library and request games, what the Playnite extension needs) and `requests` (request provider for an external app such as SeerrNG). Routes declare scopes with `requireScope()`; expired key gives 401 `API_KEY_EXPIRED`, wrong scope 403 `API_KEY_SCOPE_DENIED`; `last_used_at` written at most once a minute; 300 req/min per key on `/api/integration`; API keys card shows scope, expiry and last use. Existing keys become `all` with no expiry. Rewritten from the idea in snapetech/QuestarrNG `dc4394ac8` (no code or migration files copied).
2. **SeerrNG provider API** (Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#22). The QuestarrNG v2 contract (`apiVersion` 1, `requestContractVersion` 2) under `/api/integration/seerrng/v1`: handshake, catalog, library lookup, idempotent requests, status, retry, cancel, file streaming with byte ranges and `.tar.gz` bundles. New table `integration_requests` (SQLite 0046, Postgres 0010, `TABLE_ORDER`, parity guards). Status is derived from the game, its downloads and its files, so no extra columns on `games` or `game_downloads`. Questarr stays single tenant. Differences from QuestarrNG are listed in `docs/SEERRNG.md`: PC only, OS maps to the game's target platform (architecture recorded but not filtered), paged catalog limited to the first 100 results (IGDB's per-request limit), no restart-recovery handshake.
3. **Gameyfin** (Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#25), docs only (`docs/GAMEYFIN.md`). Gameyfin has no API tokens and its scan trigger is an admin-session endpoint, so the integration is a shared folder plus Gameyfin's file system watcher. Scan trigger, requests bridge and ownership sync are not implemented, with the reasons in the page.

Decisions taken (easy to change): UI default access is library sync (Playnite) and default expiry 1 year, the API default is no expiry so existing clients behave as before; `read` included now; legacy keys are never forced to expire; the SeerrNG request waits for the normal auto-search cycle instead of forcing a search.

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcQ98TQYEEPXVFkc2gjAwcxu)_

Closes Doezer/Questarr-mgmt#16

Before: the naming pattern (`renamePattern`, default `{Title} ({Region})`) was validated, stored and editable in Settings → Import, but no server code rendered it. Imported games were always named after the game title, and the help text advertised a `{Region}` token that never had a data source.

After: the pattern names the library leaf (the game folder, or the file of a single-file release) inside the platform folder. The settings page has token chips, presets, inline validation errors and a live preview, instant on a sample game and then confirmed by the server on the user's own library games.

The default pattern renders exactly like before (`{Region}` is empty and empty brackets are dropped), so no migration is needed and existing users see no path change.

## How

- `shared/naming.ts` is a pure engine used by both server and client. Tokens: `{Title} {TitleThe} {Year} {Platform} {Version} {Group} {Source} {IgdbId} {SteamAppId} {Region}` (Region stays empty for now). Empty tokens drop their brackets and orphan separators. Illegal characters become `_` like `sanitizeFsName` did, Windows reserved names get a `_` prefix, the name is capped at 200 UTF-8 bytes on grapheme boundaries.
- `PCImportStrategy.planImport` and `planConfirmImport` share `resolveLibraryLeafName`, which replaces the duplicated `sanitizeFsName(game.title)` logic. `{Version}`, `{Group}` and `{Source}` come from the release name, which an indexer controls, so they get the same sanitizing as the title; the existing containment checks stay in place.
- `PATCH /api/imports/config` rejects unknown tokens, slashes, `..`, control characters and unbalanced braces with a 400. New `POST /api/imports/naming/preview` renders a pattern on up to 5 library games plus one synthetic release.
- Tests: engine (tokens, empty brackets, back-compat invariant against `sanitizeFsName`, hostile release data, reserved names, byte cap, validation), strategy destinations (folder, single file, unpacked archive, hostile release name), `planConfirmImport`, routes (PATCH rejection, preview), and the settings UI.
- Not in this PR: renaming already imported folders (an "Organize" action with dry run), a separate file pattern, a `{Region}` parser.

Design inspired by [Mikurunazume/Gamearr](https://github.com/Mikurunazume/Gamearr) (`7ecec2b`, `128d847`, `0549760`, GPL-3.0); the engine was rewritten for Questarr rather than copied, with credit to its author.

pr.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcGGUbeqaDCYB9SXMroXDEkV)_

Parts 2 to 5 of release scoring (Questarr-mgmt #12, #17 and #2). The engine from #1166 is merged, and this PR is based on `main` (39 files).

Before: the scoring engine exists (#1166) but nothing stores a profile, the search ignores it, and the only way to prefer a release group is a separate setting. Auto-search takes the title match from `releaseMatchesGame`, which accepts a sequel for the base game. xREL has no influence on search results.

After:
- Each user has a release profile and custom formats, editable in Settings > Discovery & Downloads > Release Scoring, which replaces the Preferred Release Groups card.
- The manual search shows a score on every result, with a breakdown of the rules and rejections. Results sort by score by default, and rejected releases stay visible but dimmed (and last under any sort).
- Auto-search uses the same scoring: it only takes accepted releases whose title is an exact or contained match, ranked by score first, then by the user's sort order. Ambiguous names stay in the manual search. The "one candidate means auto-download" rule is unchanged.
- xREL verifies releases: a release whose name matches an xREL entry gets +125 ("Verified on xREL"), a nuked one is rejected with xREL's reason, and one xREL does not list gets a neutral "Not on xREL" badge (no penalty, since P2P and usenet releases are often missing).

**What it does**
- Tables `release_profiles` (one per user) and `custom_formats`, on SQLite and Postgres (`bigint` for the max size), with migrations, parity guards and `TABLE_ORDER` updated.
- First use creates the profile from the old settings: the preferred groups become a +50 "Preferred release group" format; strict mode adds a hard-reject "Not a preferred release group" format. `minScore` starts at 0. The seeder floor stays in the download rules. The old columns are left untouched.
- API: `GET /api/release-scoring`, `PUT /api/release-profile`, `POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/custom-formats`, with regexes checked by the engine's validator.
- xREL: `server/xrel-predb.ts` looks up the game on xREL (only the scene and P2P types the user enabled, 100 results), cached 10 minutes per title and type with the promise shared between parallel searches. It only runs when the user has an xREL feature on. The manual search waits at most 3 seconds for it; a slower lookup finishes in the background for the next search. If the lookup fails, scoring runs without it. The engine got two built-in rules (`xrel_predb_match` +125, `xrel_nuked` rejects) that a profile can reweight or disable. The release name is matched to the xREL dirname ignoring case and the separators (dots, spaces, underscores).
- Download Rules gets a "Release Score" option for Default Sort Order, which the manual download dialog applies when it opens.
- If scoring cannot load, auto-search falls back to the previous filters for that cycle, and the manual search returns unscored results.

**Behavior changes to know about**
- Non-strict preferred groups now add points instead of filtering down to those groups. Auto-search still narrows to the preferred group when one of the results matches it and its score is above zero.
- The download dialog no longer preselects a group filter from the old setting.
- The manual search badge ("results available") now counts accepted releases with a clear title match, like auto-search.
- The manual search can call xREL (the game title is sent to the configured xREL API) when the user has scene or P2P xREL releases enabled, which is on by default.

How: `server/release-scoring-service.ts` (migration and loading), `server/release-scoring-routes.ts`, `server/xrel-predb.ts`, storage methods on both implementations, `scoreReleasesForGame` in `server/cron.ts`, `ReleaseScoreBadge`, `ReleaseScoringSettings` and `CustomFormatDialog` on the client. Tests: SQLite and PGlite parity suite, route tests, engine, cron, search and xREL tests, client tests; tsc and eslint clean.

Credit: the xREL boost follows the Jessomadic/Questarr fork (commits `f90f6ff7` and `7a61aaff`), as does the scoring design adopted in #1166.

Not in this PR: sending xREL release names as extra indexer queries (the fork does it, up to 12 per search). It multiplies indexer requests, so it is better as its own change if wanted.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcCkBEVyqeZDaM9a35qLx9Yd)_

Before: background jobs were bare `setInterval`s with no visibility. The Activity menu only had Logs and Import History, there was no global view of what happened to downloads, and archives a download client left unextracted went unnoticed.

After: System Tasks, History and Blocklist pages under Activity (with search and an "Unblock all" button), and a notification when an imported game still holds unextracted archives.

Everything for the three 1.5.1 items of Questarr-mgmt (#20, #19, #18) is on this one branch.

## 1. System Tasks (#20)

- `server/task-registry.ts`: one `setTimeout` per job, next run = end of the last run + interval, no self-overlap, last run persisted in `system_config` (`task_state:<name>`, so no table). A cron job that fails at the top level now rejects, so the page shows it as failed.
- `cron.ts` registers the 8 jobs (game updates, download status, auto search, xREL, Steam wishlist, client versions, RSS, history cleanup) with unchanged intervals and startup delay.
- `GET /api/system/tasks`, `POST /api/system/tasks/:name/run` (202, 409 if already running, 404 unknown); `task:started` / `task:finished` over Socket.IO.
- Page `/system/tasks` with a search field: table on tablet/desktop, cards with 44px buttons on phones.
- The Backup job is not included: it belongs to Questarr-mgmt #5 and needs a SQLite and Postgres strategy.

![tasks desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/1bc984a52ac92f325561b7e31b0530e0450ae054/.github/pr-assets/system-tasks/tasks-desktop.png) ![tasks mobile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/1bc984a52ac92f325561b7e31b0530e0450ae054/.github/pr-assets/system-tasks/tasks-mobile.png) ![tasks search](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/b5cce4b6dd50ab592184263f4cd494d929f361a0/.github/pr-assets/search-unblock/tasks-search.png)

## 2. Activity: History and Blocklist (#19)

- New `download_events` table on both dialects (`migrations/0045`, `migrations-pg/0009`, parity guards, `TABLE_ORDER`). Written from `DatabaseStorage` so every call site is covered: grabbed, completed, imported, failed, needs review, removed, blocklisted. A status that does not change logs nothing. Failure to log never breaks the download. Events older than 90 days go in the cleanup task.
- `GET /api/activity/history` (filter by event, search by release or game, paged).
- `/activity/history` and `/activity/blocklist` pages. The blocklist page reuses `/api/blacklist`, adds a filter, an Unblock button per row and an "Unblock all" button behind a confirmation (`DELETE /api/activity/blocklist`). The name patterns of #1112 stay in Settings and are linked.
- Not done: a separate Queue page (the Downloads page already is the queue), a link from a blocklist row to the game (waiting for the game detail page route), and merging with Import History.

![history desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/2187809d7c16fa9fcf6b79a2f0c3333c1985a8fb/.github/pr-assets/activity/history-desktop.png) ![history mobile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/2187809d7c16fa9fcf6b79a2f0c3333c1985a8fb/.github/pr-assets/activity/history-mobile.png) ![blocklist desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/2187809d7c16fa9fcf6b79a2f0c3333c1985a8fb/.github/pr-assets/activity/blocklist-desktop.png) ![blocklist mobile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/2187809d7c16fa9fcf6b79a2f0c3333c1985a8fb/.github/pr-assets/activity/blocklist-mobile.png)

Search and unblock all: ![history search](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/b5cce4b6dd50ab592184263f4cd494d929f361a0/.github/pr-assets/search-unblock/history-search.png) ![unblock all](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/b5cce4b6dd50ab592184263f4cd494d929f361a0/.github/pr-assets/search-unblock/blocklist-unblock-all.png)

## 3. Archives left unextracted (#18)

Scope follows `reports/mgmt-backlog/research/18-sab-leftover-archives.md`: detect and report, no second extraction engine.

- `ArchiveService.findArchiveSets`: read-only, bounded (depth 3, 5000 entries, also inside one huge folder), `lstat` only so symlinks are never followed, one result per multi-volume set.
- After a successful import (automatic or confirmed from manual review), if the library folder still holds an archive set that is not already extracted (auto-unpack off, archive in a sub-folder, second set), a warning notification names them.
- NZBGet history with `UnpackStatus: NONE` no longer reports a completed unpack.
- Not done: nested archive layers, the Downloads "to process" strip, and the post-processing-off case (an existing test requires that no client lookup happens there). SABnzbd's `unpackStatus` is left as is.

Ideas credited to Jessomadic's fork (`bd4002f6`, `5395c91e`, `8bfa2910`); all rewritten.

## Checks

`tsc`, ESLint, the full Vitest run (3764 tests, SQLite and PGlite parity), `db:generate:pg` produces nothing further.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc4ZBH2n9imy9q6XGWAd5Emx)_

Before: `AuthProvider` migrated the legacy `localStorage` token (and reset the in-memory bearer token) during render, guarded by a ref. That is a side effect in render, fragile under StrictMode and concurrent rendering.

After: render only reads the legacy token. The migration runs in a post-commit effect, is idempotent (it re-applies the captured token, so a StrictMode re-run cannot reset it to null), and removes the token from `localStorage`. Children are not rendered and `/api/auth/me` is not enabled until migration completes, so the request-order guarantee is kept. `isLoading` stays true and the redirect logic waits until then. Cookie-only sessions and the in-memory bearer fallback are unchanged.

How: `client/src/lib/auth.tsx` (`readLegacyLocalStorageToken`, `migrated` state, `enabled: migrated`). Tests in `client/src/__tests__/auth-provider.test.tsx` cover StrictMode, "token removed only after commit" (fails against the old implementation) and a cookie-only session. Client suite, type check and lint pass.

Visual evidence: `npm run dev:test` + headless Chromium with a legacy `token` pre-seeded in `localStorage`. Exactly one `/api/auth/me` request was sent, carrying the bearer header; `localStorage.token` was `null` afterwards; the user landed on the Library page logged in as `admin`, with no redirect to `/login`.

![Library after legacy token migration](``https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/7b96aede28522dd1bae5c3fe533c6b05021921a2/.github/pr-assets/legacy-token-migration/legacy-migrated.png``)

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc1b5xt7zLYiw6Fk1H1Wfxdh)_

## Description

Before: releases only happen when a maintainer pushes a `vX.Y.Z` tag, and the Docker image is built by hand from `deploy.yml`.

After: a new `weekly-release.yml` runs every Monday 06:00 UTC (and via `workflow_dispatch`). If `main` has commits since the last tag it:

1. tags `main` as `v<next patch of latest stable>-dev.<YYYYMMDD>` (e.g. `v1.5.1-dev.20261019`);
2. creates a GitHub **pre-release** whose notes (`scripts/weekly-release-notes.mjs`) list the merged PRs (security/dependency fixes first) and commits pushed straight to `main`;
3. dispatches the existing `deploy.yml` (environment `dev`, multi-arch) with that tag, so the image is `ghcr.io/doezer/questarr` and `doezer/questarr` tagged with the release tag and `dev`. `latest` is never touched (only production deployments move it). The Windows installer is opt-in through a dispatch input and is attached to the pre-release by the existing step.

`release.yml` now ignores `-dev.` tags so only stable tags create a draft release from the changelog. Nothing is released when `main` has not moved since the previous tag.

How: PRs are read from first-parent merge commits (`Merge pull request #N` / `(#N)`), then titles and labels come from `gh pr view`; if `gh` is unavailable the script falls back to the commit message. I ran the notes script locally on `v1.5.0-rc1..v1.5.0`, and checked the version computation (`v1.5.1-dev.<date>` from `v1.5.0`). The workflow itself can only be validated on GitHub: trigger it once with `workflow_dispatch` after merging.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Documentation update (`docs/OPERATIONS.md`)

## Checklist:

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

Updates `@radix-ui/react-navigation-menu` from 1.2.22 to 1.3.0
Changelog

Sourced from @​radix-ui/react-navigation-menu's changelog.

1.3.0

  • Added a disableToggle prop to NavigationMenu.Sub.
    • true: Clicking the trigger of an already-open submenu item keeps it open. This is the default and matches existing behavior.
    • false: Clicking the trigger of a submenu item toggles it open or closed.
  • Added an activationMode prop to NavigationMenu.Root and NavigationMenu.Sub.
    • "automatic": Hovering or focusing a trigger opens its item, and moving away from the trigger closes it after a short delay. This is the default and matches existing behavior.
    • "manual": Pointer entry and focus never open an item. The item opens when its trigger is clicked.
    • When activationMode is omitted on NavigationMenu.Sub, it inherits the value from the parent NavigationMenu.Root, so setting "manual" on the root also applies to submenus unless a submenu opts back in to "automatic".
  • Fixed a bug where a submenu's defaultValue was reset when an external element was focused before the menu opened.
  • Fixed a bug where NavigationMenu.Viewport discarded its children and rendered the active content in their place. The active content is now rendered inside the consumer's element alongside any children it already had.
  • Updated dependencies: @radix-ui/react-slot@1.4.0, @radix-ui/react-dismissable-layer@1.1.20, @radix-ui/react-visually-hidden@1.2.12, @radix-ui/react-direction@1.1.5, @radix-ui/react-primitive@2.1.11, @radix-ui/react-presence@1.1.11, @radix-ui/react-collection@1.1.16

Updates `@vitejs/plugin-react` from 6.1.1 to 6.1.2
Release notes

Sourced from @​vitejs/plugin-react's releases.

plugin-react@6.1.2

Fix HMR for compound components (#1484)

Adding or removing a component from a compound component was not handled, creating stale updates. Doing this now triggers hmr invalidate on the file and propagates the invalidation to importers.

Fix compiler.logDiagnostics option not working (#1483)

With oxc-transform-react >= 0.148, the logDiagnostics was not working. This version fixes it and requires oxc-transform-react >= 0.152 as a peer dependency if you are using the compiler option. compiler.logDiagnostics option is now deprecated and should be swapped for the builtin compiler.reportDiagnostics.

Disable refresh for non-jsx with compiler enabled (fix #1478) (#1485)

When the compiler was enabled, TS files could trigger fast refresh which would cause runtime errors. The logic now follows what the builtin oxc plugin in Vite does.

Changelog

Sourced from @​vitejs/plugin-react's changelog.

6.1.2 (2026-10-05)

Fix HMR for compound components (#1484)

Adding or removing a component from a compound component was not handled, creating stale updates. Doing this now triggers hmr invalidate on the file and propagates the invalidation to importers.

Fix compiler.logDiagnostics option not working (#1483)

With oxc-transform-react >= 0.148, the logDiagnostics was not working. This version fixes it and requires oxc-transform-react >= 0.152 as a peer dependency if you are using the compiler option. compiler.logDiagnostics option is now deprecated and should be swapped for the builtin compiler.reportDiagnostics.

Disable refresh for non-jsx with compiler enabled (fix #1478) (#1485)

When the compiler was enabled, TS files could trigger fast refresh which would cause runtime errors. The logic now follows what the builtin oxc plugin in Vite does.

Updates `jsdom` from 30.1.1 to 30.1.2
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v30.1.2

  • Updated URLs to support Unicode v18.0.0 in internationalized domain names.
  • Reduced package size and memory use for CSS property definitions. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed severe slowdowns when building large DOM trees, including SVG charts with D3, which regressed in v30.1.0. (@​cmdcolin)
  • Fixed exponentially slow reads of empty inherited CSS custom properties in deeply nested documents, and custom properties incorrectly inheriting past an initial reset. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() returning stale results after editing stylesheet declarations, selectors, or media queries, including in imported stylesheets.
  • Fixed selector matching and computed styles after changes to form control checkedness, indeterminacy, selection, values, and validity, including during form resets and canceled clicks.
  • Fixed computed styles for :focus, :focus-visible, :focus-within, and selectors containing them after focus changes, including inside focus and blur listeners. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed element.focus() incorrectly focusing elements hidden by 'display', including through shadow hosts and slots, and elements excluded by shadow DOM slot assignment. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() throwing for elements without inline-style support, including XML and MathML elements.
  • Fixed a memory leak where stylesheet parsing retained the last parsed stylesheet's window after window.close().
  • Fixed memory growth from long-lived MutationObserver instances retaining bookkeeping for garbage-collected nodes. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed retained select.selectedOptions collections becoming stale after selection changes and form resets.
  • Fixed rejection of negative CSS sizing values, including for 'min-width', 'min-height', 'max-width', and 'max-height', which regressed in v30.1.0.
  • Fixed handling of deeply nested color-mix() expressions, including exceptions during color resolution. (@​asamuzaK)

  • 1efa190 Reduce generated CSS property data

## Description

Before: GitHub reported 16 open vulnerabilities on `main` (1 critical, 6 high, 9 moderate). None of them ship in the production image: 14 come from PyJWT 2.13.0 in the CI Semgrep install, and the other two from the dev-only `fast-copy` and `postcss-selector-parser`.

After: none of these advisories remain. `npm audit` reports only node-forge, which is already declared not affected in the VEX feed, and OSV reports nothing for the Semgrep lock.

How:
- **pyjwt 2.13.0 → 2.15.1**: Semgrep 1.178.0 pins `pyjwt<2.14`, so Semgrep moves to 1.180.0 (which requires `pyjwt>=2.15.0`). `.github/requirements/semgrep.txt` is regenerated with the documented `uv pip compile` command. A hash-checked install was verified locally, and `semgrep --version` reports 1.180.0.
- **fast-copy 4.0.3 → 4.1.0**: new `overrides` pin, because `pino-pretty` allows `^4.0.0`.
- **postcss-selector-parser 7.1.5 → 7.1.6**: new `overrides` pin for `@npmcli/query` (`^7.0.0`). The 6.x line has no fix, and its only consumer, `@tailwindcss/typography`, was never used (no `@plugin` or import anywhere), so it is removed instead of being forced across a major version.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcSiSGrxTApokvLhTyoQPf4c)_

## Description

Fixes M1 to M4 from the 1.5.0 release review, all in the download status cron (`server/cron.ts`).

**Before:** a 3-minute outage of qBittorrent, Deluge, Synology or NZBGet marked every tracked download failed and reset games to Wanted (those clients returned `[]` on error). A transient torrent error (rTorrent tracker message, Transmission `errorString`, qBittorrent `missingFiles`) failed the download for good, so it was never imported once it finished. A client that purges finished jobs turned each successful download into "Download Failed" and auto-search grabbed the same release again, in a loop. A restart during an import left the row in `unpacking` / `completed_pending_import` forever. Two status checks could run at the same time while an import was extracting.

**After:**
- **M1** – `getAllDownloads` and `getDownloadStatus` accept `throwOnError` on every client (SABnzbd already did for status). The cron passes it, so an unreachable client skips the tick instead of counting misses. Synology API rejections (`success: false`, e.g. unknown task) still count as "not found". Deluge's empty object for an unknown hash is now `null`.
- **M2** – a torrent error is shown on the row but the download keeps being tracked for 30 minutes; it is only failed if the error lasts that long. Usenet failures stay immediate.
- **M3** – a download that vanishes after being seen at ≥ 90 % or in a completed/seeding/post-processing state goes to manual review (Pending Imports, with a warning notification), or to completed/owned when post-processing is off. The game is not reset to Wanted. Auto-search also skips a release that already failed for that game, which breaks any remaining loop.
- **M4** – `ImportManager` tracks running imports in memory (`isImportInFlight`; a second start of the same import is ignored). A row in a mid-import status with no running import goes to manual review with an "interrupted" message and a notification.
- **Concurrency** – `checkDownloadStatus` skips a tick while the previous run is still going. Imports now run in the background so a long extraction no longer holds up tracking of other downloads; the "Download Completed" notification is sent when the import starts.

No schema change.

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcBLy4X1wP2N9HtBoDxhz1YX)_

## Description

Fixes M8 and M9 from the 1.5.0 release review.

**M8, qBittorrent before 4.4.** Before: those versions ignore the `tag` filter on `/api/v2/torrents/info` and return every torrent, so Questarr took the first entry as the download it had just added. A grab could be bound to someone else's torrent, leading to a wrong import or moving/deleting the wrong files.

After: the tagged torrent is chosen from each torrent's own comma-separated `tags` field (exact tag, not prefix), both in the add flow and in `findTorrentByTag` (async resolution by cron). When the response lists a torrent without our tag, the filter was ignored; if none carries the tag (clients older than 4.3.3 also ignore `tags` on add, and pre-4.2 clients report no tags at all), the add flow falls back to the existing title/recency matching. `findTorrentByTag` returns `null` rather than guessing.

**M9, Prowlarr behind a TLS-terminating proxy.** Before: with Prowlarr configured as `https://prowlarr.example.com/5/api`, Prowlarr reflects `http://prowlarr.example.com/5/download?link=…` (sometimes with `:9696`). `isSameProwlarrHost` required an exact origin match, so the link was treated as external and wrapped a second time, and every grab failed with "Failed to normalize provided link" (#812).

After: a link on the configured hostname counts as Prowlarr's own whatever its scheme and port. The exact `/{id}/download` path for this indexer and the `link` parameter are still required, and proxy-shaped links on any other public host are still wrapped.

How: a small `findTaggedTorrent()` helper in `server/downloaders/qbittorrent.ts`, and a hostname comparison in `TorznabClient.isSameProwlarrHost` (`server/torznab.ts`).

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcTgRx8UMgfq6dnWdnCSPCpG)_ ## Description Fixes M10 (the part #1174 does not cover) and M11 from the 1.5.0 release review. Before: in the details modal of a Discover game, Hide, Remove and the star rating sent the temporary `igdb-` to the game endpoints and failed with a 400 ("Failed to update game visibility", "Failed to save your rating"). Separately, Discover kept the library list under its own query key `["/api/games?includeHidden=true"]`, which no mutation invalidates: a game hidden from a card stayed on screen, and changing the status of a game you had just tracked re-POSTed it and got a 409 ("Failed to add game to collection"). After: Hide adds the game to the library as hidden (or hides its existing library copy) and closes the modal, and the card disappears from the carousels. Remove only shows when the game is already in the library, and removes that copy without touching files or download clients (those options need the library context the Discover card doesn't have). Rating a game that isn't tracked adds it as wanted first, the same as #1174 does for Download, then saves the rating; a tracked game shows and updates its library rating. Discover now reads the library under `["/api/games", "", true]`, the key Library (with hidden games) and Stats already use, so every game mutation refreshes it, and a status change that hits a 409 updates the existing row. How: `GameDetailsModal` looks up the library row by `igdbId` when it shows a Discover game (shared cache, so no extra request on Discover) and points Hide, Remove and rating at it. A new `addDiscoveryGameToLibrary()` in `discover-hidden-mutation.ts` does the POST-or-reuse-on-409, used by the rating and by Discover's status change. Notes: - Stats needed no change: its key `["/api/games", "", true]` already sits under `["/api/games"]`, so invalidation reached it. _Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc6bhKsuRReeb35ipfap6nVA)_

## Description

Before: `ArchiveService.extract()` emptied its output directory before unpacking. Since 1.5.0 that directory is the game's folder in the library (extraction happens in place at the destination), so confirming an import of an update into an already installed game (`/data/PC/Foo`) deleted the game and left only the patch. Picking the platform folder (`/data/PC`) as the destination wiped every game in it. Release-blocker C2 of the 1.5.0 review.

After: the archive is unpacked into a staging directory inside the destination (`.questarr-extract-<archive name>-<random>`, unique per run), then merged into it: new files are added, same-named files are replaced, nothing else is deleted. Every conflict is checked before the first file moves (file/directory clash, an existing symlink where the archive has a directory, an entry using the reserved staging name), and a failed extraction never touches the existing files. If a move fails part-way, replaced files are restored from a backup and added files are removed.

How: `extractWith7zip`/`extractWithUnrar` now target the staging directory; the old `listExtractedFiles` walk became `mergeExtracted`, which plans the whole merge, then moves each file to its final path (same-filesystem rename) and returns those paths. The in-place cleanup that kept archive volumes alive is no longer needed, since nothing in the destination is deleted anymore. I did not add a "destination not empty" refusal in `confirmImport`: with the merge, importing an update over an install is now the expected, safe case. Move mode without extraction still replaces same-named files as it did in 1.4.2. A staging directory left by a run killed mid-extraction (container restart) stays behind as a hidden folder; it is never reported as extracted.

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcXfZGwrPuMgPJf3TAojtrTu)_

## Description

Fixes M5 to M7 from the 1.5.0 release review.

Before: with ClamAV enabled, any download with more than 100 files was treated as infected, moved to quarantine (breaking seeding) and could never be imported. Downloads ClamAV could not fully scan were let through: these included an unreachable or failing clamd and files over clamd's size limit. A size-limit refusal even stopped the scan of the remaining files. Auto-unpack extracted `.iso` files, turning PS2/PSP images into unusable loose files and deleting the ISO in move mode (GameCube/Wii failed as "corrupt archive"). Sort Extras categorized every file on its full relative path, so `Foo.GOTY.Edition/` went entirely to `dlc/` and `Data/Patch/x.pak` went to `update/`, breaking the game.

After: ClamAV scans up to 10,000 files within a 30-minute budget. A detection still quarantines. Any download ClamAV can't fully scan is held in Pending Manual Imports with the reason, its files left in place, and importing it takes an explicit second confirmation. That covers going over the file cap or the time budget, an unreadable folder, clamd being unreachable or down, and a file clamd refuses. After a refusal the remaining files are still scanned, so a detection in one of them still blocks. The ClamAV settings say which clamd.conf limits to raise. `.iso` files are never auto-unpacked, and an explicit Unpack still extracts them. Sort Extras judges each top-level item by its own name, looking at most one level inside a single wrapper folder. It moves whole items, so a game's internal folders are never touched.

How: `ScanResult` gets an `incomplete` flag (blocked stays false), handled in `processImport`/`confirmImport`. The confirm route returns a 409 with the reason. A clamd reply received before a connection reset is used as the verdict. `isArchive` takes `{ includeDiscImages }`. A new `categorizeRelativeFiles()` in `ImportStrategies.ts` is used by both Sort Extras paths.

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcNxhsbNVXaWxLXFPYLY6wy2)_

## Description

Fixes M12 from the 1.5.0 release review.

Before: production builds always ran `app.set("trust proxy", 1)`. On an instance exposed without a reverse proxy, any client could send a random `X-Forwarded-For` on each request, get a new `req.ip`, and so a fresh bucket in every rate limiter, including the 20-attempt login limit.

After: Questarr trusts no proxy by default. The new `TRUST_PROXY` env var turns it on: a hop count (`1` for a single nginx/Traefik/Caddy, `true` = `1`), or a comma-separated list of proxy IPs/subnets (`172.16.0.0/12`, `loopback`, ...). An invalid value fails startup like other env vars. `true` maps to one hop on purpose: Express's own `true` trusts the whole chain and would take the client-controlled left-most entry.

How: `server/trust-proxy.ts` parses and validates the value, `server/config.ts` exposes it as `config.server.trustProxy`, and `server/app.ts` applies it. The auth cookies' `Secure` flag now comes from `req.secure` only; the old `isProduction && X-Forwarded-Proto === "https"` fallback read a header a client could also forge when no proxy is trusted.

**Upgrade note (in the changelog):** reverse-proxy users should set `TRUST_PROXY=1`. Without it, everything still works, but all clients share the proxy's IP for rate limiting and cookies lose the `Secure` flag behind an HTTPS proxy.

Docs: `docs/REVERSE_PROXY.md` (new "Trust the proxy" section), `docs/SECRETS.md`, `docs/SECURITY.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md` (1.5.0 Security), `.env.example`, both compose files, README.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcDUS84N1qQPrQto7GWsm1Fv)_

## Description

Before: upgrading a 1.4.x install to 1.5.0 broke every indexer and download client reached over plain HTTP with credentials (`http://prowlarr:9696`, `http://192.168.1.10:8080`, ...). Migrations 0033/0034 added `allow_insecure_lan` as 0 on every existing row, so on first start Questarr stopped sending API keys (indexers answered 401) and refused to send downloader passwords ("refusing to send credentials over unencrypted HTTP"). Because most clients swallow that error, in-flight downloads were then marked failed after a few status checks.

After: existing plain-HTTP indexers and downloaders are opted in once by a data migration, so they keep working exactly as in 1.4.x. HTTPS rows are untouched, and anything added from now on stays opt-in.

How: custom SQLite migration `0044_backfill_insecure_lan`. An indexer counts as HTTP when its URL starts with `http://`. A downloader counts as HTTP when its URL starts with `http://`, or has no scheme and `use_ssl` is off, which is how the clients build their base URL. Postgres gets no backfill: it only shipped in 1.5.0 release candidates with the column present from `0000_init`, so a false there may be deliberate. Instead `scripts/sqlite-to-pg.ts` now refuses a SQLite source with pending migrations, so a library copied to Postgres has already been backfilled by 0044 (DATABASE.md updated).

Found in the 1.5.0 release review; Vincent chose this over an upgrade note only.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcJBkEKevTVYeaNW4VS9aJmx)_

## Description

This is part 1 of release scoring (Questarr-mgmt #12). It adds the engine only, and nothing calls it yet. The database tables, auto-search integration and settings UI come in later PRs.

**Branch base:** this branch starts from #1164 (sequel detection in `title-utils.ts`). Until #1164 merges, its 6 commits appear in this diff. The 2 commits for this PR are the last two.

Before: auto-search filters results by platform, preferred groups and blacklists, then sorts them by date or seeders. Nothing explains why one release is preferred over another.

After: `shared/release-scoring.ts` returns an evaluation for each release:
- a score;
- the lines that make up the score;
- typed rejections;
- a title match class: `exact`, `contains`, `ambiguous`, `spinoff`, `sequel` or `mismatch`.

The module is pure, so the server (auto-search) and the client (search dialog, "test a release name" preview) can both use it.

**What it does**

- **Title classification.**
  - Matches word sequences, not substrings, and ignores edition, source, platform, language and scene words.
  - Handles spelling differences between IGDB titles and release names: `S.T.A.L.K.E.R.`, `Tom Clancy's`, `&` and `And`, a missing "The".
  - Sequels are rejected and the rejection cannot be disabled. A title with extra words after an unnumbered game name (`DOOM.Eternal` for "DOOM") counts as a spinoff and loses points.
  - Takes IGDB alternative titles into account.
- **Indexer categories.** Newznab 1xxx, 4000 and 4050 count as games. 2xxx, 3xxx and 5xxx to 7xxx count as non-games. Unknown, custom or missing categories never count against a release.
- **Built-in rules.** These are code constants, so their weights can change without a migration, and a profile can override their points or disable them. They cover:
  - title match;
  - indexer category;
  - video, music or book releases;
  - platform;
  - scene, repack and storefront sources;
  - size far from the expected size;
  - executables or disguised files.
- **Release profile.**
  - Minimum score.
  - Required terms: at least one must match.
  - Ignored terms.
  - Both kinds of terms accept `/regex/`.
  - Seeder minimum, rejected as temporary.
  - Maximum size.
  - Per-profile custom format scores.
- **Custom formats** are combined like Radarr's: conditions on the same field are alternatives unless marked `required`, `negate` inverts a condition, and `hardReject` rejects the release. Regexes are compiled once per batch and limited to 200 characters. A format with an invalid condition is skipped and reported.
- **Ordering** follows Radarr's `DownloadDecisionComparer`, adapted: accepted, then score, protocol preference, indexer priority, then seeders by order of magnitude.

The design follows the research notes in the project, including a comparison with Radarr, Sonarr and Gamarr. It is adapted from the release-profile work in the Jessomadic/Questarr fork (GPL-3.0). It does not take over that fork's migration that turns off auto-search, its hard rejection of unknown categories, or its string-compared rejections.

**How:** `classifyTitleMatch` reuses `isSequelOf` and `withoutStopWords`, which are now exported from `shared/title-utils.ts`. `evaluateRelease` computes the facts about a release once, then applies the built-in rules, custom formats and profile checks. `evaluateReleases` scores and sorts a list.

When users can't decide what to play, the Library's new **Pick a game** action draws a game and lets them open its details or mark it as Playing.

Backlog Roulette defaults to owned games, with pools for currently playing and all visible games. It uses the current Library search and filters, always excludes hidden games, and avoids consecutive repeats when multiple games match. Empty pools explain how to adjust the draw; a single candidate disables rerolling.

**Mark as Playing** saves the chosen game's status through the existing authenticated mutation and puts it on the Playing page. Failed saves leave the selection open for retry. Open game details stay synchronized with refreshed Library data, including rating changes. The feature supports desktop and mobile, dark and light themes, and requires no extra setup.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc6RaLmVwimWr1x9apFgfzU5)_

## Description

Before: root folders lived in a Discover tab under Settings → Import, and they were only scanned when you clicked Scan, even right after you added a folder or turned on post-processing. In Needs Review, picking a candidate for a release-style folder (e.g. `Absolum v1.01 [CUSA53342] [EUR]`) failed with HTTP 500 "Selected IGDB game not found in top candidates", as seen in a user's production log. When none of the guesses was the right game, there was no way to fix the folder. The Needs Review list and the Library could also stay stale after a scan.

After: root folders and Needs Review have their own **Library Import** page, listed under Library in the sidebar (and in the mobile More menu). It is always shown, since the scan does not depend on post-processing. The Discover tab is gone from the import settings. A scan starts on its own when you add a root folder, switch one back on, change its path, or save the import settings with post-processing newly enabled (all enabled root folders). Picking any candidate shown in Needs Review links the folder. When no candidate fits, each entry has a search field: you type the game's name, search IGDB, and pick from the results. Needs Review and the Library refresh as the scan progresses.

The match failure came from `matchUnmatchedFolder` re-searching IGDB with the raw folder name, while the scan searches with `cleanReleaseName(folderName)`. The two searches return different lists, so the picked id was rarely in the second one.

How:
- `server/routes.ts`:
  - POST/PATCH `/api/root-folders` start a scan when a folder is added enabled, goes from disabled to enabled, or an enabled folder's path changes. PATCH reads the folder first, so an unknown id returns 404 before updating.
  - New POST `/api/library/scan/unmatched/search` (IGDB rate limiter, string fields validated, `query` of 1–200 chars).
- `server/routes/import.ts`: PATCH `/api/imports/config` scans all enabled root folders when `enablePostProcessing` goes from off to on.
- `server/library-scanner.ts`:
  - The picked `igdbId` must be one the server offered for that folder (the scan's candidates or any name search), then the game is fetched with `igdbClient.getGameById`.
  - `searchUnmatchedFolder` searches IGDB with the user's name and replaces the displayed candidates. Results are dropped if a rescan rebuilt the entry meanwhile.
  - `rescanRootFolderById` / `rescanAllEnabledRootFolders` queue one follow-up scan instead of dropping the request when the folder is already being scanned.
  - Batch scans show waiting folders as `queued`, and one failing folder does not stop the rest of a batch.
  - A scan that wrote any game emits `gameUpdated`, so the Library refreshes app-wide, even if the scan failed later.
- Client:
  - New `pages/library-import.tsx` route `/library-import`, added to `navigation-items.ts` under Library; `ImportSettings.tsx` drops the Discover tab.
  - `RootFolderDiscovery.tsx` applies `library-scan-progress` socket events to its status cache, polls while a scan is queued or running and for 5 s after a kickoff, and refetches Needs Review and `/api/games` when a scan's status or counts change.
  - Each Needs Review entry has its own search field.

pr.body: _Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc2jdDozJcChRwCkArPM35xF)_ ## Description Before: Apprise API 2 can require a login (`APPRISE_AUTH_REQUIRED=yes`, HTTP Basic Auth), but Questarr had no way to send credentials. API mode failed with `401 Unauthorized` against such a server. Putting `user:pass@` in the API URL does not work either, because `fetch` rejects URLs that carry credentials. After: Settings > Notifications shows optional **Username** and **Password** fields in API mode. When either one is set, every call to the Apprise API (notifications and the test button) sends an `Authorization: Basic` header. The password is stored encrypted with the existing credential key and returned masked (`********`). Resubmitting the mask keeps the saved password, and an empty value clears it. A username containing a colon is rejected, as apprise-api does for `APPRISE_USER`. When a login is combined with an `http://` URL, the card warns that it is sent unencrypted. How: `server/apprise.ts` reads `apprise.username` / `apprise.password`, decrypting the password through a lazy import of `credential-crypto` so modules that only send notifications don't initialize the database module. `buildApiHeaders()` adds the Basic header. `/api/settings/apprise` masks and persists the two fields. Two rules keep credentials from leaking over redirects: - `safeFetch` already drops credentials on cross-origin redirects. - With credentials on an `https://` URL, it is now called with `requireHttps`, so a redirect cannot downgrade them to http. `torznab.ts` applies the same rule to API keys. Plain `http://` stays allowed for the usual same-Docker-network setup, as it is for downloader credentials. CLI mode is unchanged. Added a CHANGELOG line under 1.5.0 > Integrations. Follows the Apprise 2 review of #1150. ## Screenshots Captured with headless Chromium against `npm run dev:test`. A small local server that requires `admin:s3cret` stood in for apprise-api, and its log confirmed it received the Basic header both times. pr.body:
Bumps the python-tooling group with 1 update in the /requirements directory: [apprise](https://github.com/caronc/apprise). Updates `apprise` from 1.13.1 to 2.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from apprise's releases.

Apprise v2.0.0

What's Changed

:tada: Welcome to Apprise v2.0.0! :tada:

This is the first official release of Apprise v2. It's a big one. Much of how Apprise works under the hood was rebuilt, and many features people have asked for over the years are finally here:

  • template variables to keep secrets out of your config files
  • tag priorities and escalation
  • smarter retries
  • timeouts
  • a detailed AppriseResult object returned from every notify() call
  • ...and much more

Note: :warning: This is a breaking release for anyone using Apprise v1.x. If you are a developer embedding Apprise in your own project, please read the Breaking Changes section below before upgrading. If you are not ready to move yet, pin your pyproject.toml or requirements.txt to apprise >=1.0.0, <2.0.0. The v1 codebase lives on in the apprise-v1-release branch. I will keep patching it for security issues and bugs where practical for a year or two, but v2.x is the way forward.

:warning: Breaking Changes

  • notify() now returns an AppriseResult object instead of True/False/None
    • bool(result) still gives you True/False, so most existing if apobj.notify(...): checks keep working. None can't come back from bool(), so a "nothing matched" result now reads as False.
    • The object also holds the logs for each individual service called, plus a status for each one, so your application can report exactly what worked and what didn't.
    • The status values line up with the CLI exit codes:
      • SUCCESS (0) - every service was notified successfully (the old True)
      • FAILURE (1) - the notification failed (the old False)
      • NOMATCH (3) - nothing matched the tags given, or no services were loaded (the old None)
      • PARTIAL (4) - some services succeeded but at least one failed (v1 returned False here)
      • TIMEOUT (5) - a service didn't finish before its time limit (new in v2)
  • Multiple body formats per service
    • In v1 each service supported a single body format. Services can now support more than one when the upstream service allows it (Telegram, for example, accepts both Markdown and HTML).
    • Apprise picks the best matching format automatically based on the format you send with, so it no longer rewrites your content when the service can already accept it as-is.
    • You can also choose the format yourself in the URL with ?format=.
  • Consistent error handling
    • Every error Apprise raises now comes from a single AppriseException family, so developers can catch everything in one place.
    • Each error still behaves like the plain Python error it used to be (a bad setting is still a ValueError, a disk problem is still an OSError), so existing try/except blocks keep working.
  • Deprecations removed - Apprise v2 starts with a clean slate:
    • The APPRISE_CONFIG environment variable is now APPRISE_CONFIG_PATH. The old name still works for now, but prints a deprecation warning.
    • The Email options use_pgp= and ?pgpkey= (deprecated back in v1) have been removed. Use pgp_mode= and ?pgppub= instead.

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcMirFoQMGqkEMNab5RWEnGp)_

## Description

Four fixes found during a review of the public forks. None of them had been proposed upstream. Each commit keeps its original author.

**1. Scope socket notifications to their owner** (from wonghanz/Questarr, fixes #1081)
Before: `notifyUser()` used `io.emit()`, so on a multi-user instance every connected user received everyone's in-app notifications.
After: the authenticated handshake also joins a `user:<id>` room, and `notifyUser(type, payload, userId)` emits to that room only. Ownerless notifications and app-wide events (`downloadUpdate`, `importTaskUpdate`, scan progress, logs) still broadcast; scoping those is left for a follow-up. The original patch was adapted to the socket authentication that main gained since then.

**2. Literal commas in Newznab `cat=`** (from arroadie/Questarr)
Before: `cat=4000%2C4050`, and some indexers then search only the first category.
After: `cat=4000,4050`, as in the Newznab spec and as Prowlarr and Jackett send it. All other parameters keep standard encoding.

**3. IPv6-aware scan rate limiter** (from snapetech/QuestarrNG)
`scanRateLimiter` now keys anonymous clients with `ipKeyGenerator`, so each IPv6 address no longer gets its own bucket. This also removes express-rate-limit v8's `ERR_ERL_KEY_GEN_IPV6` warning.

**4. Bounded archive extraction** (from snapetech/QuestarrNG, extended)
Before extracting, the archive is listed and refused if it has more than `ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES` entries (default 50,000), declares more than `ARCHIVE_MAX_EXPANDED_BYTES` (default 250 GiB), contains an absolute, drive-letter, `..` or overly deep path, or contains a symbolic or hard link.
Two additions to the original commit, both checked against real unrar 7.12 and 7-Zip 23.01 output:
- RAR archives are now listed with `unrar lt -v`. The Alpine `7zip` package is built with `DISABLE_RAR=1`, so the new preflight would otherwise have failed every RAR import in the image. A file split across volumes is counted once. This also fixes `isAlreadyExtracted()` for RAR, which silently returned "not extracted" in the image.
- The 7-Zip `-slt` parser returned no entries for `.7z` archives, because they have no `Folder` field. It now skips the archive's own block and reads directories from the `D` attribute.

Stream formats (`.gz`, `.bz2`) behave as before.

pr.body: _Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcSxLQoq7ymdNPN6zbvZ7VDK)_ ## Description Before: after syncing from a Prowlarr reached over plain HTTP (the usual LAN setup), every synced indexer answered 401 Unauthorized, and nothing in the UI said why. The indexer and downloader **Test** buttons failed on HTTP LAN targets even with "Allow insecure LAN connection" ticked, and the error was a bare "HTTP 401" that reads like a wrong key. A re-sync also wiped the categories chosen by hand on each indexer. The sync dialog only had URL and key, and both had to be typed again on every sync. After: the sync dialog has an "Apply to all synced indexers" section with an explicit insecure LAN opt-in (unticked by default, with a warning when the URL is `http://`), a priority and categories. Ticking the opt-in makes the synced indexers work, and a re-sync with it repairs indexers already broken this way. Empty fields keep Prowlarr's priority, the indexer's existing categories and its existing opt-in. After a successful sync, the dialog remembers the URL, the key and the options, so the next sync is one click. The Test buttons respect the checkbox. A 401 or 403 caused by a withheld key says so and names the setting to enable. Cause: since the insecure-LAN hardening (migration `0033`, in 1.5.0-rc1), the API key is only sent over HTTP when `allowInsecureLan` is true. The Prowlarr sync gave no way to set that flag, so the key was stored correctly but silently withheld from every request. The two `/test` routes hard-coded `allowInsecureLan: false`. The sync always sent `categories: []`, which overwrote existing categories on update. How: - `server/prowlarr.ts`: `getIndexers()` takes optional overrides (`allowInsecureLan`, `priority`, `categories`) and only includes the fields the user chose. The insecure LAN opt-in is never inferred from the URL scheme (Codex review). - `server/db/transactional-ops.shared.ts` (SQLite and Postgres) and `MemStorage`: sync writes the flag on insert and update when provided; otherwise an existing indexer keeps its own value and a new one defaults to false. - `server/routes.ts` + `server/middleware.ts`: `POST /api/indexers/prowlarr/sync` validates the new optional fields (`sanitizeProwlarrSyncData`: strict boolean, priority 1–100, numeric category ids). `POST /api/indexers/test` and `POST /api/downloaders/test` pass through `allowInsecureLan === true`. - `server/prowlarr-settings.ts` + `GET /api/indexers/prowlarr/settings`: a successful sync saves the URL, the API key (encrypted with the credentials key, like indexer keys) and the options in `system_config`. No schema change. The GET returns the redaction placeholder instead of the key. The sync route swaps the placeholder for the saved key **only when the URL matches the saved one**, so the stored key can't be sent to another host. Failing to save never fails the sync. - `server/indexer-caps.ts` `withheldApiKeyHint()`, used by the Torznab and Newznab clients: appends an explanation to 401/403 errors only when the key was withheld. This also covers indexers added by hand before the upgrade, which migration `0033` leaves opted out (decision taken in the project thread: no auto-migration). The idea comes from the QuestarrNG fork by @snapetech (1625627eb), reimplemented here. - `client/src/pages/indexers.tsx`: the new dialog section (a fixed list of standard Newznab gaming categories, since no single indexer's caps apply to the whole batch) and the prefill. The prefill happens once per opening, and changing the URL clears the saved-key placeholder. - `docs/API.md`: documents the new fields and endpoint. ## Screenshots Captured with headless Chromium against `npm run dev:test`, syncing from a local fake Prowlarr on `http://127.0.0.1:9696` that answers 401 unless `apikey` is present. 1. An `http://` URL with the opt-in unticked shows the warning: ![Dialog warning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/cd5c752945f408bb00148482e7336c0f2be2cc69/.github/pr-assets/1148/dialog-warning.png) 2. Syncing like that, Test explains the 401 (the fake Prowlarr logged a request without `apikey`): ![401 hint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/cd5c752945f408bb00148482e7336c0f2be2cc69/.github/pr-assets/1148/hint-401.png) 3. Re-sync with the opt-in ticked, priority 10 and two categories: ![Dialog filled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/cd5c752945f408bb00148482e7336c0f2be2cc69/.github/pr-assets/1148/dialog-desktop.png) 4. The indexers show priority 10 and 2 categories, and Test succeeds because the key is now sent: ![Test succeeds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/cd5c752945f408bb00148482e7336c0f2be2cc69/.github/pr-assets/1148/test-ok.png) 5. After a page reload, the dialog reopens prefilled from the last sync, with the saved key shown as a placeholder (`system_config` holds `prowlarr.apiKey` as `enc:v1:…`): ![Prefilled dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/e0626d6f546e2f23e0f3d756d7d68508c75bd343/.github/pr-assets/1148/prefilled-desktop.png) 6. Syncing straight from the prefilled dialog works with the saved key: ![Re-sync with the saved key](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/e0626d6f546e2f23e0f3d756d7d68508c75bd343/.github/pr-assets/1148/resync-ok.png) Mobile (390x844), new dialog and prefilled dialog: ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [x] Documentation update ## Checklist: - [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [x] If this PR adds a new actor/integration, external interface, or security-relevant change, I have updated docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/API.md, and/or docs/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md accordingly - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes (`npm run test:run`: 3473 passed; `npm run check` clean) - [x] For UI changes, I have included a screenshot or recording of it running - [x] AI-written with Claude Code (see session link below). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01U56dZA1tFz9tkm7mGkjPJY ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Prowlarr sync supports batch-wide insecure-LAN access, priority, and gaming categories. Unspecified options preserve existing indexer settings. * Sync settings are saved after a successful sync and prefilled when the dialog reopens. A saved API key is reused only for its saved URL. * Connection tests support insecure-LAN access when explicitly enabled. * **Bug Fixes** * Plain HTTP URLs without insecure-LAN permission show a warning. Invalid sync options are rejected, and errors display validation details when available. * HTTP authentication errors explain when an API key was withheld. * **Documentation** * Updated API documentation with Prowlarr sync options and security checks.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc5fsF9wm7DXjWVxYLLPqnnD)_

## Description

Before: every push to a PR started up to 16 jobs, and every push to `main` up to 19, even for a README edit. When several PRs were pushed close together, jobs sat in the queue without a runner for close to an hour and were then cancelled. Two pushes 40 seconds apart on the same PR both ran to completion.

After: a PR push starts 3 CI jobs (4 when it touches the Docker image inputs) plus E2E, CodeQL and SAST. Docs-only changes skip CI, E2E, CodeQL, DAST and Scorecard. A new push cancels the runs still going for the previous commit.

The repo is public, so standard runners bill no minutes (`get_workflow_run_usage` reports `total_ms: 0`). What runs out is the Free plan's limit on concurrent jobs, which is shared across all of the account's repositories. This PR reduces how many jobs each push starts.

How:
- **ci.yml**
  - `secrets-scan` and `check-overrides` are now steps in `sca-scan`, so `npm ci` runs once instead of three times.
  - The 4 test shards and `merge-test-reports` are now one `test` job. The full suite with coverage takes 2m41 locally on 4 cores, and coverage thresholds come from `vitest.config.ts` again.
  - On PRs, `build` runs on Node 22.19.0 only, since tests already run on 26.x. Pushes still build on both versions.
  - On PRs, `docker-build` runs only when the PR touches `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `entrypoint.sh`, `package*.json`, `requirements/`, migrations or `ci.yml`. `sca-scan` reads the PR's file list to decide. It always runs on pushes.
  - Added `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress`, and `paths-ignore` for docs.
- **codeql.yml, sast.yml**: cancel superseded runs. CodeQL skips docs-only changes. SAST (Semgrep with `p/secrets`) still runs on every change, so secrets in docs are still caught.
- **e2e.yml, dast.yml, scorecard.yml**: skip docs-only changes.
- **vulnerability-scan.yml**: runs on a push only when dependencies, the image or the VEX feed change. The weekly run is unchanged.
- **dependency-review.yml**: runs only when manifests change (npm, pip requirements, workflow action refs).
- **slash-command-listener.yml**: starts a runner only for `/deploy` comments. Before, every comment on an issue or PR triggered it.

No security check or test is removed, and the weekly schedules are unchanged. `main` has no required status checks, so the renamed and merged jobs block nothing. CONTRIBUTING's CI section is updated to match.

Validated locally with actionlint 1.7.7 (0 errors) and zizmor (no new findings, same high/medium counts as `main`). I also ran the full Vitest suite with the new reporter flags.

- `trimTrailingSlashes` in `client/src/lib/app-path.ts` uses a linear loop instead of `/\/+$/`, same result (`"/"` when everything is trimmed).

## Description

The Snyk open source program requires a link back to https://snyk.io in the repository README and on the project website. This adds:

pr.body: _Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcUEdBs7jDYEjappbi2hxzqv)_ ## Description Before: Questarr had no idea which version of a game the user had. Any "update" release found for an owned game raised **Game Updates Available**, even when the user was already on that version or a newer one. After: each game has an **Installed version** (free text) in the details modal, Overview tab. It is saved on Enter or blur, and the modal suggests versions found in the release names of the game's downloads. When a full-game or update download finishes, the version in its release name is recorded automatically if it is newer than the known one (it never moves backwards). Auto-search drops update releases whose version is provably not newer than the installed one, so they neither set the "updates available" flag nor notify. Releases without a readable version, or with a different numbering scheme, still count as possibly newer. How: - `shared/version-utils.ts`: detects `v1.2.3`, `v123456`, `v 1.10`, `Update.1.7.23`, `Build 12345` in release names, and compares versions conservatively (`null` across schemes, e.g. a build number against `v1.2`, or `v20231005` against `v1.2`). - `games.installed_version` column on SQLite and Postgres, with both migrations. - `PATCH /api/games/:id/installed-version` (trimmed, ≤64 chars, blank clears), documented in `docs/API.md`. - `server/cron.ts`: version filter on owned-game update items; `recordVersionFromCompletedDownload()` called when a download completes. - `InstalledVersionField` component in the details modal. IGDB does not publish patch versions. Its `game_versions` endpoint describes editions (GOTY, Deluxe…), not version numbers, so suggestions come from the game's own download history instead. ## Screenshots Details modal, desktop, after saving `v1.8.86` (the other versions come from the game's downloads): Mobile (390px): ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] Documentation update ## Checklist: - [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [x] If this PR adds a new actor/integration, external interface, or security-relevant change, I have updated docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/API.md, and/or docs/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md accordingly - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes (`npm run check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test:run`: 3392 passed) - [x] For UI changes, I have included a screenshot or recording of it running - [x] If AI is used to write the code (partially or entirely), provide the full model name (including version) and thinking level. Written with Claude Code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01E1E7VzAePnSst4yYWpwScV --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01E1E7VzAePnSst4yYWpwScV)_ ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * View and edit a game’s installed version, with suggestions from completed or imported releases. * Clear an installed version, or have it recorded after a completed download or import when a newer version is detected. * Update searches skip releases that are not newer than the installed version. * Download categories help distinguish full-game releases from DLC and other content when tracking versions. * Changes to installed versions sync across open sessions. * **Bug Fixes** * Failed version updates restore the last saved value and display an error message.

## Description

Fixes #968.

Before: a multi-file torrent whose display name differs from the folder written to disk (typical FitGirl magnet: name `Cataclismo (v1.3.16.0.451 + The Old Kingdom DLC) [FitGirl Repack]`, folder `Cataclismo [FitGirl Repack]`) was imported from `<save path>/<torrent name>`, a path that doesn't exist, so the download fell back to manual review.

After: when every file of a multi-file torrent shares one top-level folder, that folder is used as the import path. The torrent name is still used when files don't share a root folder, and when `downloadDir` already ends with the torrent name (rTorrent reports `d.directory` as the content folder and file paths relative to it).

How: `resolveDownloadRelativePath()` in `server/downloaders/utils.ts` now looks at the file list's common root (and `downloadDir` for the rTorrent guard). It is the single helper used by both the completion cron and the manual import planner, so both paths pick up the fix.
