pr.body: _Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcX3Z47H6mwofjJZkF38w3Gc)_ ## Description Before: the Files tab of a game grouped each file under a category guessed from its folder (`dlc/`, `update/`, `extra/`, `packs/`) or its file name, with no way to correct a wrong guess. After: every file has a small category select (Main game, DLC, Update, Extra). Picking one moves the file to that group immediately, and the choice survives reloads and later scans. The file is not moved on disk. How: new `PATCH /api/games/:gameId/files/category` (`{ path, category }`). It resolves the path with `realpath` and only accepts a file inside the game's folder, which itself must sit inside the configured library root (same containment rules as the scan, now shared helpers). It updates the matching `game_files` row or creates one, and sets a new `category_overridden` flag. `GET /api/games/:gameId/files` applies only overridden categories, so rows recorded automatically by the library scanner never mask the folder/filename guess. `categoryOverridden` is left out of `insertGameFileSchema`, so `POST /api/game-files` cannot set it. Schema: `game_files.category_overridden` (boolean, default false) on SQLite and Postgres, with migrations `0042` and `migrations-pg/0007`. A new case in the dialect parity suite covers it. Context: raised while reviewing #1129, where an AI release type of `unknown` falls back to the title guess. The fallback always gives a category, and this PR lets the user fix it when that guess is wrong. ## Screenshots Captured with headless Chromium against `npm run dev:test`, using a game folder holding `Hades.exe`, an update zip, `dlc/Hades.Soundtrack.zip` and an artbook. Before the change, the soundtrack sits under DLC because of its folder: ![Files tab with category selects](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/d77ad8c119c9980ea95419024623fb5c49652a1d/.github/pr-assets/file-category/files-tab.png) The select: ![Category select open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/d77ad8c119c9980ea95419024623fb5c49652a1d/.github/pr-assets/file-category/select-open.png) After choosing Extra for the soundtrack and reloading the page, it stays under Extras: ![After reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/d77ad8c119c9980ea95419024623fb5c49652a1d/.github/pr-assets/file-category/after-reload.png) Mobile (390x844): ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Documentation update ## Checklist: - [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [ ] If this PR adds a new actor/integration, external interface, or security-relevant change, I have updated docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/API.md, and/or docs/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md accordingly - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes - [x] For UI changes, I have included a screenshot or recording of it running - [x] If AI is used to write the code (partially or entirely), provide the full model name (including version) and thinking level. Written with Claude Code (see session link below). Local checks: `npm run check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test:run` (218 files, 3345 tests, both dialects). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01DTUqAvHrUU2XyQoZdMBKFF --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01DTUqAvHrUU2XyQoZdMBKFF)_ ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * You can now assign scanned game files to Main game, DLC, Update, or Extra from the game details view. Your selections are saved and retained in future scans, overriding the automatically determined category. * Long filenames are easier to inspect: hover over a truncated filename to view its full name.

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.1 to 4.38.2
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.38.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026

No user facing changes.

4.37.7 - 13 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.3. #4085

4.37.6 - 04 Aug 2026

  • Changed the default filepath for the new remote file address format that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 / 3.37.0 to .github/codeql-config.yml to align it with the suggested path that is used elsewhere. #4070

4.37.5 - 03 Aug 2026

  • Fixed a bug where a network error while streaming the download of the CodeQL bundle could terminate the init Action instead of falling back to downloading the bundle before extracting it. #4061

4.37.4 - 29 Jul 2026

  • This version of the CodeQL Action adds support for the tools input for the codeql-action/init step to be specified using a github-codeql-tools repository property. This feature will gradually be rolled out following the release of this version. Once rolled out, this allows for the CodeQL CLI version that is used in GitHub-managed workflows, such as Default Setup, to be set to a custom value. For example, customers who run into issues with rate limits when a new CodeQL CLI version is released can set the value to toolcache to always use the CodeQL CLI version that is available in the runner toolcache. For Advanced Setup workflows, the value provided for tools in the workflow definition always takes precedence unless the value of the repository property starts with !. #4037
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.2. #4051

4.37.3 - 22 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

Updates `jsdom` from 30.1.0 to 30.1.1
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v30.1.1

  • Fixed spurious window blur and focusout events and incorrect event.relatedTarget values when focusing an element after removing the previously focused element, which regressed in v30.1.0. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed focus and blur behavior across frames, and focusing the document's viewport through document.documentElement.focus(). (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed focus targets removed or disabled by blur listeners becoming active, and text selections made by focus and blur listeners being overwritten. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed element.focus() incorrectly focusing disabled form controls and <input type="hidden"> elements with tabindex="". (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed invalid style.setProperty() calls changing existing !important priorities, serialized styles, or mutation records. (@​FedgeNo)
  • Fixed !important handling when updating CSS longhands after shorthands, using variables or CSS-wide keywords, and assigning style properties directly. (@​FedgeNo)
  • Fixed <noscript> parsing with includeNodeLocations: true or inside frames to honor the runScripts option.
  • Fixed the storageQuota option being ignored by frames.
  • Fixed encoding detection of HTML and XML byte input to honor XML encoding declarations and detect UTF-16 without a byte order mark.
  • Fixed exceptions caused by truncated charset parameters in <meta> elements, and encoding detection incorrectly using incomplete <meta> tags. (@​FedgeNo)
  • Fixed XML serialization errors for namespaces named constructor, toString, __proto__, or "null", and incorrect reuse of namespace prefixes declared on sibling elements.
  • Fixed element.innerHTML and element.outerHTML in XML documents to reject invalid characters in attribute values and avoid stack overflows on large strings.
  • Fixed selector matching for :lang(), :nth-child(... of ...) after mutations, and :has() with duplicate IDs or nested logical pseudo-classes. (@​asamuzaK)

Updates `lint-staged` from 17.5.1 to 17.6.0
Release notes

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v17.6.0

Minor Changes

  • #1850 938d3f4 - Task functions like { title, task } can now use a logger function log() to emit output while the task runs. By default, the output will only be visible if the task fails, unless the --verbose option was used. Additionally, when the task rejects, the error will be shown in the output.

    import { defineConfig } from 'lint-staged/config'

    export default defineConfig({
'*': {
title: 'Fail if PDF files are committed',
task: async (filepaths, { log }) => {
const pdfFiles = filepaths.filter((f) => f.toLowerCase().endsWith('.pdf'))
if (pdfFiles.length > 0) {
log('PDF files should not be committed: %s', pdfFiles)
throw new Error('Failed')
}
},
},
})

  • #1854 30562bc - lint-staged now stages changes to all tracked files modified by tasks, including files that weren’t originally staged or didn’t match the configured globs. This can happen when your task has side-effects, or it's a function that ignores the staged files like () => "prettier --write .".

    If you have unstaged changes in a file and the task also edits that file, your unstaged changes will be staged too. Use --hide-unstaged to hide your changes while tasks run.

Patch Changes

  • #1860 4296532 - The assignment of staged files to lint-staged configuration files (when using multiple, for example in a monorepo) has been rewritten to be more efficient. As a reminder, each staged file is assigned to exactly one configuration (the closest one), even if that config doesn't match the file in its globs.

  • #1861 c45f28a - Fix running parallel tasks for a single glob, when tasks are created by a function. Nesting one level of arrays inside an array of tasks will result in the inner tasks running in parallel. This behavior should now be consistent when creating tasks using functions. In the following example eslint and prettier will run in parallel (for all files, when any JS files are staged):

    import { defineConfig } from 'lint-staged/config'

    export default defineConfig({
'*.js': () => [['eslint --max-warnings=0 .', 'prettier --list-different .']],
})

  • #1859 f0ea69d - Various performance improvements from skipping redundant internal Git calls.

  • #1856 69d7d17 - Partially staged changes are hidden in a uniquely-named patch file to avoid multiple invocations of lint-staged overwriting it. This makes it safer to run lint-staged in multiple worktrees at the same time.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcDbtNt2jyabA78HUSg9rJMe)_

## Description

Before: every test mocked the download clients and the indexers. No test ever sent a real torrent to a real qBittorrent, or checked that a finished download actually ends up in the library.

After: a new **Real stack** workflow runs the production build (`npm run build`, `node dist/server/index.js`, `NODE_ENV=production` with its real rate limits). It runs against real qBittorrent, Transmission and SABnzbd daemons from the Ubuntu packages, plus a fake Torznab/Newznab indexer. The journey covers:

1. First-run setup through the UI.
2. Adding the indexers and clients, with their connection tests passing.
3. A grab from the library: open the game, open its download dialog, click the release.
4. The real client downloading it, then Questarr importing it into `<libraryRoot>/PC/<game>/`. This is checked for qBittorrent and for Transmission.
5. For SABnzbd, the NZB showing up in the real client's queue. There is no news server, so it stops there.

How: `tests/stack/services.ts` writes the client profiles (with real credentials), the payloads and their `.torrent`/`.nzb` files, and serves the fake indexer. Each payload already sits in the client's download folder, so the client's own hash check finds it complete without a single peer, with DHT, LSD and PeX turned off. Locally, run `npm run build && npm run test:stack` once the three clients are installed. It takes about 2 minutes, because the download check runs every minute.

Two things this surfaced, not changed here:
- With the production limit of 100 API requests per minute per IP, ordinary browsing gets throttled. Loading the library, then opening one game and its download dialog, took 89 requests in 41 s. The second dialog's `/api/search` came back 429 with no message in the UI. The spec spaces its grabs across rate-limit windows so it doesn't trip it.
- Transmission saves into `<downloadPath>/<category>`, so with the default category the path is `.../games`. qBittorrent saves straight into `downloadPath`.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcDbtNt2jyabA78HUSg9rJMe)_

## Description

Before: `sca-scan` (and the release gate in `deploy.yml`) failed on every PR because of [GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv). This high-severity advisory covers every `node-forge` version, has no patched release, and `npm audit` offers no way to ignore it.

After: the audit gates skip advisories that the project's VEX feed marks `not_affected` or `fixed`, and the feed now holds that statement for node-forge, so `sca-scan` goes green again. Any other high/critical advisory still fails the build.

Questarr does not reach the vulnerable code. The flaw is in RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification (`publicKey.verify`, reached through `certificate.verify`, `verifyCertificateChain` and `csr.verify`). Questarr only uses node-forge in `server/ssl.ts`: it generates a self-signed certificate (a signing operation) and parses an admin-supplied PEM with `certificateFromPem` (no signature verification). Key matching and TLS go through Node's `tls`.

How:
- New `scripts/audit-prod.mjs` (`npm run audit:prod`). It runs `npm audit --omit=dev --json`, drops advisories whose GHSA ID has a `not_affected`/`fixed` statement in `security/vex/questarr.openvex.json`, and exits 1 if anything at or above `--audit-level` remains. It also accepts `--report=<file>` to reuse an existing JSON report.
- `ci.yml` (`sca-scan`) and `deploy.yml` call it with `--audit-level=high`. `vulnerability-scan.yml` keeps uploading the raw report and now fails through the script with `--audit-level=low`.
- The VEX feed gets the node-forge statement (`vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path`). `docs/VEX.md` and `docs/VULNERABILITY_MANAGEMENT.md` now name the VEX feed as the risk-acceptance path, replacing the "ignore/allowlist" that the policy mentioned but did not implement.

Checked locally:
- With the statement, the gate exits 0 at both `high` and `low`, and it lists the ignored advisory.
- With an empty `statements` array, it exits 1 and names GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv.
- `--report` mode gives the same result.
- ESLint, Prettier and `check:overrides` pass.

## Screenshots

Not applicable (no `client/src` change).

**Client**

- RAWG attribution link (required by RAWG's terms) rendered in the game details view

**Testing**

pr.body:
### Motivation
- The AI classifier needs an explicit `unknown` release type for cases it cannot reliably classify. 
- When the AI reports `unknown` the system should not treat that as a suspicious classification that blocks automatic downloads. 
- The download categorizer should fall back to title-based regex heuristics when the AI returns `unknown`.

### Description
- Add `unknown` to the canonical `RELEASE_TYPES` list in `shared/typesafe-types.ts` and include a matching criterion in the TypeSafe request body in `server/typesafe.ts`. 
- Ensure the AI-to-category mapping comment and behavior treat `unknown` like `other` so the regex-based guess wins in `shared/download-categorizer.ts`.

## Description

Before: with `ssl.enabled` and `ssl.redirectHttp` set, the server logs "HTTP to HTTPS redirection is ENABLED", yet plain HTTP keeps serving the app. The redirect middleware was added with `app.use` after the HTTPS server started, which is behind the SPA catch-all and every route, so no request ever reached it. Separately, with `QUESTARR_BASE_PATH` set, the HTTPS listener served the un-mounted `app` rather than the app under the base path.

After: `http://host:5000/library?x=1` answers `302 https://host:<ssl port>/library?x=1`, and `/api/health` stays reachable over HTTP for container health checks. HTTPS serves the same tree as HTTP, base path included.

**How**
- New `server/https-redirect.ts` holds the same redirect logic, with the hostname validation that prevents an open redirect.
  - `index.ts` installs it before `registerRoutes`, and it stays a no-op until the HTTPS server is listening.
  - It redirects with `req.originalUrl` instead of `req.path`, so the base path and query string are kept.
  - Requests already marked secure pass through, including `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` when `trust proxy` is set.
- `index.ts` captures the root request handler returned by `registerRoutes` before Socket.IO wraps the server, and gives it to `https.createServer`.
- The `sca-scan` fix from #1124 (engine.io, brace-expansion and fast-uri overrides) is ported here, because `main` currently fails that check. The commit becomes a no-op once #1124 merges.

**Tests**
- `server/__tests__/https-redirect.test.ts` covers:
  - no-op until enabled;
  - redirect with path and query, ahead of an SPA-style catch-all;
  - health check exempt;
  - malformed Host falls back to localhost;
  - base path kept;
  - forwarded HTTPS passes through.
- I also checked by hand with a self-signed cert and `redirectHttp: true`: `main` answers 200 on HTTP, and this branch answers `302 https://localhost:5444/library?x=1`. Health checks answer 200 on both, and Socket.IO polling works over HTTPS.

No UI change.

pr.body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcDbtNt2jyabA78HUSg9rJMe)_

## Description

Before: a release-readiness pass over the features added since 1.4.0 found four bugs.
- **Unauthenticated real-time channel (security).** The Socket.IO server accepted any connection and broadcast everything to it: the live server log stream (`logLine`), notifications, and download/import progress. Anyone who could reach the port could read them without logging in.
- **Playing / Shelved / Completed statuses got overwritten.** Grabbing an update for a game you're playing flipped it to Downloading, then to Owned when the import finished (or to Wanted if the download failed or vanished). A root-folder scan also flipped any matched game to Owned. As a result, games dropped off the new Playing page. Update and pack searches also skipped Playing and Shelved games, and Discover didn't count them as owned.
- **Auto-search dropped every Usenet result when a minimum-seeders rule was set.** NZBs have no seeders. The manual download dialog already exempted them, but the cron didn't.
- **"Delete game with files" could remove a whole root.** If a game's `libraryPath` was the library root or an opted-in root folder itself (for example, a manual import confirmed straight into the root), deleting that one game wiped every other game's files.

Two minor functional bugs were also found:
- **Games without cover art showed a broken image.** The fallback pointed at `/placeholder-game-cover.jpg`, a file that was never shipped.
- **Unknown `/api/*` paths answered with the web app's HTML and a 200**, which clients then failed to parse.

After: the socket handshake requires the same session as the REST API. The pipeline never touches user-set statuses, even when the user changes one mid-download or mid-import. The seeder floor only applies to torrents, and Usenet results rank by grabs. Deletion only targets paths strictly inside a root. Games without art show a bundled placeholder, and unknown API paths get a JSON 404.

**How**
- `server/socket.ts`: `io.use` verifies the JWT from the httpOnly cookie, the `Authorization` header, or `auth.token`, the last one for sessions still on the legacy bearer token. The new `verifyAuthToken` in `server/auth.ts` does the check.
  - A cookie-authenticated handshake must also come from this server's own origin or one listed in `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. WebSockets bypass CORS, so without this a same-site page could ride the cookie. It's the same rule `csrfProtection` applies to REST calls.
  - On the client, `client/src/lib/socket.ts` passes the in-memory bearer token when there is one, reconnects the shared socket if a handshake was rejected, and logout disconnects it.
- `shared/schema.ts`: new `USER_CURATED_GAME_STATUSES`, `isUserCuratedGameStatus` and `ACQUIRED_GAME_STATUSES`.
  - They guard every automated status write in `cron.ts`, `ImportManager.finalizeImport`, `library-scanner.ts` and the manual `/api/downloads` route.
  - Each of those writes also passes `updateGameStatus(..., { preserveCurated: true })`, which puts the curated-status check in the UPDATE itself. A status the user picks while a download or import runs is therefore not lost to an earlier snapshot.
  - The cron's `OWNED_STATUSES` now includes playing and shelved.
- `cron.ts` `categorizeSearchItems`: exempts Usenet from `minSeeders` and sorts Usenet by `grabs`.
- `routes.ts` (DELETE `/api/games/:id`) and `root-folders.ts`: strict "inside" check.
- `client/src/lib/cover.ts` and `client/public/placeholder-game-cover.svg`: `coverSrc()` resolves the placeholder through the base path, and every card, modal and the calendar use it.
- `routes.ts`: an `/api` catch-all 404 registered after every API route, before the SPA fallback (also under `QUESTARR_BASE_PATH`).
- Docs:
  - New risk-register row in `docs/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md`, a tweak to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and changelog entries.
  - The changelog line about Postgres now says `DB_DIALECT=postgres` is required. It said `DATABASE_URL`, which on its own keeps SQLite.
  - `GOAL-product.md`: the header claimed 100/100 while its own dimensions summed to 75.3. It's now 78.2, and the items that shipped are checked.

**Tests**
- Unit tests for each fix:
  - socket auth: no credential, forged token, cookie, cookie from a foreign or malformed Origin, a bearer token from another origin, and no log lines to a rejected client;
  - playing/completed statuses across import, download completion, disappearance and scan, plus the conditional update in both storages;
  - Usenet seeders and grabs;
  - root deletion;
  - `coverSrc`;
  - the API 404, with and without a base path.
- New Playwright journeys:
  - `playing.spec.ts`: status picker, then the Playing page, then a journal note that persists.
  - `integration-api.spec.ts`: create a key in Settings, use it from a cookie-less client for ping and library sync, check it can't reach `/api/games`, revoke it, check it's refused.
  - `realtime.spec.ts`: signed-in socket accepted, anonymous socket refused.
  - `fallbacks.spec.ts`: the placeholder cover actually loads, and an unknown API path gives a JSON 404.
- Upgrade path checked by hand: a v1.4.2 database with a row in every table migrates cleanly to this branch, and the main endpoints answer 200 on it.

## Screenshots

These were captured with Playwright against `npm run dev:test`. They're in the project's shared files, not attached here:
- `screenshots/release-1.5.0-pass/library-list.png`: Library list view. The Playing game shows the new 🎮 compact status icon (it used to fall back to ★).
- `screenshots/release-1.5.0-pass/playing-journal.png`: a game moved to Playing, with the journal note added by the new e2e journey.
- `screenshots/release-1.5.0-pass/placeholder-cover.png`: a library card for a game added without cover art, showing the placeholder (a gamepad outline on the card background) instead of a broken image.

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcJUrVbKxi6fcqPFfe1XQbq5)_

## Before

After #1120, the reporter of #1106 got a working deployment, but the output still looked broken:

- Right after "Network is up", the script printed `✘ Deployment failed (exit 1)` and "Container 110 was created but is not fully configured", then carried on and installed Questarr successfully.
- Every `apt`/`perl` call inside the container printed a block of `perl: warning: Setting locale failed` / `Can't set locale` messages.

## After

A successful run prints no failure message and no locale warnings.

## How

- **Bogus failure.** Run as `bash -c "$(curl ...)"`, `$0` is `bash`, not a file. `LOCAL_INSTALLER="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/..."` could then fail in the inner command substitution (for example when the shell's working directory is inaccessible). Under `set -E` the ERR trap is inherited there, so it printed the failure banner from inside the subshell, while the outer `dirname` still succeeded and the script moved on to the curl path. `$0` is now only resolved when it is a real file. Reproduced with an inaccessible cwd: before, the trap banner prints and the script continues; after, it goes straight to the curl path. Running from a checkout still picks the sibling installer.
- **Locale noise.** `pct exec` forwards the host's `LANG` (here `en_US.UTF-8`), which the Debian template doesn't generate. Both in-container commands now run with `LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`, which Debian always ships.

Checked with `bash -n` and the repro above; no Proxmox host is available here to run it end to end.

Refs #1106

pr.body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcVxWctdRGNAqNsFbU1n5VxS)_

## Description

Before: on `main`, the Playwright e2e suite failed at setup and none of the other tests ran. Nothing runs that suite in CI, so it had gone stale without anyone noticing. Running it exposed four problems:
- The production build (`node dist/server/index.js`, which is also the Docker CMD) crashes at startup with `Cannot find package '@shared/schema'`.
- `/login` without a session, including right after logging out, shows a Login button stuck on "Logging in..." and disabled. This happens in both dev and prod builds.
- The desktop sidebar has no way to open the Discover page. When the Library and Discover groups became collapsible, the Discover header turned into a toggle, and Discover had no child entry pointing to `/discover`.
- A full e2e run uses up the per-IP rate limiters (100 requests/min on the API), so a back-to-back run or a CI retry fails with 429s.

After: the server starts from `dist/`, Login works, Discover has a **Browse** entry, and a new **E2E** workflow runs the suite on every PR and on every push to main/release. The suite passes 8/8, twice in a row, including with `CI=1`.

**How**
- **Prod crash.** `server/game-journal-routes.ts` imported `@shared/schema` as a value (added in e4e93b5), and Node doesn't resolve that alias in `dist/`. It now imports `../shared/schema.js`.
- **Stuck login.** On a 401, the `/api/auth/me` queryFn removed its own query from the cache while its fetch was still in flight, so `isLoading` never went back to false. That query is now spared. Login cancels any in-flight `/api/auth/me` check and puts the logged-in user into its cache, so a late 401 can't overwrite the user.
- **Discover.** `navigation-items.ts` adds a `Browse` child pointing to `/discover`, the same way Library has `All Games`.
- **Rate limiting.** Setting `DISABLE_RATE_LIMITS=true` makes every limiter in `server/middleware.ts` skip. The switch only takes effect when `NODE_ENV` is explicitly `development` or `test`. An unset `NODE_ENV` means production to the server config, and the Docker image sets `production`, so the switch does nothing there. `dev:test` sets it. Unit tests check that neither `production` nor an unset `NODE_ENV` can turn the limits off. The switch is documented in `.env.example` and has a row in `docs/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md`.
- **CI.** `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` follows the same conventions as the other workflows: harden-runner, pinned actions, and a full `npm ci` because better-sqlite3 needs its native build, as in `dast.yml`. It installs Chromium for the locked Playwright version, starts `dev:test`, and waits on `/api/health`. It then runs `npm run test:e2e` and uploads the report, the traces and the server log. In CI the Playwright config adds the `github` reporter.
- **Stale e2e specs.**
  - Setup: the dummy IGDB credentials now pass the format check added in a91d2e6.
  - Navigation: the test goes through the child entries, now including `Browse`.
  - Game details: the test opens the dialog by clicking the card.
  - Escape: the test presses it twice, because the dialog auto-focuses the Download button, whose tooltip opens on focus and takes the first Escape.

## Screenshots

pr.body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcJUrVbKxi6fcqPFfe1XQbq5)_

## Before

Follow-up on #1106: after #1111 (nesting/AppArmor fallback) merged, the reporter tried again and hit the same failure, this time with `--debug 1` output showing the real cause:

```
NOTICE   start - .../start.c:start:2375 - Exec'ing "/sbin/init"
ERROR    start - .../start.c:start:2378 - Exec format error - Failed to exec "/sbin/init"
ERROR    sync - .../sync.c:sync_wait:34 - An error occurred in another process (expected sequence number 7)
```

`Exec format error` on `/sbin/init` is the kernel refusing to run a binary built for a different CPU architecture. The debug log's seccomp trace confirms the host is `x86_64`, yet the script had picked an **arm64** template. `scripts/proxmox/questarr-lxc.sh` selects the template with:

```sh
pveam available --section system | awk '{print $2}' | grep -E '^debian-1[0-9]+-standard' | sort -V | tail -n1
```

`pveam`'s catalogue lists Debian templates for *every* architecture Proxmox supports, not just the host's. `sort -V | tail -n1` on names like `debian-13-standard_13.6-1_amd64.tar.zst` / `..._arm64.tar.zst` picks whichever architecture suffix sorts last — `arm64` sorts after `amd64` — regardless of the host running the script. This is architecture-independent: it can misfire on any Proxmox host where the catalogue carries templates for more than one architecture.

(The #1111 nesting/AppArmor fallback wasn't wrong to keep — a start can still fail for that reason too — but it wasn't the actual bug here.)

## After

The script now reads the host's own architecture via `dpkg --print-architecture` and filters the template list to only that architecture before picking the newest version, so it can never download and boot a template that doesn't match the host.

## How

Added a `grep -E "_${HOST_ARCH}\.tar\.(gz|zst|xz)$"` filter (covering the template archive extensions Proxmox's catalogue actually uses) ahead of the existing `sort -V | tail -n1`, and used `dpkg --print-architecture` (already implicitly required — this script only runs on Proxmox VE, which is Debian-based) to get the host's architecture. Verified with `bash -n` (no Proxmox host available to run it end-to-end in this sandbox).

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcF8T1Zs8E1myfA6xKxXjVnG)_

## Summary

Response to a batch of GitHub code-scanning alerts. This PR holds what was worth changing in code; the rest were dismissal candidates (justifications given in the thread).

**Before:** `PATCH /api/settings/ssl` checked the request's `certPath`/`keyPath` against `FILE_BROWSER_ROOT` into `resolvedCertPath`/`resolvedKeyPath`, then called `validateCertFiles()` with the raw values instead (CodeQL #35–#38). Since `FILE_BROWSER_ROOT` is the realpath of the process cwd, the raw relative path points at the same file in practice, so this was a checked-vs-used mismatch rather than an exploitable traversal.

**After:** `validateCertFiles()` receives the same root-contained paths that were checked and later saved. A test asserts it.

Also:
- `console.error` format string (#406): the indexer-controlled `download.title` is no longer in the format-string position, where a `%s` could swallow the `error` argument.
- Missing rate limiting (#3, #4): the SPA catch-all route in `server/vite.ts` gets a limiter (300 req/min/IP); `generalApiLimiter` only covers `/api`.
- Dockerfile: `apk upgrade` in both stages for Alpine's patched `openssl`/`expat` (Trivy #417, #361, #351, #364, #363); the base image's bundled npm CLI is removed after `npm prune`, dropping its vendored `tar`/`ip-address`/`brace-expansion` (Trivy #350, #287, #286, #272). `CMD` now runs `node dist/server/index.js` directly (what `npm run start` resolved to). Consecutive `RUN` steps merged per SonarCloud.

The Semgrep `missing-user` finding on the new `CMD` line is the same accepted design as before (container starts as root, `entrypoint.sh` drops to `questarr` via `su-exec`); the `nosemgrep` comment is in place and the blocking `semgrep` job passes.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run check`, eslint, prettier
- [x] `npm run test:run`: all passing
- [x] New test fails against the old `routes.ts` and passes with the fix
- [x] `npm run build` output path matches the new `CMD`
- [x] `docker-build` CI job green

Closes #991

## Summary

Before: there was no way to globally hide releases by name. Only a per-game, exact-title blacklist existed (added one result at a time from a specific game's search).

After: Settings → Discovery & Downloads now has a **Release Name Blacklist** card where you can add terms (e.g. `HYPERVISOR`). Any release whose title contains one of these terms, case-insensitively, anywhere in the name, is hidden from:
- Manual per-game search (`GET /api/search`)
- Auto-search (both the "wanted games" and "owned games / update packs" cycles)
- The AI (TypeSafe/Jev) enrichment and auto-download sanity check — filtered releases are removed before Jev ever sees them, so a blacklisted title can't be auto-downloaded or classified

The filter is a per-user setting (`userSettings.releaseNameBlacklist`, JSON string array), mirrored on both the SQLite and Postgres schemas with matching migrations.

## How

- `server/search.ts`: new `filterByReleaseNameBlacklist(items, terms)` — case-insensitive substring match, same shape as the existing exact-title `filterBlacklistedReleases`.
- `server/routes.ts`: the aggregated search handler resolves the user's blacklist terms up front (independent of any `gameId`) and filters before AI enrichment.
- `server/cron.ts`: `searchAndCategorizeItemsForGame` takes the blacklist terms and filters before categorization, so both auto-search loops and the AI auto-download hold check are covered.
- `shared/schema.ts` / `shared/schema.pg.ts`: added `releaseNameBlacklist` text column to `userSettings`, with SQLite (`migrations/0041_tranquil_kingpin.sql`) and Postgres (`migrations-pg/0006_flashy_master_chief.sql`) migrations.
- `client/src/components/ReleaseNameBlacklistSettings.tsx`: new settings card (mirrors the existing Preferred Release Groups card), wired into `client/src/pages/settings.tsx`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` (typecheck, incl. schema-parity assertions)
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run test:run` (full suite, 3197 passed / 7 skipped)
- [x] Visual verification: ran the app via `npm run dev:test`, completed setup, added terms in the new card, saved, confirmed the "Release Name Blacklist Saved" toast (PATCH `/api/settings` round-trip)

pr.body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcJUrVbKxi6fcqPFfe1XQbq5)_

## Before

`scripts/proxmox/questarr-lxc.sh` always creates the LXC with `--features nesting=1` and calls `pct start`. If the start fails, the script just dies with the exit code and no actionable info — as reported in #1106, where the container was created fine but `pct start` failed with `sync_wait: 34 An error occurred in another process (expected sequence number 7)` / `Failed to spawn container`.

Investigation: this trace, combined with AppArmor `DENIED` audit lines in the reporter's journal and an ARM64 (`debian-13-standard_13.6-1_arm64`) host, matches a known incompatibility between LXC's `nesting=1` feature and the AppArmor stack shipped by unofficial ARM64 Proxmox VE builds (e.g. [Proxmox-Arm64](https://github.com/jiangcuo/Proxmox-Arm64/issues/9), Pimox) — the generated nesting AppArmor profile fails to apply and the container never spawns. It reproduces regardless of storage backend, which matches the reporter's own observation. This isn't something our repo can fix upstream, and it isn't reproducible on standard x86 Proxmox, so it can't be verified end-to-end here — but nesting isn't actually required for Questarr (it just runs a plain systemd service, no Docker-in-LXC), so it's safe to drop automatically when it's the cause of the failure.

## After

`pct start` output is now captured. On failure, if the container was created with `nesting=1`, the script disables nesting (`pct set --features nesting=0`) and retries the start once, printing a warning explaining why and linking back to #1106. If the retry also fails (or nesting wasn't the culprit), it fails with the captured `pct start` output shown to the user instead of just an opaque exit code.

## How

Wrapped the existing `pct start` call to capture stdout/stderr to a temp file, added the nesting-disable retry path, and print the captured log on any remaining failure so future reports carry useful diagnostics instead of the generic trap-based exit message.

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026

No user facing changes.

4.37.7 - 13 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.3. #4085

4.37.6 - 04 Aug 2026

  • Changed the default filepath for the new remote file address format that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 / 3.37.0 to .github/codeql-config.yml to align it with the suggested path that is used elsewhere. #4070

4.37.5 - 03 Aug 2026

  • Fixed a bug where a network error while streaming the download of the CodeQL bundle could terminate the init Action instead of falling back to downloading the bundle before extracting it. #4061

4.37.4 - 29 Jul 2026

  • This version of the CodeQL Action adds support for the tools input for the codeql-action/init step to be specified using a github-codeql-tools repository property. This feature will gradually be rolled out following the release of this version. Once rolled out, this allows for the CodeQL CLI version that is used in GitHub-managed workflows, such as Default Setup, to be set to a custom value. For example, customers who run into issues with rate limits when a new CodeQL CLI version is released can set the value to toolcache to always use the CodeQL CLI version that is available in the runner toolcache. For Advanced Setup workflows, the value provided for tools in the workflow definition always takes precedence unless the value of the repository property starts with !. #4037
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.2. #4051

4.37.3 - 22 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

Updates `jsdom` from 30.0.1 to 30.1.0
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v30.1.0

jsdom is feeling the AGI!

This release is dedicated to @​scttcper, who unleashed @​codex upon jsdom and found tons of performance improvements. Along the way, he found and fixed many correctness issues as well.

We really appreciate his thoughtful PRs, which did a great job following the project's contribution guidelines, and were clearly human-curated, with their PR descriptions edited to be brief and respectful of the maintainers' time.

Thanks to @​scttcper, as well as all the other contributors of this release (most of whom were AI-assisted).

  • Added named access to elements on document, such as document.myForm for <form name="myForm">. (@​vojtisprime11)
  • Added QuotaExceededError, including its use for storage quota errors and oversized crypto.getRandomValues() requests.
  • Added support for the relaxed DOM naming rules when creating elements, attributes, and document types.
  • Improved performance of DOM construction, tree mutations, range operations, and live collection access, especially on large documents. (@​scttcper, @​erezrokah)
  • Improved performance of getComputedStyle(), style changes, and CSS serialization. (@​scttcper, @​jhult)
  • Improved performance of event dispatch, form control and label lookups, and updates to <select> elements and radio button groups. (@​scttcper)
  • Reduced memory use when creating and working with DOM nodes, attributes, event listeners, and mutation observers. (@​scttcper)
  • Changed window.close() to preserve access to the document and its DOM through retained references.
  • Fixed element.querySelectorAll() returning no matches when the first part of the selector matches the element itself, which regressed in v30.0.0. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed case sensitivity in CSS attribute selectors, including selectors matching data-state="", title="", and other case-sensitive values. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed document.querySelector() failing to find a matching element when an earlier element has the same ID but does not match the rest of the selector. (@​vojtisprime11)
  • Fixed :focus matching in shadow trees. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed DOM insertion and replacement, including valid document.replaceChildren() calls, invalid document element and doctype placements, and mutations during element.replaceWith().
  • Fixed the ordering of script execution, custom element callbacks, iframe loading, and mutation observer notifications during DOM insertion, including in shadow trees.
  • Fixed queued events and navigation continuing after window.close() or iframe removal, and prevented new scripts, resource loads, timers, and animation frames from starting in destroyed documents. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed parent documents waiting indefinitely for loading to finish when a child iframe removes itself during loading.
  • Fixed request cancellation across redirects, during pending requestInterceptor() callbacks, and when reusing an XMLHttpRequest after aborting it.
  • Fixed resource loading and JSDOM.fromURL() potentially hanging when response handling throws and response stream cleanup does not finish.
  • Fixed successful cached resource loads being treated as aborted.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() and document.styleSheets using the wrong stylesheet order after inserting or updating <style> elements.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() ignoring nested @import and @media rules in imported stylesheets, and returning stale results after imports finish loading.
  • Fixed style invalidation, stylesheet removal, and frame source updates in shadow trees.
  • Fixed repeated getComputedStyle() calls changing case-sensitive background URLs, and inconsistent resolution of border shorthands containing system colors. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed computed border widths, including borderless elements incorrectly reporting 16px, which regressed in v30.0.0. (@​Alberto-BaseNet)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() to resolve 'font-weight' keywords to numeric values. (@​tianrking)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() to convert lengths to pixels inside CSS math functions containing percentages, and to resolve percentages in 'font-size' math functions. (@​soroushm)
  • Fixed serialization of min() and max() containing nested calc(), which regressed in v30.0.0. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed CSS values mixing lengths or percentages with math functions, such as 'grid-template-columns' values containing both 100px and calc(). (@​rome-xi)
  • Fixed parsing of 'background' and 'border' shorthands with adjacent components, such as url(a.png)no-repeat, including a crash when parsing inline styles. Also fixed handling of invalid shorthand assignments and escaped or unusual characters in CSS declarations. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed parsing of unitless zero values in 'flex' shorthands, such as 35 1 0, and rejection of negative 'flex-basis' lengths and percentages. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed shorthand style assignments producing extra mutation records and custom element callbacks for intermediate values. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed Range and Selection handling of CDATA sections, including boundary offsets and range cloning, extraction, deletion, insertion, and stringification. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed text.normalize() incorrectly removing the text node or merging its siblings. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed cloning and importing CDATA sections and processing instructions whose contents have been modified, and serialization of CDATA sections adopted into HTML documents.
  • Fixed stale named-property collections on window, and incorrect named access from empty or namespaced id="" and name="" values. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed elements in documents created with DOMParser or document.implementation.createHTMLDocument() appearing as named properties on window and being retained in memory. (@​Iaotle)
  • Fixed memory leaks from mutation observers retaining observed nodes, abort signals retaining removed event listeners, and storage event tracking retaining closed windows. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed storage events being sent to windows created after the storage change, and ensured surviving recipients still receive events when the source document is destroyed.
  • Fixed attribute lookups after namespace prefix changes, and namespaced attributes incorrectly affecting ID lookups and element behavior. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed input.list in detached element trees. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed attr.ownerDocument after setting an attribute node on an element in another document or adopting its element. (@​Kjubikstronk)

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcPPz7cPkzoj3qy8sEDW9MEX)_

## Description

**Before:** `server/igdb.ts` already fetched a game's IGDB "expansions" (DLC, updates, etc.) and included them in `IGDBClient.formatGameData()`'s output — this was added incidentally in an earlier PR (`fix: preserve IGDB expansion metadata`) to survive a merge conflict, not as a finished feature. The data was then dropped before reaching any user: the `games` table had no column for it, `/api/games/refresh-metadata` explicitly excluded `expansions` from the fields it copies to the database, and `storage.ts`'s `addGame` implementations enumerated fields explicitly without `expansions`. No client code ever read it. Result: opening a game's details page never showed its DLC, even though IGDB metadata for it was being fetched all along.

**After:** Games now persist their IGDB expansions, and the Game Details modal has a new **DLC** tab listing each one with its cover art, name, release year, a category badge (DLC / Update / Extra), and a link to the expansion's own IGDB page. The tab and its badge count only appear when a game actually has expansions data.

## How

- Added an `expansions` JSON column to `games` in both `shared/schema.ts` (SQLite) and its Postgres mirror `shared/schema.pg.ts`, with migrations generated for both dialects (`migrations/0040_...`, `migrations-pg/0005_...`). Compile-time (`shared/schema-parity.ts`) and runtime (`shared/__tests__/schema-parity.test.ts`) parity guards pass unchanged since they check per-table shape generically.
- Added the IGDB `url` field to the expansions query in `server/igdb.ts` so each DLC entry can link to its own IGDB page (`igdbUrl`).
- Wired `expansions` through `/api/games/refresh-metadata` (was silently dropped) and through both `DatabaseStorage.addGame` and `MemStorage.addGame` in `server/storage.ts` (the real DB-backed implementation enumerated fields explicitly and dropped it).
- Added a DLC tab to `GameDetailsModal.tsx`, styled consistently with the existing Media/Files tabs (cover grid, category badges reusing the app's DLC/Update/Extra/Packs vocabulary), sharing the tab-trigger structure with every other tab via a `GameTabTrigger` component (also used to fold in `main`'s new Journal tab after a merge, keeping both deduplicated).

## Screenshots

Verified locally by driving the DLC tab in a headless browser (two seeded expansions, badge count, category badges, IGDB link). Not committing the screenshot to the repo: cover art didn't load in the sandbox (`images.igdb.com` is blocked by its egress policy) and an unrelated xREL error toast from the sandbox network was visible in the corner, so it wasn't a clean piece of evidence to keep around — removed per review feedback.

_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zcNsa7sZuEWd4G5diSHxtng2)_

## Description

Resumes #1018, which was left open since 2026-09-10 on `ForceConstant`'s fork and had drifted out of merge with `main` (conflict in `shared/__tests__/schema.test.ts`, plus two new type errors from `main`'s stricter TypeScript config that landed after the fork branch was cut). Since I don't have push access to `ForceConstant/Questarr`, this PR rebuilds that same work on top of current `main` and supersedes #1018, which I'll close with a pointer here.

Adds a single **Platforms** setting (Settings → Platforms) that governs every platform selector in the app: the Library platform filter, the download-search platform filter, the Discover and Add Game dropdowns, and the import engine's eligibility check. The stored shape is a list of IGDB platform ids (`importPlatformIds`, already used by the import filter) — this PR does not add a new `hiddenPlatforms` column; it extends the existing setting's reach instead, and adds validation so a malformed payload for it (or the sibling `ignoredExtensions` array) is rejected instead of persisted verbatim.

Checked = the platforms the user uses. Anything unchecked is hidden from every selector. An empty list means "no restriction" and shows everything.

### Before / After

Before: the Library platform dropdown, the Discover/Add Game platform pickers, and the download-search platform filter all listed every platform IGDB reports, regardless of which platforms a user actually collects for.

After: all of those surfaces narrow to the platforms selected in Settings → Platforms. Leaving the selection empty keeps the old "show everything" behavior.

## Fixes made while resuming this PR

- Resolved the merge conflict against current `main` in `shared/__tests__/schema.test.ts` (both sides added distinct, non-overlapping test cases).
- Fixed a `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` type error in `client/src/pages/discover.tsx` introduced by `main`'s stricter TS config (merged after this PR was originally opened).
- Fixed the IGDB-id-to-canonical-platform map in `shared/platforms.ts`: original Xbox (IGDB id 11) needs to map to the legacy account-wide `"Xbox"` umbrella label (which `matchesPlatformFilter` expands to cover every Xbox generation), not the newer generation-specific `"Xbox Classic"` label — the type was too narrow to express that and TypeScript caught it.

## Verification

- `npm run check`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run test:run` (3082 tests) all pass.
- Ran the app live against `npm run dev:test`: verified the Platforms picker in Settings saves selections, and that selecting PlayStation 5 + Nintendo Switch there narrows the Discover page's "By Platform" dropdown accordingly.

pr.body:
Closes doezer/questarr#1092

## Description

Adds an optional Security & Scanning step under **Settings > Post-Processing (Import) > Security & Scanning** that runs before a completed download is unpacked or moved into the library.

**Execution flow** (in `ImportManager.processImport`, right after the existing path-validation checks and before archive extraction/library transfer):
1. **VirusTotal (hash-based):** computes the SHA-256 hash of the downloaded archive/primary file and does a `GET /files/{hash}` lookup against VirusTotal, with a hard 10s timeout. If the number of flagging engines exceeds a configurable threshold, the import is aborted.
2. **Unknown-hash policy:** if VirusTotal has never seen the hash, a warning is logged and the import proceeds by default ("Block unknown hashes" is opt-in, off by default, so new legitimate releases aren't blocked).
3. **ClamAV (local deep scan):** if configured, streams the downloaded file(s) to a ClamAV daemon over its INSTREAM protocol (raw TCP, SSRF-safe host resolution via the existing `resolveSafeAddress`). A signature match aborts the import.
4. **Quarantine + notification:** a flagged download is moved to an isolated `.questarr-quarantine` directory (a sibling of the library root, never inside it) instead of being imported, the `gameDownloads` row is marked with a new `quarantined` status, and a "Security Alert" notification is raised (in-app + Apprise, following the existing notification-preferences pattern).

Both scanners **fail open** on network/timeout errors — a scanner outage never blocks the import queue. Only an actual detection, or an unknown hash under the strict "block unknown" policy, blocks an import.

Quarantined downloads are surfaced in the existing "Pending Manual Imports" card (relabeled contextually) with a "Dismiss" action, so they're not a silent dead end.

### New settings (Settings > Import > Security & Scanning)
- VirusTotal: enable toggle, API key (masked once saved, with a Test button that validates the key against VirusTotal), detection threshold, "Block unknown hashes" toggle.
- ClamAV: enable toggle, host, port, with a Test button that pings the daemon.

Settings are stored in the existing `systemConfig` key-value table, following the same pattern as the existing Apprise/Discord integration settings (masked secret on GET, unchanged-sentinel on PATCH).

### Files touched
- `server/security-scan.ts` (new) — hashing, VirusTotal client, ClamAV client, scan orchestration
- `server/services/ImportManager.ts` — wires the scan into `processImport`, adds `quarantineDownload()`
- `server/services/index.ts` — instantiates `SecurityScanService`
- `server/routes.ts` — `GET/POST /api/settings/security-scan`, `POST /api/settings/security-scan/test`
- `server/storage.ts`, `server/routes/import.ts` — surfaces the new `quarantined` status
- `shared/schema.ts` — `QUARANTINED_STATUS` constant, `securityAlert` notification event
- `client/src/components/SecurityScanSettings.tsx` (new), `ImportSettings.tsx`, `PendingImportsCard.tsx` — UI

## Screenshots

Verified against a running `npm run dev:test` instance with a headless browser: the Security & Scanning tab renders under Settings > Import, the VirusTotal/ClamAV toggles and fields work, saving persists to the backend (confirmed via reload), and the masked-API-key convention behaves correctly.

pr.body:
## Description

Follow-up to #1079, which merged with a CodeRabbit finding still open.

That PR added a section to `docs/MIGRATION.md` explaining that the pre-v1.1 migration must run under the operator's **original Compose project name** — volumes are namespaced `<project>_<volume>`, so a deployment that set `-p`, `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` or a top-level `name:` otherwise gets a fresh, empty `postgres_data`. The explanation landed. The two commands operators actually run did not, leaving the guide contradicting itself:

| Line | Command | `-p`? |
|---|---|---|
| L35 | `docker compose down app` | ❌ |
| L94 | `docker compose -p <name> -f … up` (the example) | ✅ |
| L114 | `docker compose -f … up` (step 3, the real one) | ❌ |

**Both omissions are load-bearing, in different ways:**

- **Step 3** reads an empty volume. Because the archived script continues past per-table failures and still prints `Migration completed.` — behavior this same guide warns about two steps later — it reports success over no data.
- **Step 1** targets a different project, so the original app is never stopped and keeps writing to Postgres while the migrator reads it table-by-table. That yields a torn copy *even when the operator gets the project name right at step 3*, which is the more insidious of the two.

## Changes

Both commands now carry `-p <your-original-project-name>`. Step 3 refers back to step 1 so the two cannot drift apart again, and step 1 points at the `docker volume ls | grep postgres_data` recipe already documented in step 2 for recovering the name. Operators who never set a custom project name are told to drop the flag.

Docs only — 9 insertions, 3 deletions, one file. The inlined `v1.4.2` compose block is untouched.

pr.body:
## Description

Removes `scripts/pg-to-sqlite.ts` (356 lines) and `docker-compose.migrate.yml`, and pins the documented pre-v1.1 PostgreSQL → SQLite migration to the archived **v1.4.2** release instead.

The tool shipped with the v1.1 move off PostgreSQL and has not kept up with the schema. **It is silently wrong on a current database:** its `MIGRATION_CONFIG` knows about **8** tables, the schema now has **19**, and the per-table `catch` at `:329-337` logs a failure and continues while `:342` prints `Migration completed.` regardless. Pointed at anything newer than v1.1 it migrates a third of the data and reports success.

Rather than rewrite a migrator for a path that ends at v1.1, the tool is removed and the procedure is pinned to the release that still contains it. Operators migrating a genuinely pre-v1.1 database go through v1.4.2 first, then upgrade normally.

### The version pin is load-bearing — please don't relax it to `latest`

`tsconfig.build.json` has `include: scripts/**/*`, so the script compiled to `dist/scripts/pg-to-sqlite.js`, and `Dockerfile:72` does `COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist`. **The script ships inside the published image.** A clean `npm run build` on this branch confirms `dist/scripts/` now contains only `clean-test-db.js` and `reset-password.js` — so `questarr:latest` can no longer run the migration at all, and the `v1.4.2` tag is both necessary and sufficient. No separate download of the script is needed.

Accordingly, `docs/MIGRATION.md` inlines the compose file **in full**, pinned to `v1.4.2`, since the file no longer exists on the default branch — verified byte-identical to `git show v1.4.2:docker-compose.migrate.yml`, the only change being `questarr:latest` → `questarr:v1.4.2` — and links both sources by tag permalink.

`README.md` drops its inline 5-step procedure, which linked `raw.githubusercontent.com/Doezer/Questarr/main/docker-compose.migrate.yml` — a guaranteed 404 after this commit — and points at `docs/MIGRATION.md` instead.

### ⚠️ Operator action: rotate credentials if you kept old migration logs

`docs/SECRETS.md` §8 flagged `pg-to-sqlite` for logging the full `DATABASE_URL`. Checking every tag that shipped the script:

| Tags | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `v1.1.0`, `v1.2.0`, `v1.2.1`, `v1.2.2`, `v1.3.0`, `v1.3.1` | `` console.log(`Connecting to Postgres: ${pgUrl}`) `` — logs the full URL |
| `v1.4.0`, `v1.4.1`, `v1.4.2` | `` console.log(`Connecting to Postgres`) `` — constant, no URL |

The exposure was **real for six tags** and was fixed in **v1.4.0** by commit `99984867` ("Fix visible postgreSQL URL in migration log"). §8 was **stale, not false** — it described a genuine issue and was never updated when the fix landed, by which point its `:157` reference had drifted onto the corrected line.

**If you ran this migration on v1.1.0–v1.3.1 and still hold those logs, rotate that Postgres password.** Purging them locally is not sufficient if they ever reached a log aggregator or CI provider. §8 now carries the table, the fix commit and this remediation; §9's operator checklist gains a matching item.

The `v1.4.2` pin this PR documents is on the safe side of the fix, so following the guide as written does not reproduce the exposure.

<details>
<summary>Two corrections I had to make during review — recorded for the reviewer's benefit</summary>

I got this wrong twice before landing on the above, both caught by CodeRabbit:

1. **First revision** repeated §8's claim into the commit message, changelog, migration guide and this description without opening the file.
2. **Second revision** overcorrected: I read only the v1.4.2 copy, found a constant string at the cited line, and retracted the finding entirely as "no release carried this exposure." That was worse than the original error, because it told operators with affected logs there was nothing to rotate. Checking one version and generalizing to "no release" was the mistake.

The current text is based on reading the line across all nine tags that shipped the script.

</details>

### Operator-facing fixes to the migration steps

Two ways the documented procedure could silently migrate nothing, both found in review:

- **`DATABASE_URL`, not `POSTGRES_*`.** The guide told operators to adjust `POSTGRES_USER` / `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` / `POSTGRES_DB`. Those only apply when Postgres initializes an **empty** data directory — against the existing volume they do nothing, while the migrator reads only `DATABASE_URL`, left at the sample value.
- **Compose project name.** "Run it from the same directory" only reproduces Compose's *directory-derived default*. Volumes are namespaced `<project>_<volume>`, so a deployment that set `-p`, `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` or a top-level `name:` gets a different project and a fresh empty `postgres_data`.

Either one, combined with the catch-and-continue behavior above, produces a clean-looking run over an empty database. The guide now covers both, and replaces the bare "Verify" step with one naming the `--- Migration Summary ---` table, the `❌ Failed to migrate table` / `⚠️ Integrity Check Failed` markers, and a `sqlite3` row-count spot-check before starting Questarr.

### Two notes for reviewers

**`pg` and `@types/pg` are now unreferenced on `main`, and are deliberately retained.** Nothing under `server/`, `shared/`, `scripts/` or `client/` imports `pg` after this deletion. They are kept because **#1046** (optional Postgres backend) needs them; a dependency cleanup here would break that branch.

**Not to be confused with #1046.** That PR adds a way to *run Questarr on* Postgres. This removes a tool for *leaving* pre-v1.1 Postgres. The references to `docs/DATABASE.md` (which arrives with #1046) are intentionally written as inline code rather than Markdown links so this PR is self-contained regardless of merge order — worth converting them to real links once #1046 lands.

# Pull Request

## Description

Follow-up to #1070 (the optional TypeSafe/Jev AI release-analysis integration). Auto-download (`checkAutoSearch()` in `server/cron.ts`) only ever fires once the numeric filters (min seeders, preferred platform, preferred group) have already narrowed a game's search results down to a single candidate — but that lone survivor can still be wrong: a DLC or crack-only release that happens not to match any of the title-regex keywords, or a "repack" with a suspiciously small file size. Since auto-download is the one path in the app where a release gets acted on without a human looking at the name first, this is where a bad classification actually matters, unlike the display-only badges added in #1070.

This reuses the already-built `typesafeClient.analyzeRelease()` — no new API surface, no new settings toggle — right before the single surviving candidate is sent to a downloader:

- If TypeSafe is configured **and** confidently classifies the release as something other than the full game (`dlc`/`update`/`crack_only`/`demo`/`soundtrack`/`other`, confidence ≥ 0.6), or flags the file size as implausible (legitimacy score < 0.5), the download is held back and routed through the existing "needs review" notification (repurposed from the multiple-results path: `Release Flagged for Review`, linking to the game modal) instead of downloading.
- In every other case — TypeSafe not configured, the call fails/times out, or the release looks fine — behavior is byte-for-byte identical to before. This is strictly additive and fails open, consistent with the rest of the TypeSafe integration (`enrichWithAiAnalysis()` in `server/search.ts` follows the same fail-open philosophy).

### Key design points

- **No new settings**: reuses the existing TypeSafe configuration from #1070 (Settings → Integrations). Nothing to configure for this specifically.
- **Cost**: one extra `analyzeRelease()` call, only when auto-download is about to fire on a single already-narrowed candidate — not per search result, so no additional cost concern beyond what #1070 already introduced.
- **Fail-open by design**: mirrors the existing philosophy — a broken/slow AI backend never blocks or breaks the core auto-search/auto-download flow.

pr.body:
## Description

Follow-up to #1045 and #1047. Enables `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` in `tsconfig.json` and fixes the ~103 resulting errors.

Almost all were TS's own suggested fix — widening a local/shared optional property from `field?: T` to `field?: T | undefined` — applied to interfaces we own: component props, `DownloadStatus`/`DownloadDetails`/`DownloadTracker`, indexer search params, `ImportReview`, etc.

A handful needed different treatment:
- Props spread onto external library components (wouter's `Router`, Radix's `Select`/`CheckboxItem`, recharts' `Pie`, `fetch`'s `RequestInit`) can't have their types widened, so those use a conditional spread to omit the key entirely instead of passing an explicit `undefined`.
- `server/storage.ts`'s `MemStorage` update methods spread a `Partial<T>` update onto an existing record. Added a `stripUndefined()` helper (`server/object-utils.ts`, kept out of `storage.ts` so `vi.mock("../storage.js")` auto-mocking in tests doesn't neuter it — caught this via a real test failure) that drops explicitly-undefined keys before the spread. This both satisfies the type checker and fixes a latent bug where an explicit `{ field: undefined }` update would have nulled out a non-nullable column instead of leaving it untouched.
- `server/logger.ts`'s pino setup had `base: undefined`, which pino treats as "no override, use the default `{pid, hostname}`" rather than as disabling those fields (pino's own code checks `base !== null`, not truthiness). Changed to `base: null`, matching the surrounding intent — this now actually takes effect.

`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is still not enabled — it surfaces ~300 more errors that need closer review. Left for a further follow-up.

## Description

Adds an optional, BYOK integration with [TypeSafe's Jev model](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction) — a "System One" model that returns typed, structured judgments (Choice / Score / Noul) instead of generated text. For search results, it now can:

- **Classify release type**: full game, DLC, update, repack, crack-only, demo, soundtrack, other (via a `Choice` question). This classification feeds `shared/download-categorizer.ts` so releases land in the right Main/Update/DLC/Extra section in the per-game download dialog when it's more confident than the regex-based title guess.
- **Flag implausible file sizes**: a `Noul` question asks whether the file size looks consistent with a legitimate release of that type, surfaced as a "Check size" warning badge when the plausibility score is low.

Both are display-only (per design discussion) — nothing is auto-filtered or blocked.

### Key design points

- **Fully optional / BYOK**: Questarr works exactly as before if unconfigured. Users add their own API URL + key under Settings → Integrations → "AI Release Analysis (TypeSafe)" (URL and model are both free-form so it can point at TypeSafe directly, an OpenRouter-compatible proxy like `typesafe/jev-1.13`, or a self-host).
- **Cost-bounded**: only the top 15 search results per query are analyzed (`AI_ENRICHMENT_MAX_ITEMS` in `server/search.ts`), since each release needs its own API call (the API batches *questions* per state, not multiple states per call).
- **Best-effort**: every call has an 8s timeout and swallows failures — a broken/slow AI backend never breaks search.
- **Credentials at rest**: the API key is encrypted via the existing `credential-crypto.ts` (same mechanism as indexer/downloader secrets) and stored in `system_config`, following the pattern already used for NexusMods.
- **SSRF-safe**: since the endpoint URL is user-supplied, requests go through the existing `safeFetch` with `requireHttps: true` (same protections as indexer URLs).
- **Classification feeds categorization, not a badge wall**: rather than adding a separate AI badge on top of the existing category grouping, the release-type classification is fed directly into `shared/download-categorizer.ts` and only wins over the regex-based guess when the AI is more confident. The general search page (`client/src/pages/search.tsx`, not reachable from the app's navigation) keeps only the legitimacy warning badge, since that's a distinct signal (fake-release detection) the categorizer can't express.

### New files / key changes

- `server/typesafe.ts` — thin API client (lazy-loaded config, `analyzeRelease()`).
- `server/search.ts` — `enrichWithAiAnalysis()`, wired into `GET /api/search`.
- `server/routes.ts` — `GET/POST/DELETE /api/settings/typesafe`.
- `client/src/pages/settings.tsx` — new Integrations card.
- `shared/download-categorizer.ts` — `categorizeDownload()`/`groupDownloadsByCategory()` now take an optional AI release-type hint and use it when more confident than the title-regex guess.
- `client/src/components/GameDownloadDialog.tsx` — passes the AI fields through to the categorizer.
- `client/src/pages/search.tsx` — legitimacy ("Check size") warning badge only.

## Screenshots

Verified live via headless Chromium against `npm run dev:test` (no real indexers/API key in this sandbox, so `/api/search` was mocked for these runs):

- New "AI Release Analysis (TypeSafe)" card in Settings → Integrations — empty/"Not Configured" state and after saving a key/"Enabled" state.
- Search results page with a mocked response: the "Check size" legitimacy warning badge renders on a suspiciously small release, and the release-type badge that previously appeared here is gone (that signal now only feeds the download categorizer, per the design change above).

No new console errors were introduced; existing search/settings flows verified unaffected.

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc98sJqZmtYe2T5nDeQmopp3)_

## Description

Takes over #955 (opened by @Exberg, whose fork branch isn't pushable from here) and brings it to green. The original PR's implementation and tests are unchanged in substance — only rebased/merged on top of the `DownloadCategory`/`GameFileCategory`/`ScannedGameFile` typing that landed on `main` after #955 was opened, which is what made the original PR's diff go stale and conflict.

Bounds the recursive Scan Disk endpoint per the acceptance criteria in #944.

`GET /api/games/:gameId/files` previously walked a game's library folder with no limits: no file-count cap, no wall-clock budget, no per-request rate protection. A very large tree (or repeated requests) could exhaust filesystem I/O, memory, and request capacity.

**Before:** the walk recurses without limits and always returns `{ files }`, even for a library folder with hundreds of thousands of files, and the endpoint has no rate limiting.

**After:** the walk stops once `SCAN_MAX_FILES` (5,000) files have been collected or `SCAN_TIME_BUDGET_MS` (5s) has elapsed, and the response becomes `{ files, truncated }` so callers can tell a capped result from a complete one. The route is also rate-limited to 10 requests/minute per authenticated user (IP fallback).

Changes:

- **File-count cap**: the walk stops once `SCAN_MAX_FILES` (5,000) files have been collected.
- **Wall-clock budget**: the walk stops once `SCAN_TIME_BUDGET_MS` (5s) has elapsed. Both caps set a `truncated` flag that short-circuits every pending recursion level on the way back up the tree.
- **Response contract**: `{ files }` → `{ files, truncated }` (all early-return paths report `truncated: false`).
- **Rate limiting**: a new `scanRateLimiter` (10 requests/min) keyed by authenticated user id (IP fallback), mounted in front of the route.
- **Budgets module**: `SCAN_MAX_FILES`/`SCAN_TIME_BUDGET_MS` live in `server/scan-limits.ts` with `setScanBudgets()`/`resetScanBudgets()` helpers so tests can trip the caps without creating thousands of files or waiting on real timers.
- **Docs**: `docs/API.md` gains the route row, and `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md` lists the new limiter/test.

## How

Merged `main` into #955's branch (`bound-scan-disk-endpoint`) to resolve the conflict against the newer typed `walk` implementation, then pushed the merged result here since the fork branch itself isn't writable from this session. No behavioral logic from the original PR was changed — only reconciled with the stricter types already on `main` (`ScannedGameFile[]`, `DownloadCategory`, `isCategoryDirName`).

## Screenshots

Backend-only change; no `client/src/**` files touched.

## Test evidence

- `npm run check` (typecheck): green
- `npm run lint`: green
- `npm run test:run`: 2876 passed, 7 skipped
- New/updated tests: `game_files_routes.test.ts` (file-count cap, time budget, complete-scan cases) and `scan-ratelimit.test.ts` (429 after 10 req/min, rate-limit headers)

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Documentation update

pr.body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Doezer"} -->
_Requested by **Vincent** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc?thread=cmsg_01Bbp9WkSHrxJWLwfbggk3zc4rmoHEYCYwUkk8UAnjdsMR)_

## Description

**Before:** zizmor flagged every job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that sets `cache: "npm"` on `actions/setup-node` (`secrets-scan`, `check-overrides`, `sca-scan`, `test`, `merge-test-reports`, `build`) as a potential cache-poisoning vector. This was called out during review of PR #806 (CI test sharding) and explicitly left open as a follow-up rather than fixed on the spot, since it's a repo-wide posture question, not something scoped to that PR.

**After:** each `cache: "npm"` line is annotated with `# zizmor: ignore[cache-poisoning]`, with the reasoning documented inline right above the first occurrence, and the same acceptance is recorded as a new row in `docs/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md`'s risk register (matching the format already used there for other accepted findings like COEP and CSP `style-src`).

The finding isn't actionable here: GitHub Actions caches are scoped per branch, so a `pull_request` run can't write into the cache a `push`/`main` run restores from, and every `npm ci` in this workflow already runs `--ignore-scripts`, so a compromised dependency can't execute install/postinstall code to tamper with the cache before it's saved. The repo also has a single maintainer with push access. Splitting cache restore/save by trust level (the alternative fix) would touch all 6 jobs for no real risk reduction in this threat model.

## How

- Added `# zizmor: ignore[cache-poisoning]` to the 6 `cache: "npm"` lines in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, with the full rationale documented once as a comment block above the first occurrence.
- Added a matching row to the risk register in `docs/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md`.
- Validated the workflow YAML still parses and both files pass `prettier --check`.

No behavior change to the CI pipeline itself — this only documents and suppresses a static-analysis finding.

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • Fixed a bug where a network error while streaming the download of the CodeQL bundle could terminate the init Action instead of falling back to downloading the bundle before extracting it. #4061

  • The new address format for the config-file input that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 is now enabled by default.
