Updates `multer` from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0
Release notes

Sourced from multer's releases.

v2.4.0

Highlights

multer finally supports Google Cloud Functions and Firebase 🎉

These platforms read the request body before your code runs, so multer's classic req.pipe(busboy) received nothing: empty req.body, empty req.files, and nearly a decade of duplicated issues.

The new streamHandler option closes that gap: you decide how the body reaches the parser, so the pre-read rawBody just works (see image).

const multer = require('multer')

const upload = multer({

storage: multer.memoryStorage(),

streamHandler: (req, busboy) => {

// Cloud Functions / Firebase expose the pre-read body here

if (req.rawBody) busboy.end(req.rawBody)

else req.pipe(busboy)

}

})


app.post('/upload', upload.single('file'), (req, res) => {

res.json({ name: req.file.originalname, size: req.file.size })

})

This landed thanks to community PRs going back to 2017; their authors are credited as co-authors in the release.

Important: Security

## Description

Follow-up to a discussion about IGDB/Twitch setup friction. It doesn't change the underlying credential model — Questarr still can't ship a working IGDB credential out of the box, since Twitch requires every application to register its own Client ID/Secret and a secret baked into an open-source client would be public the moment it's committed — but it removes the friction that *can* be removed within that model:

- **Server-side format validation**: `POST /api/settings/igdb` and `POST /api/auth/setup` now reject an obviously malformed Client ID/Secret (wrong shape — extra whitespace, partial copy, stray punctuation) before it's ever saved or sent to Twitch. In the setup wizard, this check runs *before* the admin account is created, so a bad format can't leave the account created but setup permanently blocked (setup can only run once).
- **"Test connection" button**, in both the setup wizard and the Settings → Integrations → IGDB API card: calls a new `IGDBClient.testCredentials()` method that performs the real Twitch OAuth handshake + one lightweight IGDB query against the entered credentials (without touching the app's cached token), and reports success/failure inline immediately — instead of the user only finding out later when a game search silently fails.
  - New endpoints: `POST /api/settings/igdb/test` (authenticated) and the public `POST /api/auth/setup/test-igdb` (only functions before the first account exists, so it can't become a standing unauthenticated Twitch-credential probe).
- **Copy button** for the `http://localhost` redirect URI in the help popover — the field most often mistyped.
- **Short explanatory text** in the popover on why Questarr can't provide a one-click credential.
- Extracted the previously-duplicated help popover into a shared `IgdbHelpPopover`/`IgdbTestConnectionButton` component pair (`client/src/components/IgdbCredentialsHelper.tsx`) used by both the setup wizard and the settings page, so the instructions can't drift out of sync between the two.

Also fixed a bug caught during manual testing: `apiRequest` throws on a non-2xx response, so the test button was swallowing the server's actual error message (e.g. "Invalid Client ID or Client Secret.") and always showing a generic "Could not reach the server" — fixed by reading the message off the thrown `ApiError`.

## Screenshots

Verified with a headless Chromium session against `npm run dev:test` (port 5100), driving the actual app rather than unit tests:

- **Setup wizard**: IGDB Configuration section renders with the help "?" icon, Client ID/Secret fields, and a disabled "Test connection" button when fields are empty.
- **Help popover** (both setup and settings): shows the numbered instructions, a copy icon next to `http://localhost` (confirmed clicking it copies the URI), and the new explanatory paragraph about why no one-click credential is possible.
- **Test connection, invalid credentials**: typing a dummy Client ID/Secret and clicking "Test connection" shows a "Testing..." spinner state, then the real server-returned message "Invalid Client ID or Client Secret." ## Description

Adds "Time to Beat" (Hastily / Normally / Completely, in hours) to game details, sourced from **IGDB's own `game_time_to_beats` endpoint** rather than HowLongToBeat directly.

Context: Questarr previously had a HowLongToBeat integration that was removed because it depended on reverse-engineering HLTB's internal endpoints (see `docs/CHANGELOG.md`: "Removed the HLTB integration from Questarr (no API or stable service)."). Ziff Davis's (HLTB's owner) Terms of Use explicitly prohibit crawling/scraping/automated retrieval of any kind, with no partner-API program found — so this PR does not revisit that approach. Instead, it uses IGDB, which Questarr already talks to as an authenticated, official integration (`server/igdb.ts`, Twitch OAuth), and which exposes the same completion-time data (community-sourced through IGDB itself) via its own official endpoint. No new external service, no new ToS exposure, no new trust boundary.

**Changes:**
- `server/igdb.ts` — new `getTimeToBeats(igdbIds)`, chunked queries against `game_time_to_beats`, converts IGDB's seconds to hours, 24h cache. Best-effort: a game with no IGDB submissions is simply absent from the returned map, never a zero/placeholder.
- `shared/schema.ts` + `migrations/0036_gray_mimic.sql` — three new nullable `real` columns on `games` (`timeToBeatHastily/Normally/Completely`).
- `server/routes.ts` — `GET /api/igdb/game/:id` merges time-to-beat into the single-game detail response.
- `server/cron.ts` — `checkGameUpdates()` batch-refreshes time-to-beat for tracked library games each cycle, which also backfills existing games with no extra migration script needed.
- `client/src/components/GameDetailsModal.tsx` — new "Time to Beat" block under the Ratings section, styled to match the existing rating tiles, rendered only when at least one value is present (nothing rendered otherwise — no placeholder/zero).
- Bulk listing endpoints (search, popular, recent/upcoming releases) intentionally do **not** fetch this, to avoid multiplying IGDB request volume for a list view.

## Summary

- Adds a "Crack Status" section to the game detail page's Overview tab, showing a **Cracked** and/or **Hypervisor Bypass** badge (e.g. EMPRESS-style Denuvo VM bypass releases) — both badges show together if the game has both. No group name, date, or link is shown; just the status.

pr.body:
## Description

Fixes #1036.

`downloaderAllowsCredentials()`/`assertCredentialsAllowed()` in `server/downloaders/utils.ts` previously decided whether a credential could be sent based solely on the downloader's `useSsl` config flag, while each client's URL builder kept whatever scheme was literally configured in the downloader's `url` field. A downloader configured `useSsl: true` but with a URL field that still literally starts `http://` would pass the guard (trusting the flag) while the actual request went out over plaintext HTTP, leaking the credential.

**Fix:**
- `downloaderAllowsCredentials`/`assertCredentialsAllowed` now take the *resolved request URL* and key the decision off its actual scheme (new `isHttpsUrl()` helper) OR an explicit `allowInsecureLan: true` opt-in — no longer trusting `useSsl` in isolation.
- Threaded the resolved URL into all 7 downloader clients' guard call sites (qBittorrent, Deluge, rTorrent, Synology, Transmission, NZBGet, SABnzbd).
- Added `requireHttps: isHttpsUrl(url)` to every credential-bearing `safeFetch` call that didn't already have it, so a downgrade redirect can't strip TLS after the guard passes. SABnzbd's existing (but flag-trusting) `requireHttps` logic was corrected to the same URL-based check.
- Test fixture default in `downloaders.test.ts` changed from `allowInsecureLan: true` to `false`, with explicit opt-ins added only to the tests that specifically exercise insecure HTTP credential transmission.
- Added the missing allowed-HTTP-credential test cases for qBittorrent and Deluge in `downloaders_insecure_lan_policy.test.ts`, plus a regression suite proving `useSsl: true` + a literal `http://` URL is now rejected (the exact bug class this closes) for Deluge, qBittorrent, and Transmission.

## Description

Fixes [CVE-2026-90711](https://vuldb.com/cve/CVE-2026-90711) (also tracked as [AIKIDO-2026-101201](https://security.aikido.dev/cve/AIKIDO-2026-101201)), a critical IP-spoofing vulnerability in `proxy-addr`, the module `express` uses to compute `req.ip`/`req.ips` behind trusted proxies.

Versions `1.1.0`–`2.0.7` accept an under-sized IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet (e.g. `::ffff:10.0.0.0/8` instead of the correct `::ffff:10.0.0.0/104`) without error, but the malformed prefix ends up trusting *every* IPv4 address on the internet instead of the intended block. Since the socket peer is then treated as trusted at hop 0, any unauthenticated client can send an arbitrary `X-Forwarded-For` header and control the address the app reads — defeating IP-based access control, rate limiting, and audit logging.

`express@4.22.2` still declares `proxy-addr: ~2.0.7`, a range that doesn't include the patched `2.0.8`, so the lockfile was resolving to the vulnerable version. Added a `proxy-addr: ^2.0.8` entry to `package.json`'s `overrides` (following the existing pattern used for `body-parser`, `qs`, etc.) and documented it in `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md`.

No dependencies were added; this is required for the change.

pr.body:
## Description

Fixes #1035.

Both Torznab and Newznab search clients silently dropped configured indexer categories that didn't start with `40`/`10` or contain "game"/"pc" — so an indexer that maps game content to a category like `8000` ("Other") could never return results for it, even when that category was explicitly selected in the indexer's settings.

This adds `resolveSearchCategories(requested, configured)` to `server/indexer-caps.ts`:
- Explicit per-request categories always win.
- Otherwise, the indexer's configured categories are sent as-is (no game-only filtering) — categories are picked deliberately per indexer via the category picker, so sending them unfiltered is the least surprising behavior.

# Pull Request _Template_

## Description

Fixes #1019: the claim and scan routes lowercased `downloadHash` / `downloadId` unconditionally. That's harmless for BitTorrent info hashes (hex, already canonical once lowercased), but Usenet ids (e.g. SABnzbd's `nzo_id`) are opaque, case-sensitive strings that the downloader clients match with `===`. A mixed-case Usenet id was corrupted on the way into `game_downloads`, so later per-item status lookups (`server/downloaders/sabnzbd.ts`, `server/downloaders/nzbget.ts`) never matched, eventually marking the download `failed`.

**Before:** `POST /api/downloads/claim`, `POST /api/downloads/claim-batch`, and `GET /api/downloads/scan` called `.toLowerCase()` directly on the download id/hash — for both duplicate-check comparisons and the persisted/returned value.

**After:** these call sites go through the existing `normalizeDownloadHash()` helper (`server/download-hash.ts`), which only lowercases 40/64-char hex torrent hashes and passes everything else (including Usenet ids) through verbatim. Added a new `normalizeTrackedKey()` helper to apply the same normalization to the hash portion of `"downloaderId:downloadHash"` tracked-key strings (without touching the downloaderId prefix), and used it consistently on both sides of the claim / claim-batch duplicate checks so they match what `getTrackedDownloadKeys()` actually returns.

## How

- `server/download-hash.ts`: added `normalizeTrackedKey()`.
- `server/routes.ts`: replaced the 7 `.toLowerCase()` call sites identified in #1019 (claim persist + duplicate check, claim-batch persist + duplicate check, scan's tracked-key set, scan's live-id key/returned hash) with `normalizeDownloadHash()` / `normalizeTrackedKey()`.
- Added regression tests: a unit test file for the new helper, plus route-level tests asserting a mixed-case Usenet id is persisted/returned verbatim and that duplicate detection stays exact-match for Usenet ids while remaining case-insensitive for torrent hashes.

## Description

Two related changes, prompted by the calendar-view PR (#1051), where taking a screenshot of the UI change was harder than it should've been:

1. **Require screenshots for UI PRs.** `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` now call for a screenshot (or short recording) of the actual running UI in any PR touching `client/src/**`, taken by driving the app (e.g. via the `run` skill) rather than relying on unit tests alone.

2. **Fix `server/vite.ts` killing the dev server on any browser console error.** Vite 8 has a built-in `forwardConsolePlugin` that relays browser `console.error`/`console.warn` calls and uncaught client exceptions to the server-side logger. The dev server's `customLogger.error` treated *every* logger.error call as fatal and called `process.exit(1)` — so any `console.error` in the browser tab, including unrelated/harmless ones, took down the whole dev server. This made it impossible to screenshot a UI change whenever an unrelated client-side fetch failed (e.g. the GitHub version-check failing in a network-sandboxed environment). Now only genuine server-side Vite errors (no `[console.*]`/`[Unhandled error]`/`[Unhandled rejection]` marker) exit the process; forwarded client messages are still logged but no longer fatal.

Verified the fix by starting `dev:test`, driving the app with a headless browser to trigger the same forwarded `console.error` that used to kill the server, and confirming the server stays up while the error is still visibly logged.

# Pull Request _Template_

## Description

Follow-up to #1049, resolving the CodeQL `js/path-injection` limitation flagged in [this status comment](https://github.com/Doezer/Questarr/pull/1049#issuecomment-5720004531) on that PR. Stacked on top of `library-side-extraction-v2` (not `main`) because the flagged code — `walkRelative()`/`gatherFiles()` in `ImportStrategies.ts` — only exists on that still-open branch; `main` has an older, independently-rewritten version of this file with no `walkRelative` at all.

CodeQL's default path-injection query flagged 3 alerts: reads (`fs.stat`/`fs.readdir`) on a source path that ultimately derives from downloader-reported paths. The existing `isSensitivePath()` blocklist isn't a shape CodeQL recognizes as a sanitizer — it narrows what's forbidden but never proves the value is confined to a known-safe space, which is what CodeQL's taint-tracking wants to see before it clears the flow.

This adds that containment proof:
- `PathMappingService.getConfiguredRoots()` exposes the local filesystem roots the admin has actually mapped downloader paths onto — `translatePath()` already confines its own output to one of these internally, so this just surfaces that same trusted set.
- `PCImportStrategy` now takes that root list and enforces containment at both `planImport()` and `executeImport()` — two independent entry points, since `confirmImport` can hand `executeImport` a source path directly without ever going through `planImport` first.
- `ImportManager.resolveArchive()` gets the same check, since it reads the source directly before either of those runs.
- With **no mappings configured**, the check is a deliberate no-op: `translatePath()` already trusts the local filesystem wholesale in that case (common for single-host setups where the downloader and app share a filesystem), so there's no meaningful root set to restrict against — this doesn't change behavior for that common configuration.

**Confirmed against CI:** since this PR's base branch isn't `main`, most workflows (including CodeQL) don't trigger automatically on PRs/pushes here — the repo's Actions are scoped to `main`/`release/*`. I manually dispatched `codeql.yml` and `ci.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` against this branch to get a real signal rather than guessing. Result: **the `CodeQL` check now reports "No new alerts in code changed by this pull request"** — the exact same check that failed identically with "3 new alerts including 3 high severity security vulnerabilities" across every one of the 5 commits I pushed to #1049 trying earlier, less-targeted guards (a function-call blocklist, then an inline regex test). The allowlist-containment shape here — a real trusted-root set, `path.relative()` + `startsWith("..")`/`isAbsolute()`, enforced at every entry point before any read — is what actually clears it. All other checks (build, tests, lint, SonarCloud, SCA, secrets-scan, dependency-review) are green too.

# Pull Request _Template_

## Description

Redo of #809, which was closed for being 612 commits stale — `main` had independently rewritten every file that PR touched (password-protected-archive support and CLI-exec-based extraction in `ArchiveService.ts`, `sortExtras` file categorization in `ImportManager.ts`/`ImportStrategies.ts`) since it was opened. This reimplements the same feature fresh on top of current `main`, threading it through that newer work instead of conflicting with it. See `memory/decisions.md` for the detailed account of what changed in the rebuild and why.

- Unpack archives at the destination instead of the downloader directory: move/copy relocate then extract in place; hardlink/symlink extract straight from the archive's original path to the final destination
- Detect archives already extracted by the downloader via content comparison against loose sibling files (name+size match), excluding them from transfer
- Fix `.partN.rar` and `.7z.NNN`/`.zip.NNN` sibling detection for multi-volume archives (stem derivation previously left the volume suffix attached, blocking later volumes from matching)
- Normalize cross-platform path separators when matching archive entries against loose files on disk
- Surface stranded move/copy extraction failures as an in-app notification (with recovery guidance) instead of failing silently
- Reorganize `sortExtras` categories in place after an archive unpacks (there's nothing to categorize before extraction happens, unlike a plain directory import)
- Add `ImportReviewModal` hints explaining hardlink/symlink volume requirements

**Archive listing** (`ArchiveService.listEntries`, used by the already-extracted check) always shells out to 7-Zip's `l -slt` mode, even for `.rar` — extraction still routes `.rar` to unrar, but 7-Zip's `-slt` output has a stable format regardless of archive type and has built-in read support for RAR (including RAR5), so a second parser for unrar's own column-aligned list commands wasn't needed. A listing failure degrades to "assume not already extracted" rather than failing the import — it's an optimization, never load-bearing for correctness.

**Known limitation carried over unchanged from the original design** (not new to this PR): `fs-extra`'s cross-device (`EXDEV`) move fallback is copy-then-remove, not atomic — a failure mid-copy can leave a partial file at the library destination. Flagged as future work.

## Description

pr.body:
## Description

Adds **Postgres as an opt-in database backend**. SQLite remains the default and stays completely zero-config — an existing install that sets only `SQLITE_DB_PATH`, or nothing at all, behaves exactly as before.

Motivation: self-hosters who already run a Postgres server currently have no way to point Questarr at it. Note this does not reverse the v1.1 move to SQLite — SQLite is still the default and the recommended path; Postgres is an alternative for people who specifically want it.

Existing SQLite users can bring their library across with `scripts/sqlite-to-pg.ts`.

### How it fits together

Drizzle has no single-schema-many-dialects mode, and 47 client files import from `shared/schema.ts`, so the type surface could not move. Instead:

- `shared/schema.ts` stays the single source of TypeScript types and Zod schemas.
- `shared/schema.pg.ts` is a **runtime-only** Postgres mirror.
- `server/db/tables.ts` resolves the right tables behind one documented cast.

Postgres columns use the most native type that preserves the **exact** TypeScript type, so application code is identical on both backends: `boolean`, `jsonb`, `double precision`, and `bigint` for byte counts. Timestamps deliberately stay epoch-milliseconds rather than `timestamptz`, because several queries compare them to `Date.now()` and `timestamptz` would reject an integer bind, forcing per-dialect branches through the storage layer. The app does no calendar arithmetic in SQL, and converting later is one `ALTER` with zero app-code change — documented in `docs/DATABASE.md`.

Two guards stop the parallel schemas from drifting, since the cast above depends on them:

- `shared/schema-parity.ts` — 38 compile-time assertions that all 19 tables infer identical row/insert shapes.
- `shared/__tests__/schema-parity.test.ts` — runtime assertions on SQL column names, nullability, defaults and primary keys, i.e. drift the type system cannot see.

**The guards have already proven themselves.** While this PR was open, `main` added an `allowInsecureLan` column to `indexers` and `downloaders`. Merging `main` in failed four compile-time assertions immediately, naming exactly which tables had diverged. Without that, the Postgres schema would have shipped silently missing two security-relevant columns, surfacing only at runtime on a real Postgres install.

The only genuinely per-dialect code is five transactional operations, behind `TransactionalOps`. The two drivers disagree about what a transaction *is* — better-sqlite3's callback is synchronous with `.all()`/`.run()`, node-postgres's is async with neither. Hand-rolling SQLite transactions so one async body could serve both was considered and rejected: `await` points between `BEGIN` and `COMMIT` yield to the microtask queue, so a concurrent request's continuation would run inside our transaction. Two of these exist precisely to close races (API-key cap, setup guard), so widening them to save ~150 lines is the wrong trade. The reasoning is recorded in the interface. The dialect-independent parts of `syncIndexers` live in `transactional-ops.shared.ts` so only the transaction mechanics are duplicated.

Dialect selection is by `DB_DIALECT` **only**, never inferred from `DATABASE_URL`. Questarr ran on Postgres before v1.1, so an install may still carry a stale `DATABASE_URL`; inferring would silently swap a live SQLite library for an empty or four-versions-stale database on upgrade. A stale `DATABASE_URL` now warns loudly and is ignored.

### Bugs found and fixed along the way

Six latent portability bugs surfaced. Several are worth fixing on their own merit:

1. **`count(*)`/`sum()` return a *string* on node-postgres** (10+1 sites typed `sql<number>`) — `count > 0` would silently be `"0" > 0` === `false`.
2. **32-bit overflow** — Postgres `integer` maxes at ~2.1 GB. Affects `file_size` (×2), `min_file_size`, and — found while transcribing — `disk_free_bytes`/`disk_total_bytes`, which overflow for any drive over 2.1 GB.
3. **`real()` precision loss** — drizzle `sqlite-core` `real` is 8-byte, Postgres `real` is 4-byte.
4. **`result.changes` is better-sqlite3-only** — Postgres reports `rowCount`; six delete sites would have reported "nothing deleted".
5. **`LIKE '%update%'` is case-insensitive on SQLite but not Postgres** — the release-type heuristic detected "Update" on one backend and silently missed it on the other. Scoping had wrongly cleared this block as portable; the new test suite caught it.
6. **`createApiKey` destructured a binding named `count`**, shadowing the imported helper and tripping its own TDZ. Caught before it shipped.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Documentation update

## Checklist:

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] If this PR adds a new actor/integration, external interface, or security-relevant change, I have updated docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/API.md, and/or docs/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md accordingly — added `docs/DATABASE.md`, plus notes in `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `README.md` and `.env.example`
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

### Verification

Post-merge with `main`: **193 test files / 2766 tests green**, typecheck clean, and lint clean under main's stricter `--max-warnings 0`. SonarCloud quality gate **passed**, with duplication on new code down to **1.2%** (from 3.8%) and 0 security hotspots.

- `server/__tests__/dialect-parity.test.ts` runs the same behavioural assertions against **both** backends via `describe.each`, with Postgres in-process through PGlite — no container, and no measurable change to suite runtime. Reverting the `LIKE` fix was confirmed to fail on Postgres while still passing on SQLite, so the suite has teeth.
- The generated Postgres baseline was executed against a real Postgres engine: every statement applies, a 9 GB `file_size` and an 8 TB `disk_total_bytes` round-trip, epoch-ms defaults populate, and `jsonb` round-trips structured data.
- `server/__tests__/sqlite-to-pg.test.ts` round-trips a populated library through the migration script and asserts on the values whose storage differs between dialects.
- SQLite migrations still apply cleanly from scratch (all 34, 19 tables).
- Emitted SQL was diffed before/after for every rewritten query in the dialect-neutral refactor — aggregate, date and cutoff queries are byte-identical.
- Connection factory exercised across all five configurations (default, stale `DATABASE_URL`, unknown dialect, missing `DATABASE_URL`, unreachable server).
- Both ESLint import guards negative-tested.

### Known gaps

- **No real-Postgres CI job.** The dialect suite runs Postgres in-process via PGlite, which is single-connection — pool exhaustion, lock contention and deadlock ordering are therefore untested. A job running the DB suites against a real `postgres:17-alpine` service container, on PRs touching `server/db/**`, `shared/schema*.ts` or `server/storage.ts`, is the obvious next step.
- **`docker-compose.postgres.yml` is validated as YAML, not by running it** — Docker was unavailable in the authoring environment.
- **Unrelated observation:** SonarCloud reports 0.0% coverage on new code because `sonar-project.properties` points at `coverage/lcov.info`, but the Sonar scan runs before `merge-test-reports` produces it (coverage goes to Codecov instead). This is pre-existing and affects every PR; left alone rather than widening this one.

### Follow-up

`.claude/skills/db-dialect-parity/SKILL.md` was added so future sessions know a DB-impacting change has to satisfy both dialects, with the type-mapping table and the traps above.

pr.body:
## Description

Reported bug: a SABnzbd download failed repair ("Repair failed, not enough repair blocks") and was visible in SABnzbd's History tab, but Questarr logged:

```
Download not found in downloader - assuming completion. This could indicate the download was manually removed.
```
and silently marked the game as "owned" with nothing actually downloaded.

### Root cause

`server/downloaders/sabnzbd.ts`'s history lookup (`getFromHistory`) had two independent gaps that could each make a real, non-archived history entry invisible:

1. **Archive bucket**: SABnzbd auto-archives finished jobs out of its "active" history once the configured history retention (job count/age) is exceeded. The `mode=history` API only ever searches one bucket per request — active (`archive IS NULL`) or archived (`archive = 1`) — and `nzo_ids` filtering does not search across both. We never passed `archive=1`.
2. **Confirmed against the actual failing case** (the user supplied SABnzbd's real history payload for this download — `"archive": false`): `nzo_ids` filtering returned nothing even though the job was genuinely present and non-archived, and our unfiltered full-scan fallback *also* missed it, because omitting `limit` makes SABnzbd's API silently fall back to the user's configured `history_limit` (often well under 1000) rather than returning everything — so a job older than that cap was invisible to the fallback scan too.

### Fix

`getFromHistory`/`getHistoryDownloadDir` now share a `fetchHistorySlot()` helper that:
- Checks both the active and archived history buckets.
- Falls back to an unfiltered scan with an **explicit large `limit`** (1000 — confirmed sufficient against the reporter's real data) instead of an omitted/default-capped one.

With this, the failed download is now correctly read back with its real SABnzbd status (`Failed` → `error`, with `fail_message` as the error), instead of falling through to the "not found" fallback. The `fail_message` ("Repair failed, not enough repair blocks (15 short)") already flows through `cron.ts` into the game's stored `errorMessage`, which `GameDetailsModal` already surfaces to the user — so no separate UI change was needed for that part.

As a secondary safety net, `server/cron.ts`'s handling of a download that genuinely can't be found anywhere (e.g. actually removed by the user) was also changed to mark it `failed` and reset the game to `wanted` instead of assuming success, using the same active-sibling-status logic already used elsewhere in the file, and independent in-app/Apprise notification gating.

## Why

`docs/PRD.md` and `GOAL-product.md` already state single-user is the supported configuration ("No multi-tenant isolation in scope"), but `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md` still described things in multi-user-*eventual* terms:
- A `cron.ts` TODO reference framed as "once multi-user socket auth is wired up"
- `THREAT_MODEL.md` calling Questarr a "self-hosted, multi-user app" and treating a cross-account Socket.io broadcast as something to fix "if multi-user usage grows"

That inconsistency is exactly what led to #1039 (closed): a same-instance, cross-account data-isolation finding in `library-scanner.ts` got raised and initially treated as if it might be release-blocking, when under Questarr's actual deployment model (one trusted operator per instance) it isn't.

## Changes

- **`THREAT_MODEL.md`** — reworded the two residual-risk rows (Socket.io broadcast, flat trust model) that described things in multi-user-eventual terms, cross-referencing the new `ARCHITECTURE.md` §9 instead of repeating (and contradicting) the rationale.

pr.body:
## Problem

`storage.getGameByIgdbId()` looks up a game across **every user's library**, not just the caller's — it's a global lookup by `igdbId` only. Two call sites in `server/library-scanner.ts` used its result directly to decide whether to reuse (and mutate) an existing game row, without ever checking `game.userId`:

- `matchUnmatchedFolder()` — the manual "resolve this unmatched folder to an IGDB game" flow (`POST /api/library/scan/unmatched/match`)
- `recordMatchedCandidate()` — the scanner's auto-match path, run during every library scan

**Impact:** an authenticated user could pick any `igdbId` already owned by a *different* user (e.g. by trying common titles, or observing `GET /api/library/scan/unmatched`, which is intentionally global scanner state) and have the scanner:
- flip that other user's game status to `"owned"`,
- overwrite its `libraryPath` with a path from the attacker's own scan, and
- attach the attacker's own scanned files to a game they don't own.

This is CWE-862 (Missing Authorization). Root folders themselves are legitimately global/shared server config (confirmed via `GET /api/root-folders`, also unauthenticated-by-user), so the scanner's shared visibility is by design — the bug is specifically the missing ownership check before *mutating* a game row.

## Fix

Both call sites now discard a `getGameByIgdbId()` hit that isn't owned by the calling user and fall through to creating a new game for that user instead — mirroring the exact `existing && existing.userId === userId` pattern already used for the same kind of igdbId-reuse check elsewhere in `server/routes.ts` (the download-attach and bulk-import flows).

```ts
let game = await storage.getGameByIgdbId(igdbId);
if (game && game.userId !== userId) {
  game = undefined; // not ours — treat as not found, create a new row instead
}
if (!game) {
  game = await storage.addGame(igdbToInsertGame(igdb, userId));
  ...
```

No schema or storage-layer changes — this is a minimal, targeted fix at the two vulnerable call sites.

## Tests

Added two regression tests to `server/__tests__/library-scanner.test.ts`:
- `matchUnmatchedFolder creates a new game instead of mutating another user's game with the same igdbId`
- `auto-match during a scan creates a new game instead of mutating another user's game`

Verified both fail against the pre-fix code (confirmed via a local revert) and pass with the fix. Also updated two pre-existing fixtures that were missing `userId` on their mocked game objects, since that field is now actually read.

**Full validation:**
- `npm run check` (tsc) — clean
- `npm run lint` (eslint) — clean
- `npx vitest run` — 2637 passed, 7 skipped (188 files)

## Context

Found during an independent code review of #1015, which touches an unrelated part of the codebase (qBittorrent download tracking) — this vulnerability is in pre-existing scanner code, untouched by that PR, so it's split out here rather than folded into it.

pr.body:
## Summary

This PR documents the duplication between #1015 and #1034, which address the same underlying problem: qBittorrent v5+ async pending responses leave downloads untracked in Questarr.

## Analysis

Both PRs fix the issue where qBittorrent v5+ returns `pending_count: 1` with an empty `added_torrent_ids` list during asynchronous torrent additions, causing the download to proceed invisibly in qBittorrent while remaining "wanted" in Questarr.

### Approach Comparison

| Aspect | #1015 | #1034 |
|--------|-------|-------|
| **Strategy** | Track from start with correlation tag, resolve hash later | Sync untracked downloads periodically |
| **Scope** | qBittorrent-specific | All downloaders |
| **Tracking** | Immediate (on route response) | Delayed (on cron run) |
| **CPU Cost** | Low (resolve tagged items only) | Higher (scan all games/downloads) |
| **Determinism** | High (only processes tagged downloads) | Medium (inferred from title match) |
| **Schema Changes** | Yes (correlation tag, hash update) | No |

### Key Trade-offs

**#1015 Pros:**
- Immediate tracking → game status updates instantly
- Deterministic: only processes downloads Questarr created
- Lower overhead: resolves only tagged items
- qBittorrent-appropriate for a qBittorrent-specific problem

**#1015 Cons:**
- Requires schema changes and `updateGameDownloadHash()` method
- qBittorrent-specific

**#1034 Pros:**
- Downloader-agnostic, works with any client
- Resilient to any async race condition
- No schema changes needed
- Reuses existing `releaseMatchesGame()` logic

**#1034 Cons:**
- Runs every 60s (high frequency overhead)
- Best-effort matching (could have false positives/negatives)
- Detects problem after the fact, not preventing it upfront

## Recommendation

**#1015 should be the primary fix** because it's immediate, deterministic, and appropriate for a qBittorrent-specific problem.

**#1034 could be a complementary safety net** if needed later as a generic recovery mechanism (with reduced frequency to minimize overhead).

## Next Steps

1. Review both PRs thoroughly to understand implementation details
2. Clarify with authors whether #995 and #885 are truly the same root cause
3. Choose implementation path (see DUPLICATION_ANALYSIS.md for three options)
4. Consolidate into a single, cohesive fix

See `DUPLICATION_ANALYSIS.md` for the full detailed analysis.

pr.body:
## Problem

qBittorrent v5 can reply to `torrents/add` with `pending_count: 1` and an empty `added_torrent_ids` list while the .torrent/magnet is still being processed. Questarr currently polls for the hash for a short moment and then gives up, so the completed torrent is never tracked and the game stays "wanted".

This could be the root cause behind downloads that show up in qBittorrent but remain "wanted" in Questarr (see #885).

## Solution

Add a new `syncUntrackedDownloads()` cron task that runs after every download-status check (every 60 s):

1. Loads all wanted games grouped by user.
2. Fetches active downloads from every enabled downloader.
3. Filters out hashes already present in `game_downloads`.
4. Matches each remaining torrent name to a wanted game title with the existing `releaseMatchesGame()` helper.
5. Skips the match if the game already has an active sibling download.
6. Inserts a new `game_downloads` row in `downloading` status and updates the game status so the normal import pipeline takes over.

## Scope

- Targets the qBittorrent async-add race, but works for any downloader whose `getAllDownloads()` returns torrents that Questarr has not yet recorded.
- Does not change the existing `checkDownloadStatus()` flow.

## Testing

- Verified locally by temporarily deleting a tracked Corsair Cove row, setting the game back to `wanted`, and confirming the cron job re-linked the untracked qBittorrent torrent.
- The new function is exported and can be covered by unit tests with mocked storage and downloader manager.

Fixes #885

## Description

**Depends on #803** — this branches off `fix-7zip-permission-issue` because the encrypted-archive path only exists once the unrar/7-Zip `ArchiveService` from that PR is in place. This should merge after #803, or be rebased onto `main` once #803 lands.

Today, an encrypted RAR/7z/zip fails extraction against `unrar`'s `-p-` (refuse to prompt) or 7-Zip's default no-password behavior, gets retried twice more for no benefit (a password failure is deterministic — retrying can't fix it), and finally surfaces as a generic **"the archive is corrupt or incomplete — re-download the release"** error. That message is actively wrong: the archive is fine, it's just encrypted, and there was no way to supply a password anywhere in the app.

This PR adds that missing path end-to-end:

- **`ArchiveService`**: `extract()`/`testArchive()` take an optional `password`, forwarded to unrar/7-Zip as `-p<password>` instead of `-p-` / no flag. A password-related failure (detected via both tools' consistent use of the word "password" in their error output) now throws `ArchivePasswordRequiredError` immediately, skipping the pointless retry loop, with a message that distinguishes "this archive needs a password" from "the password you gave was wrong."
- **`ImportManager`**: threads the password through `processImport`, `confirmImport`, and `extractIfArchive`. Tags the `manual_review_required` `errorMessage` with an `ARCHIVE_PASSWORD_REQUIRED:` marker prefix so the API layer can derive a `passwordRequired` flag — no schema migration needed, since `game_downloads.error_message` already exists.
- **`routes/import.ts`**: `GET /pending` strips the marker and exposes `passwordRequired: boolean`; `POST /:id/confirm` accepts an optional `password` field and returns `400 { passwordRequired: true }` if the given password is rejected, distinct from a generic failure.
- **`ImportReviewModal`**: when `passwordRequired` is set, shows a "Password Required" header and a required password field, pre-enables and locks the Unpack Archive toggle, and surfaces "Incorrect Password" distinctly from "Import Failed" if a retry password is wrong.

The archive stays in the existing `manual_review_required` → Pending Manual Imports flow (per the linked discussion) — this reuses the existing review/confirm UI rather than adding a new status or endpoint.

pr.body:
## Description

CodeQL's "Default setup" (configured at the repo-settings level, not in a workflow file) autodetects languages from repo contents, and it has been misdetecting C# for this repo — which has zero C# code. Every run of `Analyze (csharp)` fails autobuild with `No source files found`, showing up as a red CodeQL check on every PR (including #803) with no actual signal behind it.

This replaces that default, autodetected setup with an explicit **advanced-setup** workflow (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`) that scans only the languages actually present: `javascript-typescript` and `actions`, both using `build-mode: none` since neither needs a compiled build step. It follows this repo's existing conventions — same `harden-runner` pinning, same `actions/checkout` + `persist-credentials: false` pattern, same `github/codeql-action` SHA already pinned elsewhere in the repo (`sast.yml`, `scorecard.yml`, `vulnerability-scan.yml`).

**Manual follow-up required after merge:** GitHub refuses to run an advanced CodeQL workflow while the repo's "Default" code-scanning setup is still enabled — it will reject this workflow's runs with a conflict error until then. A repo admin needs to go to **Settings → Code security and analysis → Code scanning → CodeQL analysis → Edit → Switch to advanced** (or just disable Default), which is a settings-only change no PR can make.

Added

Updates `undici` from 8.10.0 to 8.10.2
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v8.10.2

⚠️ Security fixes

High severity

  • GHSA-vp8m-p9jh-q5pm: cache and deduplication interceptors could use caller-controlled request metadata instead of the authoritative dispatcher origin, enabling cross-origin cache poisoning and data disclosure. Undici now derives interceptor identities from the dispatcher origin and bypasses origin-dependent interceptors when no authoritative origin exists. Fixed by caf6194d.
  • GHSA-w293-vg96-wgc3: BalancedPool could drop function-valued connection options while cloning its configuration, including custom TLS certificate validation callbacks. Undici now preserves connect and legacy tls options when creating upstreams. Fixed by 8f5868fb.
  • GHSA-rfgv-xxqx-mfg5: a WebSocket server could select a subprotocol when none was requested, causing an uncaught TypeError that could terminate the process. Undici now rejects the handshake with protocol error 1002. Fixed by 66e12816.

Medium severity

  • GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v: a malformed permessage-deflate payload exceeding the configured decompression limit could emit an unhandled zlib error and terminate the process. Undici now destroys the inflater after reaching the limit. Fixed by 4411a238.
  • GHSA-rx4f-c7p8-82vq: an unclean WebSocketStream close could create an unobserved rejected promise when its writable stream was locked, potentially terminating the process. Undici now propagates the failure through the retained writable stream controller. Fixed by 662d0ea6.
  • GHSA-2jfj-6hjv-fm6j: shared caches could store and replay responses containing Set-Cookie, disclosing one user's cookies to another caller. Undici now excludes these responses from shared caches, including existing entries and revalidation paths. Fixed by cb75bbb3.
  • GHSA-3xpg-4rpp-hhhm: the decompression interceptor did not bound decoded output, allowing compressed responses to consume excessive memory. Undici now limits every decompression stage to 64 MiB by default and supports a configurable maxSize. Fixed by 7aac7f12.
  • GHSA-pmjh-fq2x-6v4x: a terminal retry failure after response headers were exposed could orphan the original response body, causing consumers to hang indefinitely. Undici now propagates the terminal error to the exposed body. Fixed by e905b5b8.

Low severity

  • GHSA-8436-99hf-9mmv: cache interceptors could store and replay responses to unsafe HTTP methods such as POST or DELETE. Undici now restricts cache reads and writes to safe methods while preserving invalidation by successful unsafe requests. Fixed by 2be07bf9.
  • GHSA-2gqq-gqf2-x968: the dump interceptor could treat an oversized chunked response as successfully truncated when no Content-Length was present. Undici now enforces maxSize against received bytes and aborts oversized responses. Fixed by 6d583124.
  • GHSA-r53p-7pc4-xj5r: the retry interceptor could concatenate a resumed response with inconsistent framing into downstream output, enabling response splitting or corruption. Undici now validates Content-Range against the original response framing before resuming. Fixed by 0160a719.

Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API

pr.body:
Newznab/Torznab API keys were unconditionally appended to request URLs, meaning any HTTP-configured indexer transmitted credentials in clear text across every request path.

## Policy
API keys are **never sent over HTTP** unless the user explicitly enables a per-indexer `allowInsecureLan` flag. HTTPS indexers are unaffected.

## Changes

### Schema & persistence
- New `allow_insecure_lan` boolean column on `indexers` (default `false`), migration `0033_indexer_allow_insecure_lan.sql`

### Policy enforcement
- `server/indexer-caps.ts`: adds `indexerAllowsApiKey(indexer)` — `true` when scheme is `https:` or `allowInsecureLan === true`; `buildCapsUrlCandidates` now conditions `apikey` on this helper
- `server/newznab.ts`: policy applied to `search`, `testConnection`, `fetchServerInfo`
- `server/torznab.ts`: policy applied to `buildSearchUrl`, `fetchServerInfo`, and Prowlarr proxy URL construction

```ts
// server/indexer-caps.ts
export function indexerAllowsApiKey(indexer: Pick<Indexer, "url" | "allowInsecureLan">): boolean {
  const { protocol } = new URL(indexer.url);
  if (protocol === "https:") return true;
  return indexer.allowInsecureLan === true;
}
```

### UI
- `allowInsecureLan` checkbox added to the indexer form with an inline security warning (mirrors the `allowSelfSignedCertificate` pattern on downloaders)

### Tests
- Existing HTTP-based tests updated: those that legitimately test API-key-present behavior now use `allowInsecureLan: true`
- 10 new policy tests cover all three cases (HTTP without opt-in → no key, HTTP with opt-in → key, HTTPS → key) for both Newznab and Torznab, including the Prowlarr proxy URL path

pr.body:
Imports silently fail for qBittorrent users with no error message or notification, primarily affecting Nintendo Switch NSP files. Three distinct failure paths all ended with the download quietly entering `manual_review_required` state with no user-visible signal.

## Changes

### `shared/title-utils.ts` — NSP/XCI platform detection
`nsp` and `xci` were not recognized as Switch platform indicators. Release names like `"Game Title NSP"` never matched the Switch platform pattern, meaning platform folder resolution and platform filters relied entirely on the IGDB game record having the correct platform attached.

### `server/cron.ts` — Notification when download path can't be resolved
When post-processing is enabled but the download client returns no `downloadDir`, the download was placed in `manual_review_required` with `shouldSendCompletionNotification = false` — no user-visible signal. ## Description

Closes #994.

Adds a **Hidden Platforms** setting so users can remove systems they don't care about from the Library platform filter dropdown. The Library filter previously listed every unique platform across the whole library, which is cluttered for anyone who only collects 2–3 systems.

The setting is stored as a new `hidden_platforms` JSON text array on `user_settings` (same shape as `preferred_release_groups`), edited from **Settings → Appearance**.

A platform hidden here is hidden from the *filter dropdown only* — games on that platform are still shown in the Library, so this cannot silently make a user's collection disappear.

### Deliberate design decision

I kept a dedicated `hiddenPlatforms` field rather than driving the dropdown off the existing `importPlatformIds`. They look similar but are not interchangeable:

- the Library dropdown is built from IGDB platform **names** in `games.platforms`
- the import filter stores IGDB platform **ids** and gates *imports*

Reusing one for the other would either gate imports as a side effect of hiding a filter chip, or require a lossy name↔id translation at render time. Keeping them separate is the smaller, safer change.

### Test plan

New/updated tests, all passing locally:

- `client/__tests__/Library.platform-filter.test.tsx` — reproduces the issue (fails before the change), asserts hidden platforms drop out of the dropdown and others remain
- `client/__tests__/HiddenPlatformsSettings.test.tsx` — settings UI behaviour
- `client/__tests__/HiddenPlatformsRace.test.tsx` — regression for a load-order race: if `/api/igdb/platforms` resolves before `/api/settings`, the picker must still pre-check saved platforms
- `client/__tests__/Library.hidden-platforms-guard.test.tsx` — regression for a malformed stored value
- `shared/__tests__/schema.test.ts` — payload validation

Verification performed:

- `npx vitest run` on the touched suites — 50/50 pass, stable over repeated runs
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx eslint` on all touched files — clean
- CI on the fork commit: all checks green (test matrix, both Node builds, semgrep, sca-scan, secrets-scan, dependency-review, docker-build)

### Post-review fixes

An independent review of the first commit caught two real defects, both fixed in the second commit:

1. `updateUserSettingsSchema` accepted **any** value for the JSON array columns — `"oops"`, `42`, `{a:1}` and `["ok", 5]` all passed `safeParse`, and `PATCH /api/settings` persists the request body verbatim, so a malformed payload was stored as-is. Validation now rejects non-arrays and wrong element types for `importPlatformIds`, `hiddenPlatforms`, and `ignoredExtensions` — all three shared the bug, so fixing only the new field would have left the others open.

## Problem
When qBittorrent v5+ accepts a URL add asynchronously (pending_count: 1, added_torrent_ids: []), the hash isn't immediately known. The game_downloads tracking record was only created when the hash was present, so async downloads were silently dropped and never tracked.

Fixes Doezer/Questarr#995

## Fix
- Return correlationTag from qBittorrent async adds so the route can create the tracking record upfront with the tag as a temporary downloadHash
- Cron resolves the correlation tag to the real hash via qBittorrent's tag API before matching downloads
- Added findTorrentByTag() to the downloader interface (no-op for non-qBittorrent)
- Added updateGameDownloadHash() to storage (both MemStorage and DatabaseStorage)

## Tests
New coverage (22 tests, all passing locally — 63/63 across the 5 touched files):

| File | Tests |
|------|-------|
| cron_async_download_resolution.test.ts (new) | 4 — tag→hash resolution, unresolved skip, non-async skip, resolve+complete |
| downloaders_find_by_tag.test.ts (new) | 7 — no-op for all 6 non-qBittorrent downloaders |
| downloaders_qbittorrent_regression.test.ts | 5 — findTorrentByTag success/not-found/no-hash/error/multi-match |
| api_routes_async_download.test.ts | 1 (added) — route prefers real id over correlationTag |
| database_storage_extended.test.ts | 3 — updateGameDownloadHash tag→real, skips real hash, no-op missing |

### Reproduction test for this exact issue
`server/__tests__/api_routes_async_download.test.ts` → **"creates a game_downloads record when downloader returns a correlationTag (async, no hash)"**

This is the exact #995 scenario end-to-end at the route level:
- Mocks `DownloaderManager.addDownloadWithFallback` to return `{ success: true, correlationTag: "questarr-add-abc123", downloaderId: "d-1", ... }` with **no `id`** — i.e. what qBittorrent v5+ returns for an async add (`pending_count: 1`, `added_torrent_ids: []`)

pr.body:
## Problem

Large .rar files take **longer than 60s** to extract — and during that window, the download **restarts from scratch** (the extraction directory's file grows, then starts small again).

## Root cause (reproduced)

1. When a download finishes, cron's `checkDownloadStatus()` calls `processImport()`, which sets the DB row to `"unpacking"` and starts extracting via 7zip/unrar
2. `checkDownloadStatus()` runs **every 60s** (`DOWNLOAD_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS = 60 * 1000`), and `setInterval` does **not** wait for the previous run to finish
3. `getDownloadingGameDownloads()` only excludes *terminal* statuses — `"unpacking"` (and `"completed_pending_import"`) are still returned
4. So on the next 60s tick, the still-extracting row is picked up again, the remote download still reports `completed`, and cron calls `processImport()` a **second time** → a second `extractFull` writes into the same `_extracted` directory, clobbering the first extraction

That is exactly the observed symptom: files grow, then "start small again" at ~60s.

## Fix

Skip rows whose status is `"unpacking"` or `"completed_pending_import"` in `checkDownloadStatus()` — an import already in flight is left alone until the current run finishes or fails (failures route to `manual_review_required`, where they remain re-actionable).

## Test

- Reproduction test added: `cron re-triggers processImport for an unpacking download` — **failed before the fix** (demonstrating `processImport` was called again), **passes after**

All 9 cron tests pass. TypeScript compiles clean.

---

Note: this will be most useful alongside #803 — once the 7zip bin permissions fix merges, real extraction in Docker runs for large .rar files, which is exactly the long-running case this guard protects from being double-triggered into the same directory.

Feel free to edit this PR with your agent.

## Summary
- `ArchiveService.extract()` now has a hard 60-second timeout — if the 7zip/unrar process hangs longer than that, the process group is SIGKILL'd and the extraction restarts
- Configurable via `{ timeoutMs?, maxRetries? }` options (defaults: 60s, 1 retry)
- Only timeouts trigger retries; real errors fail immediately

## Why
If unrar hangs on a corrupt or heavily compressed .rar, the extraction would block forever — the import pipeline stalls and never recovers.

## How
- New `extract()` wraps `extractOnce()` in a retry loop
- `extractOnce()` sets a `setTimeout` — on fire, calls `killExtraction()` which does `process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL")` (kills the whole process group including unrar) with a `child.kill("SIGKILL")` fallback
- `ExtractionTimeoutError` distinguishes timeouts from fatal errors

## Test coverage
- kills process and restarts on timeout
- throws after all retries exhausted
- no restart when extraction completes before timeout
- default 60s/1-retry behavior

All 17 archive service tests pass. TypeScript compiles clean.

pr.body:
## Description

Fixes a real usability bug in the Playnite extension reported as "it only accepts local IP", plus a related product decision from Doezer to relax the connect-time HTTP policy.

**Root cause of the "only local IP" symptom:** `Invoke-QuestarrApi` set `MaximumRedirection = 0` and refused *any* HTTP redirect outright. Any reverse proxy that redirects at all — enforcing `https://`, normalizing a trailing slash, `apex -> www` — made every request fail. A bare local `IP:port` never has a proxy in front of it to redirect, so it "just worked" while every realistic remote/proxied deployment didn't. From the outside that looks exactly like "only local IPs are accepted."

**Fix:** replaced the `Invoke-RestMethod` + `MaximumRedirection = 0` approach (which on Windows PowerShell 5.1 throws with no `Response` attached at all, so there's no way to read the redirect's `Location` header) with a raw `HttpWebRequest` (`AllowAutoRedirect = $false`), which gives a real `WebException` carrying the 3xx response. A same-host redirect is now followed once, with the API key reattached by hand; a redirect to any other host is still refused outright — that's the actual threat the original restriction existed to close (the key silently following a redirect to an untrusted host).

**Also, per explicit direction:** `Invoke-QuestarrConnect` no longer hard-refuses a plain `http://` address outside the caller's own local network. It's the operator's own server, and the extension's job is to make sure they know what they're choosing, not to choose for them. Both the local and non-local cases now go through one warn-and-confirm dialog, worded more strongly for a non-local address (the traffic can cross the open internet in cleartext) — but never an outright block.

Updated the extension's README and the `docs/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md` risk register entry to match both behavior changes.

pr.body:
## Description

Fixes #812 (regression reported on v1.4.2 with Prowlarr `2.5.2.5491`).

Prowlarr builds its `/{id}/download` proxy links from the address the request arrived on, so a Questarr container querying `http://prowlarr:9696` can get those links back on the container IP (`http://172.19.0.8:9696`).

`TorznabClient.isSameProwlarrHost` only accepted an exact hostname match or a `localhost` ↔ `127.0.0.1` pair (the #647 fix), so the service-name ↔ container-IP form fell through to the wrapping branch. The already-proxied URL was then base64-encoded into a new `link` parameter, burying Prowlarr's own token one level too deep:

```
http://prowlarr:9696/39/download?file=...&link=base64(http://172.19.0.8:9696/39/download?...&link=<real token>)&apikey=[redacted]
```

Prowlarr answers `BadRequestException: Failed to normalize provided link`, and every download fails with a 500.

### Change

A returned link counts as already proxied when **the link itself** names a loopback or private address (`localhost`, or an IP literal in loopback/RFC1918/ULA/link-local space) — no public indexer hands back a download link on one, so it can only be the Prowlarr we just queried. Scheme and port may legitimately differ there, since a reverse proxy terminating TLS on 443 fronts a container answering HTTP on 9696. Any other host has to match the configured origin exactly.

The signal deliberately does **not** come from the configured host: with Prowlarr addressed by container IP (the workaround #812 reporters are using), a public link mimicking the proxy path would otherwise be treated as already proxied and reach the download client without the API key. That case is covered by a regression test.

Supporting fixes, both in the same normalization gap:

- **Port.** Assigning `URL.host` without a port leaves the previous port in place, which kept Prowlarr's internal `:9696` on a reverse-proxied configured URL. The port is now set explicitly.
- **Scheme.** The outer rewrite guard compared hosts, so a link differing only by scheme was skipped entirely — Prowlarr behind TLS termination reflects `http://`, and a configured `https://` endpoint got an `http://` link that need not be reachable. It compares origins now.

`isPrivateNetworkAddress` lives in `server/ssrf.ts`, defined as the negation of the existing `isSafeIp` with private access disallowed, so the address ranges have one home rather than two.

Links that mimic the proxy path on a public host, and proxy-shaped links carrying a different indexer id, are still wrapped as before.

No dependency changes.

pr.body:
## Description

The Docker build on [#970](https://github.com/Doezer/Questarr/pull/970) failed with:

```
ERROR: failed to build: failed to solve: process "/bin/sh -c apk add --no-cache su-exec shadow python3 py3-pip && ..." did not complete successfully: exit code: 127
```

Exit code 127 is "command not found" — `apk` did not exist in the base image.

**Root cause:** both `FROM` lines in the `Dockerfile` referenced the base image by digest only, with the intended tag left in a comment:

```dockerfile
# node:26-alpine
FROM node@sha256:aadf416... AS base
```

Dependabot's docker updater cannot read that comment. With no tag on the reference, it resolves digest updates against `node:latest`, so #970 proposed the digest for the Debian variant instead of the Alpine one. Verified against the Docker Hub registry API:

| digest | `org.opencontainers.image.base.name` |
| --- | --- |
| `aadf416` (current, on `main`) | `alpine:3.24` |
| `f5d1cc4` (proposed by #970) | `buildpack-deps:trixie` |

On a Debian-based image there is no `apk`, hence the 127. The same would have hit the `base` stage's `apk add --no-cache g++ make python3`.

**Fix:** pin the tag explicitly alongside the digest so Dependabot tracks `26-alpine`:

```dockerfile
FROM node:26-alpine@sha256:aadf416... AS base
```

The digest itself is unchanged. Docker resolves a `tag@digest` reference by digest and ignores the tag, so the image this builds is identical to what `main` builds today — the change only affects which tag Dependabot resolves future digest bumps against.

pr.body:
## Description

The `/play` easter egg's facility had no walls of its own — the map's outer ring did that job, so a run began already indoors, with nothing to enter through. This gives the building a real perimeter and puts the player *outside* it, on an approach they have to cross to reach the one way in.

**Level generation**

- The grid interior is split into an **apron** and a **walled facility**. The apron is carved *out of* the span rather than added to it, so the two always tile the grid exactly; on a grid too small for the configured approach the apron gives way instead of running off the edge and stranding the spawn outside the world.
- The facility's perimeter is now listed wall like any partition, with exactly one cell missing: the gate. Only the grid's outer ring stays implicit.
- The gate is chosen *after* the rooms are known, from positions whose inner neighbour is open room floor (a partition can meet the perimeter anywhere along that face, and a gate opening onto the end of one would lead into solid wall). Among those, the best-connected room wins, so entering never lands in a stranded part of the room graph.
- Spawn moves to the far edge of the apron, straight out from the gate, so the run opens with the whole approach and the way in already lined up.

**A connectivity bug this surfaced**

BSP doors are now chosen after every cut instead of during each one. Choosing the door during a split and sealing it later when a perpendicular cut spoiled it silently dropped that split's edge from the room graph — seed 10 came out with 5 rooms and 2 doors, no route to lock, and so no keycard at all. Picking afterwards, from the cells with a room on either side, means every cut keeps its edge and the graph is a tree again. Verified as `doors === rooms - 1` across 500 seeds.

**Engine**

- The gate joins the existing door list, so its collider, its proximity trigger, and its blocking of paths and sight lines are the machinery the interior doors already use — one implementation of "a door is shut" for the pathfinder, the collision test and the sight lines to agree on. What is its own is the geometry: a ribbed cog leaf in a dressed stone portal, turning about the passage axis as it retracts.
- The approach is lit by lamps strung back from the gate, added to the **same list the stealth math reads**, so crossing the open ground genuinely costs cover rather than being a free hide.
- The apron is laid as square tiles rather than one stretched plane (it is a long thin band; a plane that shape smears the flagstone pattern along its length), and the facility shell is tinted apart from its partitions.
- A first objective line — "cross the approach and get through the gate" — latched the first time the player is inside.

Three rendering issues were found by looking at the result rather than assuming it: the status emissive flooded the whole leaf flat teal, `metalness: 0.85` with no environment map rendered it black, and deep jambs tunnelled the view so the wheel showed as a vertical slot. All three are fixed, with the reasoning recorded at each site.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)

- [x] If this PR adds a new actor/integration, external interface, or security-relevant change, I have updated docs/ — n/a, no external interface or security surface is touched
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

## Verification

- `npm run check`, `npm run lint`, `prettier --check` — clean
- `npm run test:run` — 2311 passed, 7 skipped
- New gate coverage in `level.test.ts`: spawn is on the apron; the gate is the **only** opening in the perimeter; it opens from apron to room floor; and **sealing it strands the terminal** — the property that makes the approach mean anything. Mutation-tested by punching a second hole in the perimeter, which fails 5 tests including all three of those.
- A 300-seed invariant harness over the generator: 0 failures, with all four approach sides represented.
- Production build driven in a real browser (Chromium/SwiftShader) across three seeds, close and zoomed out, with no console or page errors.

Updates `axios` from 1.19.0 to 1.20.0
Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.20.0 — August 19, 2026

This release hardens runtime option handling, adds RFC 9110 status-code aliases, fixes Node.js and XHR reliability issues, and refreshes project tooling and documentation.

⚠️ Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • HTTP Status Naming: Added ContentTooLarge (413) and UnprocessableContent (422), while retaining PayloadTooLarge and UnprocessableEntity as backward-compatible deprecated aliases. (#11082)

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Runtime Option Handling: Hardened behavioral configuration reads against shared and foreign prototype pollution and normalized unsafe interceptor replacement objects. This also clarifies Fetch redirect and custom implementation behavior, HTTP/2 DNS and proxy handling, CIDR-based NO_PROXY matching, and malformed data URI rejection; see the PR for documented compatibility effects. (#11141)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Interceptor Lifecycle: Prevented unbounded handler-array growth by trimming trailing ejected interceptors without changing iteration semantics, and kept interceptor operations safe when the public handlers field is nullish. (#11087, #11118)
  • Request Error Preservation: Prevented custom Error.prepareStackTrace implementations that return non-string values from replacing the original request failure with an unrelated TypeError. (#11109)
  • XHR Reliability: Navigation-canceled requests now reject with ECONNABORTED instead of resolving with status 0, while successful downloads flush their final progress callback during the live loadend dispatch. (#11094, #11121)
  • Node.js Socket Memory: Removed request-context retention from per-socket error listeners, preventing completed response data from being pinned for the lifetime of pooled keep-alive sockets. (#11091)
  • Core Methods and HTTP Errors: Prevented structural method-header buckets from leaking into outgoing headers, standardized invalid DNS lookup and httpVersion failures as AxiosError.ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE, and corrected the timeoutErrorMessage merge strategy. (#11096)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Dependencies: Updated fast-uri, postcss, js-yaml, mocha, development-tooling groups, and GitHub Actions dependencies. (#11092, #11098, #11099, #11106, #11107, #11122, #11123, #11126, #11127, #11133, #11140, #11143, #11144)

[5.4.1] - 2026-08-26

Updates `react-hook-form` from 7.86.0 to 7.87.0
Release notes

Sourced from react-hook-form's releases.

Version 7.87.0

✨ Features

  • Add shouldTouch option to trigger() ([#13671](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13671))

    setValue already supported shouldTouch; trigger() now does too. This allows you to mark field(s) as touched after manual or programmatic validation, such as validate-on-mount or multi-step form navigation, without needing a setValue workaround:

    // Mark a single field as touched after validating it
await trigger('firstName', { shouldTouch: true });

    // Mark every mounted field as touched after validating the whole form
await trigger(undefined, { shouldTouch: true });

  • Add OpaqueTypes registry for opaque leaf types ([#13676](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13676))

    Recursive type helpers (Path, DeepPartial, DeepRequired, FieldErrorsImpl, etc.) previously stopped only at Primitive | BrowserNativeObject. As a result, rich third-party value types such as Dayjs and Decimal could be recursively traversed member-by-member, potentially causing TypeScript to report "Excessive complexity" diagnostics on large form types.

    You can now register a type as an opaque leaf via declaration merging:

    import type { Dayjs } from 'dayjs';

    declare module 'react-hook-form' {
interface OpaqueTypes {
dayjs: Dayjs;
}
}

    While the registry is empty, types remain identical to the existing behavior. This is purely opt-in.

🐞 Fixes

  • Fix inconsistent behavior among useController().field.onChange()-like APIs. ([#13673](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13673))
  • Fix Controller under a null parent submitting undefined instead of a value. ([#13675](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13675))
  • Fix ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND when resolving react-hook-form due to a react-server declaration in Next.js builds. ([#13682](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13682))
  • Fix useWatch never reconciling when an Activity subtree is hidden on its first render. ([#13683](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13683))
  • Fix resetField not recomputing isValid for subscribe-only consumers. ([#13684](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13684))
  • Fix generateWatchOutput ignoring defaultValue for an array of names. ([#13686](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13686))
  • Fix useFormState never reconciling when an Activity subtree is hidden on its first render. ([#13687](react-hook-form/react-hook-form#13687))

Release notes

Sourced from @​vitejs/plugin-react's releases.

plugin-react@6.1.1

Add compiler.logDiagnostics option

Recoverable React Compiler diagnostics are no longer logged by default. Set compiler.logDiagnostics to true to log them through Vite. Fatal diagnostics are always logged and fail the transform.

Respect environment sourcemap option for React Compiler transform when builder.sharedPlugins is enabled (#1439)

The React Compiler transform was using the top-level sourcemap option instead of the environment sourcemap option. This caused a problem when the experimental builder.sharedPlugins was enabled.

Updates `lint-staged` from 17.3.0 to 17.4.1
Release notes

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v17.4.1

17.4.1

Patch Changes

  • #1840 efe5b63 - This is a version-bump-only release because the previous version 17.4.0 was not published to npmjs.com due to problems with GitHub Actions and Changesets.

17.4.0

Minor Changes

  • #1836 90ec282 - Added a new defineConfig helper for type-checking the lint-staged configuration:

    // lint-staged.config.ts

    import { defineConfig } from 'lint-staged/config'
    

    export default defineConfig({
'*.js': ['prettier --check', 'eslint'],
})

  • #1832 510a27c - Added a new flag --all to make lint-staged include all files tracked by Git, instead of only staged.

    By default lint-staged only runs tasks on files that include staged changes (hence the name). Use this flag to include all files tracked in Git version control (standard exclusions apply). Using this flag implies the --no-stash flag, disabling the automatic backup, and the --allow-empty flag so that lint-staged doesn't fail when there are no changes after running. This makes it easier to run npx lint-staged --all on a clean state, for example in CI.

Patch Changes

  • #1838 69bec99 - The behavior of the automatic backup stash has been improved when running lint-staged in multiple worktrees in parallel. You should still avoid running multiple instances of lint-staged in parallel in the same tree, because some of the Git operations are locking and might lead to data loss.

  • #1839 5e5bdd2 - Parsing of lint-staged CLI flags and Node.js API options has been rewritten to avoid inconsistent behavior between the two.

pr.title: chore(deps-dev): bump the dev-dependencies group with 8 updates

pr.body:
## Description

The **Vulnerability Scan** workflow has been failing on every push to `main` (and on the weekly schedule) for some time — [run #169](https://github.com/Doezer/Questarr/actions/runs/34089393105) is the latest. `ci.yml` itself is green; this workflow was the only red one.

Its `npm-audit` job gates on `npm audit --omit=dev`, which reported 3 moderate advisories in **production** dependencies:

| Advisory | Package | Affected | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) — DoS via attacker-controlled `isBuffer` | `qs` | `>=2.2.5 <6.16.0` | moderate |
| [GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx) — array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing | `qs` | `>=6.14.2 <=6.15.3` | moderate |

Both reach us transitively through `express@4.22.2` → `body-parser@1.20.6` → `qs@6.15.2`, which is why `express` and `body-parser` were also listed as vulnerable.

Both are fixed in **`qs@6.16.0`** (no `6.15.4` was ever published). However, `express@4.22.2` and `body-parser@1.20.6` both pin `qs: ~6.15.1`, which excludes `6.16.0` — so npm's only suggested remedy was `npm audit fix --force` → `express@5.2.1`, a semver-major upgrade that would churn the entire ~3360-line route layer. Pinning `qs` through the existing `overrides` block lifts it to the patched release without that risk.

`npm run check:overrides` confirms the override is doing work for more than just express: `openid`, `steam-web` and `superagent` all declare ranges that still permit a vulnerable `qs` too.

While auditing I also found a **high**-severity dev-side advisory that the workflow's `--omit=dev` gate does not catch, so it was going unnoticed:

| Advisory | Package | Affected | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj) — quadratic CPU consumption in `!!omap` resolution | `js-yaml` | `4.0.0 - 4.3.0` | high |

`@eslint/eslintrc` was holding a nested copy at `4.3.0` even though it already allows `^4.1.1`. That override is **scoped to `@eslint/eslintrc`** rather than declared globally, so the top-level `js-yaml@5.3.0` is left untouched.

### Changes

`package.json` — two entries added to the existing `overrides` block:

```json
"@eslint/eslintrc": { "js-yaml": "^4.3.1" },
"qs": "^6.16.0"
```

`package-lock.json` — regenerated with npm 11 (matching CI) so no unrelated lockfile metadata churns. The diff is limited to three bumps:

- `qs` 6.15.2 → 6.16.0
- `side-channel` 1.1.0 → 1.1.1 (pulled up by `qs@6.16.0`)
- `@eslint/eslintrc/node_modules/js-yaml` 4.3.0 → 4.3.2

`docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` — both new overrides documented alongside the existing ones, per the convention there of recording each override's advisory and why the upstream range still permits a vulnerable release.

`npm audit` now reports **0 vulnerabilities** both with and without dev dependencies.

### Note for a follow-up (not addressed here)

`security/vex/questarr.openvex.json` is bound only to Trivy via `TRIVY_VEX` in the `image-scan` job. The `npm-audit` job's failure message points maintainers at that VEX file, but a VEX statement there would not affect `npm audit` — so an advisory that is genuinely not exploitable in Questarr currently has no way to be waived out of this gate. Worth wiring up separately if a non-actionable advisory ever blocks the pipeline.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Checklist:

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas — the rationale is captured in the commit messages, in `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md`, and above
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation — both overrides added to `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds a new actor/integration, external interface, or security-relevant change, I have updated docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/API.md, and/or docs/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md accordingly — no interface or architecture change; this only moves transitive dependencies to patched releases, and the dependency-level record lives in `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md`
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works — the regression gates here are `npm audit --omit=dev` (the Vulnerability Scan and `sca-scan` jobs) and `check-overrides`, all of which now pass; no application code changed
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

### Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm audit --omit=dev` (the failing CI gate) | 0 vulnerabilities |
| `npm audit` (incl. dev) | 0 vulnerabilities |
| `npm run check:overrides` | both new overrides report "still needed" |
| `npm run check` | pass |
| `npm run lint` | pass |
| `npm run format:check` | pass |
| `npm run secretlint` | pass |
