Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from esbuild's changelog.

0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

### 💡 What

Added an `aria-label` to the "More Options" (`<MoreHorizontal />`) icon-only button in the downloads page row (`client/src/pages/downloads.tsx`).

### 🎯 Why

Icon-only buttons must have an explicit accessible name for screen reader users to understand their purpose. Without an `aria-label`, assistive technologies would likely just read out "button" without providing context on what the button does.

### ♿ Accessibility

The button now clearly announces "Options for [Game Title]" or "Options for download" if the title is missing, significantly improving the experience for visually impaired users relying on screen readers.

💡 What: Consolidated four separate `useMemo` hooks (which used chained `.filter().map()` operations) into a single `useMemo` hook with one `for...of` loop in `client/src/pages/discover.tsx`.
🎯 Why: The previous implementation required 4 distinct iterations over the `localGames` array and created numerous unnecessary intermediate arrays. This caused an O(4N) overhead which can bottleneck React renders when a user's library grows large.
📊 Impact: Reduces iteration overhead from O(4N) to O(N) and completely eliminates intermediate array allocations when computing hidden, wanted, and owned game sets.
🔬 Measurement: Verify the discovery page correctly displays, hides, and filters games depending on user preferences, with no changes in visible behavior but less memory and CPU usage during component mounting/updates.

---

pr.body:
Users requested a Home Assistant add-on path for Questarr so it can be installed directly from HA Add-on Store. This PR adds a complete add-on repository structure and wires persistence correctly for Questarr’s existing container runtime.

- **Home Assistant add-on repository metadata**
  - Added `home-assistant/repository.yaml` so Home Assistant can register this repo as an add-on source.

- **Questarr add-on definition**
  - Added `home-assistant/questarr/config.yaml` with slug, startup behavior, web UI mapping, exposed port, and architecture declaration (`amd64`).

- **Add-on image wrapper for persistent data**
  - Added `home-assistant/questarr/Dockerfile` that extends Questarr’s published image and maps app data to HA persistent storage by linking `/app/data` to `/data`.
  - Includes one-time migration logic if `/app/data` already contains seeded content.

- **Documentation updates**
  - Updated root `README.md` with Home Assistant add-on installation instructions.
  - Added `home-assistant/questarr/README.md` with add-on-specific runtime/storage notes.

```dockerfile
ARG BUILD_FROM=ghcr.io/doezer/questarr:1.4.0
FROM ${BUILD_FROM}

RUN mkdir -p /data
RUN if [ -d /app/data ] && [ ! -L /app/data ]; then cp -a /app/data/. /data/ && rm -rf /app/data; fi
RUN ln -sfn /data /app/data
```

## 🎨 Palette: Add ARIA label to Add Release Group button

**💡 What:** 
Added an `aria-label` attribute to the "Add release group" icon-only button in the `PreferredReleaseGroupsSettings` component. 

**🎯 Why:**
This enhances the accessibility of the UI. Icon-only buttons without an explicit label are often read as "unlabelled button" by screen readers, which can be confusing. The newly added ARIA label accurately describes the action that the button performs.

**📸 Before/After:**
*   **Before:** The "Add release group" icon-only button was lacking an `aria-label` attribute, making it less accessible for users relying on screen readers. 
*   **After:** The button now includes an `aria-label="Add release group"` attribute.

**♿ Accessibility:**
This micro-UX improvement ensures that the "Add release group" button is properly announced by screen readers, making the interface more accessible and intuitive to navigate.

---

pr.body:
💡 What: Wrapped the `resultsWithCollectionStatus` mapping in a `useMemo` hook and replaced the `userGames.some(...)` lookup with a `Set` to achieve O(1) membership checks.

🎯 Why: The original logic evaluated an $O(N \times M)$ nested array iteration (where N is search results and M is the user's library) directly in the component body. This meant it was re-calculating on every single keystroke during the search typing debounce and any other state change in `AddGameModal`, causing micro-stutters for users with large libraries.

📊 Impact: Reduces time complexity from $O(N \times M)$ to $O(N + M)$ and ensures the calculation is strictly memoized to only run when the search results or local library actually change.

🔬 Measurement: Observe the "Add Game" modal's typing responsiveness and render timings in React DevTools, especially for users with hundreds of games in their library.

---

*PR created automatically by Jules for task [7444706966073268596](https://jules.google.com/task/7444706966073268596) started by @Doezer*

pr.body:
This pull request introduces a new `SendLogsDialog` component for uploading logs to support, along with comprehensive tests for both the dialog and the underlying log upload utilities. The changes ensure that logs are scrubbed of PII, uploaded securely, and that users receive clear feedback and guidance throughout the process. The most important changes are summarized below.

### New Feature: Send Logs Dialog

* Added the `SendLogsDialog` component (`client/src/components/SendLogsDialog.tsx`) for uploading logs to support, including UI for consent, upload progress, success (with support code and GitHub issue link), and error handling. The dialog scrubs PII from logs, detects platform, and provides user feedback via toasts and UI states.

### Testing: Dialog and Log Upload Utilities

* Added a full test suite for the `SendLogsDialog` component (`client/__tests__/SendLogsDialog.test.tsx`), covering log submission, error and rate-limit handling, clipboard copy feedback, and UI state transitions.
* Added a test suite for log upload utilities (`client/__tests__/send-logs.test.ts`), verifying PII scrubbing, log submission, error handling, GitHub issue URL generation, and platform detection.

### Test Improvements and Fixes

* Improved an existing test in `LogsPage.remaining.test.tsx` to ensure log streaming events are handled inside `act` for proper React state updates.
* Added `act` import to `LogsPage.remaining.test.tsx` to support the above fix.
pr.title: Add send logs
Fix Torznab/Prowlarr download URL rewrite to avoid proxy double-wrapping on host aliases

pr.body:
This pull request introduces a new "Shelved" status for games and refactors how status changes are handled in the UI, replacing the old "cycle through statuses" button with a more accessible and flexible `StatusPicker` component. It also adds comprehensive tests for `StatusPicker` and updates the UI and tests across several components to support the new status and picker.

**Major improvements and changes:**

### 1. Status Picker Refactor and Accessibility

- Replaces the old "Mark as [Next Status]" button with a new `StatusPicker` component in both `GameCard` and `CompactGameCard`, providing a popover to select any user-settable status directly. The new picker is more accessible, with improved aria-labels and keyboard navigation. (F5204ed3L243R243, F5204ed3L525R525, F83e7866L375R375)
- Removes the legacy "getNextStatusLabel" logic and related code, as status changes are no longer cyclical but user-chosen. (F5204ed3L42R42, F5204ed3L97R97, F83e7866L91R91, [client/__tests__/utils.test.tsL7](diffhunk://#diff-6363ac1643aa83494d06ca091a62eba1b988f0af40a1d4ffd8cd6a74761698d7L7), Fbfd779dL132R132)

### 2. "Shelved" Status Support

- Adds a new "Shelved" status to `StatusBadge` and all relevant UI, including filters and library statistics, with appropriate icons and colors. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-240e12ab12eea4e28c73f3c21c24f41d858e6caea1b1052218001cd85f0ee11fR13-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a49d94a3d3ed0a08be40f6db1411942aeab9aa57ca1b817d3a7a466b7e3f030fR8) Faca4928L247R247, Faca4928L420R420)

### 3. Test Suite Updates

- Adds a comprehensive test suite for `StatusPicker`, covering accessibility, active state, custom triggers, and status change handling.
- Updates existing tests for `GameCard` and `CompactGameCard` to use the new picker and check for correct aria-labels and behavior. Removes tests for the old status cycling logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1103bf191cff66b6663c381394e3877378aaf8c805eb17dee6d3ad602b554ad3L154-R157) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8e8ee8bb3306cd3f6a4c5146b385c492c5b6becc9ab998af82e324cae42374fbL101-R111) F57e9f72L124R124, [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1e7eb3699e26a937837a69497d0031dd9d61599c3e2638cb4285a015e255aed1L259-R272) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-819951863d9ca80261232d2cbb8790cca67ae9057cfba5845d467b0c6de10874R109-R126) Fbfd779dL132R132)

### 4. UI Consistency and Bugfixes

- Ensures the `StatusPicker` is used consistently for both main and compact game cards, including custom triggers and correct popover behavior. (F5204ed3L243R243, F5204ed3L525R525, F83e7866L375R375)
- Updates the library filter and stats display to include "Shelved" as a selectable and visible status. (Faca4928L247R247, Faca4928L420R420)

**Summary:**  
These changes modernize the status selection UX, improve accessibility, introduce the "Shelved" status throughout the app, and ensure comprehensive test coverage for the new logic.
pr.title: Add shelved status feature

pr.body:
This pull request introduces responsive mobile support for several modal components by adding bottom sheet (drawer) layouts for mobile devices, while retaining the existing dialog/modal layouts for desktop. It also refactors common content into reusable variables and makes minor UI adjustments for consistency.

**Mobile drawer support for modals:**

pr.body:
In some UNRAID/Docker setups, qBittorrent returns `Ok.` for URL-based torrent add, but Questarr fails immediate verification and then hits a 500 from indexer fallback download, resulting in a false `"All downloaders failed"` response. This change preserves success semantics when qBittorrent has already accepted the add.

- **Downloader behavior: accepted-but-unverified path**
  - In `QBittorrentClient.addDownload`, track when non-magnet URL add returns `Ok.` but no torrent is immediately observable.
  - If fallback `.torrent` fetch fails afterward, return success (`accepted by qBittorrent`) instead of surfacing a hard failure.

- **Failure-mode handling**
  - Restricts this behavior to the specific non-magnet case where qBittorrent explicitly acknowledged URL add.
  - Keeps existing magnet behavior and fallback logic unchanged for other error paths.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Added focused test for: URL add `Ok.` → verification miss → fallback fetch `500` → operation treated as accepted.

```ts
if (urlAddAcceptedButUnverified) {
  return {
    success: true,
    message: "Download accepted by qBittorrent but could not be verified immediately",
  };
}
```
pr.title: Handle qBittorrent accepted-but-unverified adds to avoid false 500 failures

pr.body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** Several backend components (`server/igdb.ts`, `server/routes.ts`, and `server/downloaders.ts`) were making outbound HTTP requests using the global `fetch` API. This bypassed the application's built-in SSRF and DNS rebinding protections, potentially allowing attackers to pivot requests into internal networks.
🎯 **Impact:** An attacker could potentially perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and access sensitive internal services, local host ports, or cloud metadata endpoints.
🔧 **Fix:** Replaced all global `fetch` calls with the `safeFetch` utility from `server/ssrf.ts`. `safeFetch` securely resolves hostnames, checks the resulting IPs against an allowlist/denylist to prevent access to private networks, and pins the connection to the validated IP to prevent Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) DNS rebinding attacks.
✅ **Verification:** Verified by running the project's test suite, which includes comprehensive tests for SSRF protection (`ssrf.test.ts`, `downloaders_ssrf.test.ts`) and ensuring all integrations still function as expected.

---

pr.body:
### 💡 What

Consolidated multiple sequential array traversals (`filter`, `map`) into a single manual `for` loop inside a unified `useMemo` block in `client/src/pages/discover.tsx`.

### 🎯 Why

The component previously iterated over the potentially large `localGames` array up to 7 times on every memoization re-evaluation, generating multiple intermediate arrays and `Set` objects across 4 separate `useMemo` hooks. This resulted in unnecessary garbage collection and O(7N) time complexity for an operation that can be done in O(N).

### 📊 Impact

Reduces component re-calculation time complexity from O(7N) to strictly O(N), significantly reducing redundant array allocations and garbage collection overhead during React state updates or when navigating back/forth to the page.

### 🔬 Measurement

Run a local performance profile while loading the discover page with a library of 1000+ games. The `useMemo` execution time for `hiddenIgdbIds`, `ownedIgdbIds`, `wantedIgdbIds`, and `igdbToLocalIdMap` is drastically reduced. Functionality and existing test cases remain fully covered.

---

pr.body:
This pull request introduces robust support for deploying the app under a configurable base path, making the frontend work seamlessly in subdirectories or behind reverse proxies. It does so by centralizing base path logic in new helpers, updating routing and asset references, and ensuring all API and socket connections use the correct path. Additionally, it replaces direct use of the Socket.IO client with a shared singleton to avoid redundant connections and streamline event handling.

Base path support and routing:

* Added `app-path.ts` with helpers to normalize, resolve, and prefix URLs with the app's base path, and updated all static asset and API references to use these helpers. This ensures assets, API requests, and navigation work correctly regardless of deployment location. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-87229c5e5cc83ef0b0354b0556d5f50831bb5dd8436f9ad38921c5d92a07a45bR1-R91) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-edfa4829c58ad696e48ab606527eabead1471963a743486a94b65fe215035814L7-R16) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b7e0b9d1c8563f05f86d60331e194a4b961d58fbfd37e4dbdff394b9b7ff9417R35) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b7e0b9d1c8563f05f86d60331e194a4b961d58fbfd37e4dbdff394b9b7ff9417L146-R147) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-79591be67a2f529544c5ef31ae2dd40bdaeffca114eef8ce9d6214bf403d6dc8R18) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-79591be67a2f529544c5ef31ae2dd40bdaeffca114eef8ce9d6214bf403d6dc8L44-R49)
* Updated the main router in `App.tsx` to use Wouter's `base` prop, so client-side navigation is also base path aware. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ce931a2269184f4b06d6be36ead81f2ca3e95e44a5c8d600f47da1dfa35b9337L1-R1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ce931a2269184f4b06d6be36ead81f2ca3e95e44a5c8d600f47da1dfa35b9337R14) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ce931a2269184f4b06d6be36ead81f2ca3e95e44a5c8d600f47da1dfa35b9337L66-R67) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ce931a2269184f4b06d6be36ead81f2ca3e95e44a5c8d600f47da1dfa35b9337R147-R154)

API and authentication requests:

* Centralized API requests through a new `apiFetch` function that automatically applies the base path and authorization headers; refactored all fetch calls and the query client to use this. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4174db2b5432c130a919f3e9ce7492edc899f9ec052db153918b90de87ce7e4bR2) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4174db2b5432c130a919f3e9ce7492edc899f9ec052db153918b90de87ce7e4bR36-L50) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4174db2b5432c130a919f3e9ce7492edc899f9ec052db153918b90de87ce7e4bL61-R98) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-8b8927c32ff11dca6c914ad78cbdbfdf0e5a9e48b7b2fd0d59c59ce793164498L21-R21) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-8b8927c32ff11dca6c914ad78cbdbfdf0e5a9e48b7b2fd0d59c59ce793164498L105-R105) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-2f983a4badfb7166da73ff8df7890fe927412b5da66bf740cddf1890c2061f2fL4-R4) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-2f983a4badfb7166da73ff8df7890fe927412b5da66bf740cddf1890c2061f2fL40-R40) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-2f983a4badfb7166da73ff8df7890fe927412b5da66bf740cddf1890c2061f2fL66-R66)

Socket.IO connection management:

* Introduced a `getSocket` helper that provides a shared singleton connection, using the correct socket path for the current base path. All Socket.IO usage now goes through this singleton, preventing redundant connections and ensuring consistent event handling. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e511e33767f5faa431f25880fef5e6504560471d202299721a1049a1d790d213R1-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5fd1e1cfb4fe8cbc1120534cf887e0566b846da231be4c51687e1045bf7a455dL52-R52) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5fd1e1cfb4fe8cbc1120534cf887e0566b846da231be4c51687e1045bf7a455dL333-R336) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3cd8c8fa96e290c0950ca134e3eac7060a8509cd57d016c67c4b2496b8a8ab40L10-R13) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-3cd8c8fa96e290c0950ca134e3eac7060a8509cd57d016c67c4b2496b8a8ab40L46-R47) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-3cd8c8fa96e290c0950ca134e3eac7060a8509cd57d016c67c4b2496b8a8ab40L63-R62) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-7c8cdff5413092cf3282053a373d6c690c57668345059b067503abeb90b67fa1L2-R7) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-7c8cdff5413092cf3282053a373d6c690c57668345059b067503abeb90b67fa1L16-R16)

pr.body:
This pull request introduces a mobile-first design direction for Questarr, including a new bottom navigation bar, improved mobile layouts for game cards, and a refactor of navigation item management. The changes improve usability on small screens, unify navigation definitions, and enhance touch target safety and visual clarity.

**Mobile Design and Layout Improvements**

* Added a new `MobileBottomNav` component and updated the main layout in `App.tsx` to support persistent bottom navigation on mobile, ensuring primary actions remain thumb-accessible. (`client/src/App.tsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ce931a2269184f4b06d6be36ead81f2ca3e95e44a5c8d600f47da1dfa35b9337R9-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ce931a2269184f4b06d6be36ead81f2ca3e95e44a5c8d600f47da1dfa35b9337L132-R105)
* Enhanced `CompactGameCard` with a dedicated mobile layout via a `mobileLayout` prop, optimizing information density, touch targets, and visual hierarchy for phones. (`client/src/components/CompactGameCard.tsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b3bb94dc8e8fb66062efc87c944f23be2eac3275afb279796636d8ef3b5914fcR32) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b3bb94dc8e8fb66062efc87c944f23be2eac3275afb279796636d8ef3b5914fcR51) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b3bb94dc8e8fb66062efc87c944f23be2eac3275afb279796636d8ef3b5914fcR137-R319)
* Updated button and tooltip interactions in `CompactGameCard` to improve accessibility and prevent click event propagation issues, especially on mobile. (`client/src/components/CompactGameCard.tsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b3bb94dc8e8fb66062efc87c944f23be2eac3275afb279796636d8ef3b5914fcR557-R597) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b3bb94dc8e8fb66062efc87c944f23be2eac3275afb279796636d8ef3b5914fcL423-R619)
* Added a new `useIsMobile` hook and integrated it into `GameCard` to enable responsive behavior based on device type. (`client/src/components/GameCard.tsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c42fe014381af84d247dfdc557b754d6585ecfc873f16d4dd646dbe00358e05bR18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c42fe014381af84d247dfdc557b754d6585ecfc873f16d4dd646dbe00358e05bR53)

**Navigation Refactor**

* Centralized navigation item definitions into `navigation-items` and updated `AppSidebar` to use these shared lists, reducing duplication and improving maintainability. (`client/src/components/AppSidebar.tsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b7e0b9d1c8563f05f86d60331e194a4b961d58fbfd37e4dbdff394b9b7ff9417L2-L15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b7e0b9d1c8563f05f86d60331e194a4b961d58fbfd37e4dbdff394b9b7ff9417L35-R23) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b7e0b9d1c8563f05f86d60331e194a4b961d58fbfd37e4dbdff394b9b7ff9417L129-R52) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b7e0b9d1c8563f05f86d60331e194a4b961d58fbfd37e4dbdff394b9b7ff9417L199-R122)

pr.body:
This pull request introduces a new downloader management system, providing a unified interface for interacting with multiple download clients (such as Transmission, rTorrent, qBittorrent, SABnzbd, NZBGet, and Synology Download Station). It adds a central `DownloaderManager` class, a shared downloader client interface, and several utility functions for handling download URLs and protocols. The main changes are as follows:

### Downloader Management

* Added the `DownloaderManager` class in `manager.ts`, which centralizes creation and management of downloader clients, provides fallback logic for adding downloads, and standardizes all downloader operations (test, add, pause, resume, remove, get status/details, get free space). This enables consistent handling of different downloader types and error management.
* Updated `index.ts` to re-export all downloader clients and the new `DownloaderManager`, simplifying imports elsewhere in the codebase.

### Downloader Client Interface

* Introduced a new shared downloader client interface (`DownloaderClient`) and related types (`DownloadRequest`, `DownloadResult`, etc.) in `types.ts`, ensuring all downloader implementations follow a common contract.

### Utility Functions

* Added utility functions in `utils.ts` for:
  - Fixing URL encoding issues with NZB/torrent download links, especially for Prowlarr and similar indexers (`fixNzbUrlEncoding`).
  - Extracting BitTorrent info hashes from magnet links (`extractHashFromUrl`).
  - Fetching URLs with manual redirect handling to detect and handle magnet link redirects (`fetchWithMagnetDetection`).

pr.body:
### 💡 What

Added an `aria-label` to the "Add preferred release group" button and improved ARIA semantics in the App Sidebar by applying `aria-hidden="true"` to inner icon and text elements when the parent button already defines a comprehensive, consolidated `aria-label`.

### 🎯 Why

Icon-only buttons must provide an `aria-label` so screen reader users understand their function. Additionally, when a parent element provides a complete, accessible name via `aria-label` (such as combining the navigation text and notification badge count), the child elements should be hidden from assistive technologies. If they are not hidden, screen readers will redundantly read the parent label and then the text of the child elements again.

### 📸 Before/After

**Before:**

- Screen readers encounter an unlabelled `<button>` in the release groups settings.
- Screen readers reading the sidebar hear: "Downloads, 2 active downloads, button. Downloads. 2."

**After:**

- Screen readers announce "Add preferred release group, button" in the settings.
- Screen readers reading the sidebar hear only: "Downloads, 2 active downloads, button."

### ♿ Accessibility

- Fixed missing accessible name for icon-only button.
- Prevented redundant reading of text and badges by assistive technologies in the navigation sidebar.

🚨 Severity: MEDIUM
💡 Vulnerability: Information Leakage - The Express framework natively advertises its presence by injecting an `X-Powered-By` header in HTTP responses. Exposing the underlying technology stack can give attackers insight that could assist in crafting tailored exploits.
🎯 Impact: While not a direct avenue for compromise, leaking version or stack details reduces the effort an attacker needs to profile the target, aiding in vulnerability scanning.
🔧 Fix: Added `app.disable("x-powered-by");` to the global application setup in `server/index.ts` to prevent Express from sending this header. Tests were updated in `server/__tests__/security.test.ts` to enforce this policy.
✅ Verification: Ensured unit tests passed and verified that `x-powered-by` is no longer output.

Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.60.0

🌐 HAR recording on Tracing

tracing.startHar() / tracing.stopHar() expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same content, mode and urlFilter options as recordHar. The returned Disposable makes it easy to scope a recording with await using:

await using har = await context.tracing.startHar('trace.har');
const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://playwright.dev');
// HAR is finalized when `har` goes out of scope.

🪝 Drop API

New locator.drop() simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element. Playwright dispatches dragenter, dragover, and drop with a synthetic [DataTransfer] in the page context — works cross-browser and is great for testing upload zones:

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  files: { name: 'note.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('hello') },
});

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
data: {
'text/plain': 'hello world',
'text/uri-list': 'https://example.com',
},
});

🎯 Aria snapshots

  • expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot() now works on a Page, in addition to a Locator — equivalent to asserting against page.locator('body').
  • New boxes option on locator.ariaSnapshot() / page.ariaSnapshot() appends each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height], useful for AI consumption.

🛑 test.abort()

New test.abort() aborts the currently running test from a fixture, hook, or route handler with an optional message. Use it when you have detected an unrecoverable misuse and want to fail the test right away:

test('does not publish to the shared page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/publish', route => {
    test.abort('Tests must not publish to the shared page. Use the `clone` option.');
    return route.abort();
  });
  // ...
});

pr.body:
qBittorrent 5.2.x can return session cookies named `QBT_SID_<port>` rather than `SID`. Questarr’s qBittorrent client assumed `SID` only, so auth appeared successful but subsequent API calls were sent without a valid session cookie and failed with 403.

- **Auth cookie parsing**
  - Updated qBittorrent login cookie extraction to accept both legacy `SID` and new `QBT_SID_*` cookie names.
  - Parses cookie *name and value* together from `Set-Cookie` headers instead of extracting only the value.

- **Cookie forwarding behavior**
  - Preserves the exact session cookie returned by qBittorrent (`SID=...` or `QBT_SID_...=...`) and reuses it on subsequent API requests.

- **Coverage for new cookie format**
  - Added downloader unit coverage for a login response returning `QBT_SID_20080=...`, asserting requests include the same cookie key/value pair.

```ts
const match = cookie.match(/((?:QBT_)?SID(?:_[^=;]+)?)=([^;]+)/);
if (match) {
  sessionCookie = `${match[1]}=${match[2]}`; // preserves SID or QBT_SID_*
}
```
pr.title: Handle qBittorrent 5.2.x `QBT_SID_*` auth cookies instead of assuming `SID`

pr.body:
### 💡 What

Added an `aria-label` to the icon-only delete button in the RSS feed settings (`client/src/components/RssSettings.tsx`) and explicitly marked the inner `Trash` SVG icon with `aria-hidden="true"`.

### 🎯 Why

Icon-only buttons must have descriptive ARIA labels to provide context for screen reader users. The "Delete feed" button lacked any textual description, making it difficult for users relying on assistive technology to understand the button's action.

### 📸 Before/After

*(Visuals remain unchanged, but the DOM now includes the appropriate accessibility tags).*

**Before:**

```tsx
<Button
  variant="ghost"
  size="icon"
  onClick={() => deleteFeedMutation.mutate(feed.id)}
  className="text-destructive"
>
  <Trash className="h-4 w-4" />
</Button>
```

**After:**

```tsx
<Button
  variant="ghost"
  size="icon"
  onClick={() => deleteFeedMutation.mutate(feed.id)}
  className="text-destructive"
  aria-label={`Delete feed ${feed.name}`}
>
  <Trash className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
</Button>
```

### ♿ Accessibility

- Provides a clear and descriptive label (`Delete feed [Feed Name]`) for screen readers.
- Hides the decorative icon from the accessibility tree to prevent redundant announcements.

---

*PR created automatically by Jules for task [332970449602909932](https://jules.google.com/task/332970449602909932) started by @Doezer*

Bumps [actions/github-script](https://github.com/actions/github-script) from 7.0.1 to 9.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/github-script's releases.

v9.0.0

New features:

  • getOctokit factory function — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See Creating additional clients with getOctokit for details and examples.
  • Orchestration ID in user-agent — The ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID environment variable is automatically appended to the user-agent string for request tracing.

Breaking changes:

  • require('@actions/github') no longer works in scripts. The upgrade to @actions/github v9 (ESM-only) means require('@actions/github') will fail at runtime. If you previously used patterns like const { getOctokit } = require('@actions/github') to create secondary clients, use the new injected getOctokit function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.
  • getOctokit is now an injected function parameter. Scripts that declare const getOctokit = ... or let getOctokit = ... will get a SyntaxError because JavaScript does not allow const/let redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected getOctokit directly, or use var getOctokit = ... if you need to redeclare it.
  • If your script accesses other @actions/github internals beyond the standard github/octokit client, you may need to update those references for v9 compatibility.

What's Changed

  • Add ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID to user-agent string by @​Copilot in actions/github-script#695
  • ci: use deployment: false for integration test environments by @​salmanmkc in actions/github-script#712
  • feat!: add getOctokit to script context, upgrade @​actions/github v9, @​octokit/core v7, and related packages by @​salmanmkc in actions/github-script#700

pr.body:
Two bugs prevented auto-download from firing reliably: `filterByPreferredGroups` was silently ignored in the cron path, and the same release appearing on multiple indexers inflated `mainItems.length` above 1, bypassing the auto-download gate.

## Bug #1 — `filterByPreferredGroups` not respected

`applyPreferredGroupsFilter` always fell back to all items when no preferred-group match was found, regardless of the strict toggle. This caused two failure modes:
- With strict filtering on and no match → all items returned → wrong release auto-downloaded
- With preferred group SKIDROW and results [SKIDROW, CODEX, CODEX] → 3 items, no auto-download instead of 1 item triggering it

`applyPreferredGroupsFilter` now accepts a `strict` boolean; when `true` and no items match, it returns `[]`:

```typescript
// before
return filtered.length > 0 ? filtered : items;

// after
if (filtered.length > 0) return filtered;
return strict ? [] : items;
```

Both call sites pass `settings.filterByPreferredGroups ?? false`.

## Bug #2 — Cross-indexer duplicates block auto-download

The same torrent hosted by two indexers produced two identical `mainItems`, pushing `mainItems.length` to 2 and preventing the single-result auto-download path from ever firing for users with multiple indexers.

New `deduplicateByTitle(items, indexerPriorityMap)` normalizes titles and keeps one entry per release, preferring the item from the highest-priority indexer (lowest `priority` number). Indexers are fetched once per `checkAutoSearch()` run. Applied to both `mainItems` and `updateItems`.

## Tests

- Added `getEnabledIndexers` to the storage mock
- 11 new test cases covering: strict group filter (auto-download triggered, availability cleared on no match, soft fallback preserved), deduplication (fires download, selects correct indexer, preserves genuinely distinct releases, handles title normalization across punctuation variants)

pr.body:
On NFS shares with root squash enabled, `chown` called as container root is rejected even when the target directory already has the correct ownership — causing the container to fail on startup despite correct PUID/PGID being set.

## Changes

- **`entrypoint.sh`**: Wrap both `chown` calls in ownership checks using `stat`. `chown` is skipped when the directory's UID/GID already matches the resolved `questarr` user/group.

```sh
QUESTARR_UID=$(id -u questarr)
QUESTARR_GID=$(id -g questarr)

DATA_OWNER_UID=$(stat -c '%u' /app/data)
DATA_OWNER_GID=$(stat -c '%g' /app/data)
if [ "$DATA_OWNER_UID" != "$QUESTARR_UID" ] || [ "$DATA_OWNER_GID" != "$QUESTARR_GID" ]; then
  chown -R questarr:questarr /app/data
fi
```

The ownership check runs after any `usermod`/`groupmod` adjustments, so the resolved UID/GID is always accurate.
pr.title: Fix unconditional chown failing on NFS mounts with root squash

pr.body:
The Steam ID save button was sending a `PUT` request to `/api/user/steam-id`, but the server only registers a `PATCH` handler for that route. The unmatched `PUT` fell through to the SPA catch-all, returning `index.html` instead of JSON — causing the client to throw `Unexpected token '<'` when attempting to parse the response.

## Change

- **`client/src/pages/settings.tsx`**: `apiRequest("PUT", ...)` → `apiRequest("PATCH", ...)` to match the server route definition in `steam-routes.ts`.

pr.body:
This pull request introduces several new features and improvements to the client-side codebase, focusing on enhancing import workflows and path mapping management. The main additions include a reusable file browser dialog, a modal for reviewing and confirming imports, and a settings page for managing path mappings. Additionally, the dashboard now displays pending imports. Some cleanup and permission changes are also included.

**New import and path mapping features:**

* Added a reusable `FileBrowser` dialog component for browsing and selecting directories within the filesystem, with support for navigation, loading states, and error handling. This is used in multiple places for consistent directory selection.
* Introduced an `ImportReviewModal` component that allows users to review and manually configure import details, such as destination path, transfer mode (move, copy, hardlink, symlink), and unpacking archives before confirming an import. Integrates the new file browser for destination selection.
* Added a `PathMappingSettings` component, providing a UI to view, add, and remove path mappings that translate remote download paths to local paths. Includes inline documentation, validation, and integration with the file browser dialog for selecting local paths.

**Dashboard enhancements:**

* Imported and rendered a `PendingImportsCard` component in the `Dashboard` to display pending imports, improving visibility of ongoing import operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1df1ef613c99932d5627b6157ab8fd8f8afcb975bac6099809f694ba3007cddfR41) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1df1ef613c99932d5627b6157ab8fd8f8afcb975bac6099809f694ba3007cddfR227-R228)

**Project maintenance and permissions:**

* Updated `.claude/settings.local.json` to allow a specific Bash command for searching third-party service references, likely for code review or auditing purposes.
* Removed the `TASKS.md` file, which previously tracked hardening and maintenance tasks, suggesting a change in how tasks are managed or documented.

These changes collectively improve the user experience for import management and path configuration, while also streamlining project maintenance.

pr.body:
⚡ Bolt: Optimize dashboard statistics computation

### 💡 What:

Refactored the dashboard statistics logic in `client/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` to use a single O(n) loop instead of multiple chained functional array operations (`filter`, `reduce`, `flatMap`, `forEach`). Fixed edge cases with missing (`undefined`/`null`) rating logic and `NaN` year outputs.

### 🎯 Why:

In a dashboard rendering potentially hundreds or thousands of games, deriving multiple distinct metric lists using nine independent O(n) array loops within a single `useMemo` block creates unnecessary memory allocations and redundant iterations. A single pass is significantly faster.

### 📊 Impact:

Reduces array iteration overhead from O(9n) to O(n) during the derivation of statistics (e.g. `topGenre`, `topPlatform`, `avgRating`).

### 🔬 Measurement:

1. Add a large number of games (1000+) to your library.
2. Load the dashboard page.
3. Use React Profiler to verify that the `Dashboard` component renders faster and consumes less JS memory during recalculations.

Release notes

Sourced from step-security/harden-runner's releases.

v2.19.0

What's Changed

New Runner Support

Harden-Runner now supports Depot, Blacksmith, Namespace, and WarpBuild runners with the same egress monitoring, runtime monitoring, and policy enforcement available on GitHub-hosted runners.

Automated Incident Response for Supply Chain Attacks

  • Global block list: Outbound connections to known malicious domains and IPs are now blocked even in audit mode.
  • System-defined detection rules: Harden-Runner will trigger lockdown mode when a high risk event is detected during an active supply chain attack (for example, a process reading the memory of the runner worker process, a common technique for stealing GitHub Actions secrets).

Bug Fixes

Windows and macOS: stability and reliability fixes

Full Changelog: https://github.com/step-security/harden-runner/compare/v2.18.0...v2.19.0

v2.18.0

What's Changed

Global Block List: During supply chain incidents like the recent axios and trivy compromises, StepSecurity will add known malicious domains and IP addresses (IOCs) to a global block list. These will be automatically blocked, even in audit mode, providing immediate protection without requiring any workflow changes.

Deploy on Self-Hosted VM: Added deploy-on-self-hosted-vm input that allows the Harden Runner agent to be installed directly on ephemeral self-hosted Linux runner VMs at workflow runtime. This is intended as an alternative when baking the agent into the VM image is not possible.

### 💡 What

Added dynamic `aria-label`s to interactive elements inside list components (`AddGameModal` and `CompactRssFeedItem`), and hid their decorative child icons from screen readers using `aria-hidden="true"`.

### 🎯 Why

When buttons in a list (like search results or RSS feeds) only contain generic text like "Add" or an icon, screen reader users hear the same announcement repeated without context. By injecting the specific item's title into the `aria-label` (e.g., "Add Cyberpunk 2077 to collection"), we provide crucial context. Hiding the internal icons prevents redundant or confusing announcements.

### 📸 Before/After

*(No visual changes; accessibility enhancements only.)*

### ♿ Accessibility

* Improved context for screen reader users navigating search results in the Add Game modal.
* Improved context for screen reader users navigating the RSS Feed lists on mobile/compact views.
* Reduced auditory noise by explicitly hiding decorative icons within buttons that already have a descriptive label.

💡 What: Optimized render loops in `client/src/pages/calendar.tsx` (`YearView`, `MonthView`, `WeekView`) by extracting invariant Date calculations and `Object.entries` conversions outside of `.map` iterators, and replacing Date parsing with string prefix checks.
🎯 Why: Creating `new Date()` objects and stringifying them 30-40+ times per render cycle (especially inside nested loops) is computationally expensive and blocks the main thread.
📊 Impact: Reduces `Date` object instantiations and string operations by >90% during Calendar tab renders, significantly reducing jank when switching calendar views.
🔬 Measurement: Verify by switching between Year, Month, and Week views in the Calendar tab. Monitor React DevTools profiler for reduced render times in the respective view components.

pr.body:
This PR fixes a series of bugs introduced or exposed in release 1.3.0, covering real-time
   updates, download search filtering, modal state management, settings persistence, and UI
   correctness across 14 files.

  ---
  Context for reviewers

  Questarr is a game library manager in the style of the *Arr ecosystem. The frontend is   
  React 18 + TanStack Query; the backend is Express + SQLite/Drizzle. Downloads are managed
   via qBittorrent/Transmission/SABnzbd/NZBGet. Real-time updates flow through Socket.io.  

  ---
  Changes by area

  Real-time download status (server/cron.ts, GameDetailsModal.tsx)

  Root cause: The cron job was updating download statuses in the DB but never emitting     
  Socket.io events, so the frontend had no signal to re-fetch. The modal's
  GameDownloadDialog unmount bug compounded this.

  - cron.ts: Emit downloadUpdate socket event after every status transition. Also clear    
  searchResultsAvailable when searchAndCategorizeItemsForGame returns null — previously the
   "has results" badge would persist forever once set.
  - GameDetailsModal: The component returned null when game was nullish, which unmounted   
  the Radix <Dialog> while the parent open state stayed true. Radix never fired
  onOpenChange(false), breaking the X button. Fix: always render <Dialog>, gate the content
   on game != null. Also added a socket downloadUpdate listener that calls
  queryClient.invalidateQueries for the game's downloads. Reset isSummaryExpanded,
  selectedScreenshot, and downloadOpen on modal close and game change to prevent stale     
  state across opens.

  Download search filter (GameDownloadDialog.tsx, downloads-utils.ts)

  - The bundle dialog used categorizedDownloads.update (unfiltered) in all code paths —    
  init, execution, direct download, and select-all — so active platform/seeder filters were
   ignored when selecting update bundles. All five sites now use
  filteredCategorizedDownloads.update.
  - The totalWithoutPlatformFilter calculation in the "no platform results" banner was     
  missing the isUsenetItem(t) || guard, so usenet items could incorrectly suppress the     
  banner.
  - isUsenetItem heuristic updated to prefer the explicit downloadType field when present, 
  falling back to grabs/age detection only when absent.

  Downloads page (downloads.tsx)

  - Infinite re-render (DL-1): hasShownErrors was a useState<Set> in the useEffect
  dependency array and mutated inside the same effect — each mutation triggered a
  re-render, which re-ran the effect, causing toast spam every 5 s. Replaced with useRef;  
  the effect dep array is now [errors, toast] only.
  - downloaderSummaries was computed from raw downloads instead of filteredDownloads, so   
  the status pill counts disagreed with visible cards when type/source filters were active.
  - Pause/resume button was rendered for terminal statuses (completed, error, seeding),    
  which would fire a downloader API error. Now guarded to downloading | paused | repairing 
  | unpacking only.

  Claim modals (ClaimBatchModal.tsx, ClaimDownloadModal.tsx)

  ClaimBatchModal:
  - When an IGDB search result was selected, selectedGame.id was set to g.igdbId.toString()
   (a numeric IGDB string). If that value reached the API as gameId, the DB UUID lookup    
  returned 404. Fix: set id: undefined for IGDB-sourced selections — the source: "igdb"    
  field already signals that newGame should be used.
  - progress in the onSuccess closure was the stale React state from the render that       
  triggered mutate(), so the toast always reported "0 group(s) linked". Fix: return        
  processedCount from mutationFn and read it as the data argument in onSuccess.
  - If firstResult.gameId was missing (API error that didn't throw), subsequent downloads  
  in the same group would create duplicate game rows. Fix: throw when gameId is absent.    
  - groupStates was never cleared on modal close — stale IGDB query, selection, and open   
  state persisted on reopen.

  ClaimDownloadModal:
  - Mutation error state was never reset between modal opens, showing a previous failure on
   reopen. Fix: claimMutation.reset() on open → true.
  - displayedIgdbResults (introduced to clear stale results when query < 3 chars) was      
  computed but the JSX still used raw igdbResults. Fixed the template to use
  displayedIgdbResults.

  Settings (settings.tsx)

  - IGDB save blocked (SET-1): igdbClientSecret is always initialised to "" on load (the   
  server never returns it). The save guard required both fields to be non-empty, so users  
  updating only their Client ID got a "provide both fields" error. Fix: allow save when    
  already configured and at least one field has a value; never send an empty string as the 
  secret.
  - xREL API base wiped (SET-2): xrelApiBase state was only set when config.xrel existed.  
  If the config arrived without apiBase, saving would send apiBase: undefined, silently    
  clearing the stored value. Fix: only update state when config.xrel.apiBase is explicitly 
  defined.

  Empty states and display (Dashboard.tsx, wishlist.tsx, xrel-releases.tsx, GameCard.tsx)  

  - Dashboard: Empty state only triggered when filteredGames.length === 0 && searchQuery — 
  filter-induced zero results fell through to an empty <GameGrid>. Now triggers on
  filteredGames.length === 0 with distinct messages for filters vs truly empty library.    
  initialQuery on AddGameModal was using the raw un-debounced value; changed to
  debouncedSearchQuery. Store cleanup extracted into a dedicated unmount-only effect.      
  - Wishlist: Empty state checked wishlistGames.length (ignores showDownloadsOnly) instead 
  of filteredGames.length. When all filters combined to zero results, blank sections       
  rendered with no feedback. Added a visible indicator when multiple filters are
  simultaneously active.
  - xREL: Added ?. null guards on matchCandidate.title in the disabled prop, title
  attribute, and spinner check. Added a useEffect to sync local page state to
  data.pagination.current_page when the API clamps the page number.
  - GameCard: new Date(isoString).getFullYear() returns the wrong year in UTC− timezones.  
  Replaced with .slice(0, 4). genres.map() always returns a truthy array so the || "No     
  genres" fallback never fired; replaced with an explicit .length > 0 check.

  ---
  What was intentionally not changed

  - game.rating ? truthiness check in GameCard — the test suite and product intent confirm 
  that rating: 0 means "unrated" in IGDB data; the falsy check is correct.
  - Backend security bugs (RT-1 ownership checks, DLR-4 SSRF bypass, MG-1/MG-2 migration   
  issues) — out of scope for this bug-fix branch; tracked separately.

  ---
  Test coverage

  All 976 existing tests pass. No new tests added in this PR — the bugs fixed here are     
  primarily UI state/interaction issues and real-time plumbing that are not covered by the 
  current Vitest suite.
pr.title: Fix download search, UI bugs, and state management issues

pr.body:
This pull request introduces a new feature that allows users to link (or "claim") downloads to games in their library or via IGDB search, directly from the downloads page. It also adds batch scanning for unlinked downloads, improves category handling for Transmission downloads, and makes several related UI and backend adjustments.

**Key changes:**

### Claim Download Feature (UI & UX)

* Added a new `ClaimDownloadModal` component, allowing users to link a download to a game from their library or IGDB, with category selection and confidence indicators. This modal is loaded lazily for performance. (`client/src/components/ClaimDownloadModal.tsx`, `client/src/pages/downloads.tsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4229187d830a74ca396ba785e012e9d43ddf30791e3fa0dab645822fea67b454R1-R332) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R52-R53) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R804-R821)
* Integrated "Link to Game" action in the downloads table dropdown menu, opening the claim modal for the selected download. (`client/src/pages/downloads.tsx`)
* Added a "Scan Unlinked" button to trigger batch scanning for unlinked downloads, with a corresponding modal loaded lazily. (`client/src/pages/downloads.tsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R487-R497) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R804-R821)

### Backend & Data Model Improvements

* Enhanced Transmission downloader support to fetch and expose the `labels` field as the download's category, improving category filtering and identification. (`server/downloaders.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-be03eb09753a830ce7841910dfc733cb66aa7457b1f2faefb7dd628926880d54R69) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-be03eb09753a830ce7841910dfc733cb66aa7457b1f2faefb7dd628926880d54R539) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-be03eb09753a830ce7841910dfc733cb66aa7457b1f2faefb7dd628926880d54R658)
* Removed legacy category filtering logic from `DownloaderManager.getAllDownloads`, as category is now handled per-download and per-client. (`server/downloaders.ts`)

### Shared Utilities & Schema

* Imported and utilized `categorizeDownload` and `releaseMatchesGame` in the backend routes to support new claim and matching logic. (`server/routes.ts`)
* Updated imports to include `insertGameDownloadSchema` for future download-claiming logic. (`server/routes.ts`)

### UI Enhancements & Test Adjustments

* Updated test setup in `GameCard.test.tsx` for consistency in mocking `window.matchMedia`. (`client/__tests__/GameCard.test.tsx`)
* Added new icons and improved import structure for UI consistency. (`client/src/pages/downloads.tsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R36-R37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R52-R53)

These changes collectively improve the process of associating downloads with games, streamline category handling, and enhance the user experience for managing downloads.

This pull request introduces a new backend route for fetching direct PCGamingWiki URLs for games via their Steam App IDs, integrates this route into the frontend to display more accurate links, and adds comprehensive tests for the new functionality. It also includes minor refactoring and formatting changes in several files.

**Backend: PCGamingWiki Integration**

- Adds a new Express router (`pcgamingwiki-router.ts`) that exposes a `/api/external/pcgamingwiki` endpoint. This endpoint takes a `steamAppId`, queries PCGamingWiki via their Cargo API, caches results for 24 hours, and returns the direct wiki page URL if found.
- Integrates the new router into the main server routes (`routes.ts`) so the endpoint is accessible to clients. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R71) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R201-R202)
- Provides unit and integration tests for the PCGamingWiki route, covering cache behavior, error handling, and URL formatting.

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5fd1e1cfb4fe8cbc1120534cf887e0566b846da231be4c51687e1045bf7a455dR364-R376) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5fd1e1cfb4fe8cbc1120534cf887e0566b846da231be4c51687e1045bf7a455dL367-R392)

💡 What: Wrapped the `sortedItems` calculation in `client/src/pages/search.tsx` inside a `useMemo` hook, adding `searchResults?.items` as the dependency.
🎯 Why: React Query triggers re-renders on components when queries fetch or update. The component also has local state. Previously, the `O(N log N)` date parsing and array sorting ran on every single render.
📊 Impact: Prevents expensive sorting and date parsing calculations on state changes, reducing CPU usage and potentially noticeable jank, especially when searching across many indexers returning hundreds of results.
🔬 Measurement: Verify by typing in the search bar or opening the download dialog; the `sortedItems` array will no longer be recreated unless the underlying `searchResults` change.

The feature includes UI updates, backend filtering logic, persistent storage, and comprehensive tests to ensure correct behavior.

The option is persisted and loaded with user settings. It includes a new interactive star rating UI, backend API and database changes, input validation, and comprehensive tests for the new functionality.

**User Rating Feature Implementation:**

- Added a new `userRating` field to the `games` table via a migration, and updated the backend storage and API to support reading and updating this field. Updates `esbuild` from 0.27.4 to 0.28.0
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.0

  • Add support for with { type: 'text' } imports (#4435)

    The import text proposal has reached stage 3 in the TC39 process, which means that it's recommended for implementation. It has also already been implemented by Deno and Bun. So with this release, esbuild also adds support for it. This behaves exactly the same as esbuild's existing text loader. Here's an example:

    import string from './example.txt' with { type: 'text' }
console.log(string)

  • Add integrity checks to fallback download path (#4343)

    Installing esbuild via npm is somewhat complicated with several different edge cases (see esbuild's documentation for details). If the regular installation of esbuild's platform-specific package fails, esbuild's install script attempts to download the platform-specific package itself (first with the npm command, and then with a HTTP request to registry.npmjs.org as a last resort).

    This last resort path previously didn't have any integrity checks. With this release, esbuild will now verify that the hash of the downloaded binary matches the expected hash for the current release. This pull request introduces Questarr-specific tracking and filtering features to the downloads system, enabling the UI and backend to distinguish and display downloads initiated through Questarr, as well as expose and filter by downloader categories. The changes span the backend storage, API, shared schema, frontend state and filtering logic, and include new tests to ensure correct behavior.

**Questarr tracking and downloader category support:**

* Added `trackedByQuestarr` and `downloaderCategory` fields to the shared `DownloadStatus` type and related interfaces, allowing the system to mark and expose downloads initiated through Questarr and their categories. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-248adfc01eb4816dcacc7b777efec7f15df5a4c21da1eaa3f5214b3eb61e1e9aR414-R416) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9eeafc43ad46f9266f66ec61ae470eeaeb6feb9e88814a114c4fa0e6d651c236R45-R47) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R73-R75)
* Backend now determines which downloads are tracked by Questarr by comparing hashes against stored game downloads, and includes the downloader's category in the API response if configured. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R2047) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R2059-R2060) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6af4f8e34285120717169f57249241ec070dfd0f878e186658aaa341e568c84fR115) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6af4f8e34285120717169f57249241ec070dfd0f878e186658aaa341e568c84fR643-R650) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-6af4f8e34285120717169f57249241ec070dfd0f878e186658aaa341e568c84fR1417-R1426)

**Frontend filtering and display enhancements:**

* Added a new "Source" filter tab in the downloads UI to show only Questarr-tracked downloads, and implemented logic to filter downloads accordingly. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R35) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R96) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R118-R133) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-405acc89e0958fce88b18f36396e3e51bd4abbe368ba4ef530d1cfbc2ad01156R394-R435)

**Testing improvements:**

* Extended API route tests to verify correct marking of Questarr-tracked downloads and proper inclusion or omission of the downloader category in API responses. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-33d772e1fd33ebcda5d001b58ae51771f6237e9433abc0ec64d2161082a523dbR91) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-33d772e1fd33ebcda5d001b58ae51771f6237e9433abc0ec64d2161082a523dbR1130-R1180)

This pull request improves the caching strategy and cache consistency for IGDB-powered discovery sections on both the client and server. It adds explicit control over cache durations for different types of game data, aligns client- and server-side cache times, and ensures more stable cache keys by rounding timestamps. These changes will reduce unnecessary API calls, improve performance, and provide a more consistent user experience.

**Client-side caching improvements:**

- Added `staleTime` as an optional prop to the `GameCarouselSection` component, allowing each section to specify its own cache duration for game queries. (`client/src/components/GameCarouselSection.tsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-00e726586a4b6ef674ba59be7af1df39a73facd6754934ab17fd5332a907554cR23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-00e726586a4b6ef674ba59be7af1df39a73facd6754934ab17fd5332a907554cR38) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-00e726586a4b6ef674ba59be7af1df39a73facd6754934ab17fd5332a907554cR59)
- Defined `DISCOVERY_STALE_TIME` (30 minutes) and `GENRE_PLATFORM_STALE_TIME` (15 minutes) constants, and applied them to the relevant discovery sections in the Discover page to match server-side cache TTLs. (`client/src/pages/discover.tsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b6fbd2242a7c06b522ac916019c00aa08c2d4dea546abcec33cd9f946e735140R66-R70) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b6fbd2242a7c06b522ac916019c00aa08c2d4dea546abcec33cd9f946e735140R545) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b6fbd2242a7c06b522ac916019c00aa08c2d4dea546abcec33cd9f946e735140R557) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b6fbd2242a7c06b522ac916019c00aa08c2d4dea546abcec33cd9f946e735140R569) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b6fbd2242a7c06b522ac916019c00aa08c2d4dea546abcec33cd9f946e735140R607) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b6fbd2242a7c06b522ac916019c00aa08c2d4dea546abcec33cd9f946e735140R646)

**Server-side caching and cache key stability:**

- Set explicit `Cache-Control` headers for all IGDB API endpoints to enable effective browser and CDN caching, with durations matching the client-side configuration. (`server/routes.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R1258) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R1275) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R1292) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R1316) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R1340) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R1352) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-a063e361b4700c847d46e6e6384d6b8c8b6f20ea277f3f5c43cbf4d28737de11R1364)
- Updated the IGDB client to round timestamps to the nearest hour for recent and upcoming releases, ensuring stable cache keys and maximizing cache hits. (`server/igdb.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-81ca365def826116883f5d8f4aeefbf7e993a599e8ad1c9f596119f0b2520925R94) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-81ca365def826116883f5d8f4aeefbf7e993a599e8ad1c9f596119f0b2520925L616-L643)

These changes collectively result in more predictable and efficient caching behavior across the discovery features of the app.

This pull request significantly refactors the dashboard's filtering, search, and display settings UI for improved usability and code maintainability. The main changes include replacing the `SearchBar` and `DisplaySettingsModal` components with a new integrated `PageToolbar` and in-place controls, as well as streamlining filter management and badge display.

**Dashboard UI and UX Improvements:**

* Replaced the `SearchBar` and `DisplaySettingsModal` components with a new `PageToolbar` that combines search, view controls, filter toggle, and display settings (grid columns, show hidden games) into a unified toolbar at the top of the dashboard. All display settings are now managed via an inline popover instead of a modal. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1df1ef613c99932d5627b6157ab8fd8f8afcb975bac6099809f694ba3007cddfL4-L50) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1df1ef613c99932d5627b6157ab8fd8f8afcb975bac6099809f694ba3007cddfL226-L261) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-180a8dc38fdfabc22321faf3f3c58d206881f35870daa9b74a61764d04fff84bL1-L143)
* Filter management is now more intuitive: active filters are displayed as badges with individual remove buttons, and a "Clear all" button is provided. Filter state is managed via objects with `onRemove` handlers for better encapsulation and UI clarity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1df1ef613c99932d5627b6157ab8fd8f8afcb975bac6099809f694ba3007cddfL92-L161) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1df1ef613c99932d5627b6157ab8fd8f8afcb975bac6099809f694ba3007cddfL226-L261)
* The filter panel is now rendered inline below the toolbar when toggled, with a more compact and responsive layout.

**Codebase Cleanup and Simplification:**

* Removed the now-obsolete `DisplaySettingsModal` component and its related logic from the dashboard. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1df1ef613c99932d5627b6157ab8fd8f8afcb975bac6099809f694ba3007cddfL226-L261) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1df1ef613c99932d5627b6157ab8fd8f8afcb975bac6099809f694ba3007cddfL321-L333) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-180a8dc38fdfabc22321faf3f3c58d206881f35870daa9b74a61764d04fff84bL1-L143)

* Refactored filter and search logic for conciseness, including more compact memoization and event handler code. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1df1ef613c99932d5627b6157ab8fd8f8afcb975bac6099809f694ba3007cddfL59-L71) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1df1ef613c99932d5627b6157ab8fd8f8afcb975bac6099809f694ba3007cddfL92-L161)

These changes modernize the dashboard UI, improve accessibility and clarity for filter management, and simplify the codebase by consolidating controls and removing redundant components.

pr.body:
On the Discover page, the "By Platform" select opens upward when the trigger is near the bottom of the viewport. Without a valid `max-height` constraint, the dropdown expanded to its full natural height (200+ platforms), overflowing past the top of the viewport with no way to scroll to earlier entries.

**Before:** only the tail-end of the alphabetical list was reachable
![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf509d4a-843e-47c9-8ebd-93752323429d)

## Root cause

Tailwind v4's `[--var-name]` arbitrary value syntax passes the value through as-is — it does **not** auto-wrap in `var()`. The class `max-h-[--radix-select-content-available-height]` compiled to:

```css
max-height: --radix-select-content-available-height; /* invalid, no-op */
```

Radix sets `--radix-select-content-available-height` as an inline CSS variable on the content element to communicate available space to the consumer. Without a valid `max-height` reading it, the dropdown was unconstrained.

## Fix

- **`client/src/components/ui/select.tsx`** — use explicit `var()` in the arbitrary value so Tailwind emits valid CSS:

```diff
- "... max-h-[--radix-select-content-available-height] ..."
+ "... max-h-[var(--radix-select-content-available-height)] ..."
```

This matches how `dropdown-menu.tsx` already handles the equivalent Radix variable for dropdown menus.

pr.body:
When a SABnzbd download completes and moves from queue to history, Questarr fails to find it and incorrectly assumes the download was manually removed — marking the game as owned without importing the file.

## Root cause

The cron job's `checkDownloadStatus` function builds a lookup map from `DownloaderManager.getAllDownloads()`, but for SABnzbd (and NZBGet) that method only queries the **queue** — never history. Once SABnzbd moves a completed download into history (~20–30 seconds after completion), it disappears from the queue, so `getAllDownloads()` returns nothing for it. The cron then finds nothing in the map and fires the "not found → mark as owned" error path with the wrong notification and log message.

## Changes

- **`server/cron.ts`** — `checkDownloadStatus`:
  - When a tracked download is absent from the bulk `activeDownloadMap`, fall back to `DownloaderManager.getDownloadStatus()` for that specific download hash. This method checks **both queue and history** for SABnzbd/NZBGet. Only if that individual check also returns `null` is the download declared truly missing.
  - Export `checkDownloadStatus` to make it unit-testable.

- **`server/downloaders.ts`** — `SABnzbdClient.getFromHistory`:
  - Replace `fetch(url)` with `this.fetchWithFallback(url)` so SSL certificate handling is consistent with all other SABnzbd API calls (fixes a secondary failure path on HTTPS instances with self-signed certificates).
  - Pass `nzo_ids: id` to `getApiUrl` so the history request targets the specific download directly.

- **`server/__tests__/cron_download_status.test.ts`** — new test file validating the fallback behaviour: bulk path works when download is in the queue; fallback detects a completed history item and routes it through the normal completion path; download is only declared missing after both checks return `null`; no extra `getDownloadStatus` call when the bulk map already contains the item.

- **`server/__tests__/downloaders_comprehensive.test.ts`** — adds SABnzbd test cases for: completed item in history, failed item in history, item absent from both queue and history, and verification that `nzo_ids` is included in the history request URL.

💡 **What:** Added `useMemo` hooks around the sorted game arrays (`upcomingGames`, `releasedGames`, `tbaGames`) in `client/src/pages/wishlist.tsx`, and moved the `sortGames` pure function outside the component.

pr.body:
Upgrade node-forge to fix Ed25519 signature malleability (CVE-2026-33895), RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 forgery (CVE-2026-33894), BigInteger modInverse DoS (CVE-2026-33891), and X.509 chain validation bypass (CVE-2026-33896).
⚠️ Breaking changes in this upgrade
All breaking changes by upgrading node-forge from version 1.3.3 to 1.4.0 ([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/digitalbazaar/forge/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)) | Version | Description | | --- | --- | | 
1.4.0
| `BigInteger.modInverse()` now exits early with zero when the target object value is <= 0, instead of entering an infinite loop | | 
1.4.0
| RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification now rejects signatures that lack the required minimum of 8 bytes of padding | | 
1.4.0
| RSA signature verification now rejects forged signatures with extra fields in the ASN.1 DigestInfo structure (requires sequence length of two) | | 
1.4.0
| Ed25519 signature verification now rejects non-canonical signatures where scalar S >= L (group order) | | 
1.4.0
| `pki.verifyCertificateChain()` now rejects certificate chains where intermediate certificates lack `basicConstraints` extension |
✅ 4 CVEs resolved by this upgrade
This PR will resolve the following CVEs: | Issue | Severity           | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | 
[CVE-2026-33895](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/25518218/detail?groupId=69598#CVE-2026-33895)
| 
HIGH
| [node-forge] Ed25519 signature verification accepts forged non-canonical signatures where the scalar S is not reduced modulo the group order, allowing signature malleability attacks that bypass authentication and authorization logic. Applications relying on signature uniqueness for deduplication, replay tracking, or canonicalization checks may be compromised. | | 
[CVE-2026-33894](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/25518218/detail?groupId=69598#CVE-2026-33894)
| 
HIGH
| [node-forge] RSASSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts forged signatures for low public exponent keys (e=3) due to insufficient ASN.1 structure validation and missing minimum padding length checks, enabling Bleichenbacher-style signature forgery attacks. This allows attackers to forge valid signatures that pass verification despite being rejected by standard implementations like OpenSSL. | | 
[CVE-2026-33891](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/25518218/detail?groupId=69598#CVE-2026-33891)
| 
HIGH
| [node-forge] A Denial of Service vulnerability exists in the BigInteger.modInverse() function due to an infinite loop when called with zero input, causing the process to hang indefinitely and consume 100% CPU. An attacker can trigger this by sending crafted cryptographic parameters (e.g., malicious DSA/ECDSA signatures) to any application using this library. | | 
[CVE-2026-33896](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/25518218/detail?groupId=69598#CVE-2026-33896)
| 
HIGH
| [node-forge] Certificate chain verification fails to enforce RFC 5280 basicConstraints requirements, allowing leaf certificates without basicConstraints and keyUsage extensions to act as intermediate CAs and sign other certificates that are accepted as valid. |
pr.title: [Aikido] Fix security issue in node-forge via minor version upgrade from 1.3.3 to 1.4.0

pr.body:
This pull request introduces a new feature that allows users to share their library statistics directly to a Discord channel via a webhook. It includes both frontend and backend changes to support Discord webhook configuration, image generation and sharing, and UI improvements for stats sharing.

Key changes include:

**Discord Webhook Integration**

* Added Discord webhook configuration to the settings page, allowing users to save and manage their webhook URL. The backend provides endpoints to get and set this configuration securely. **Stats Sharing Functionality**

* Introduced a new `ShareDiscordDialog` component that lets users select which stats to include, generates a styled image of their stats using `html-to-image`, and handles sharing to Discord with user feedback.
* Added a "Share to Discord" button to the stats page, opening the share dialog and integrating the new sharing workflow. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a76281a1ccb3b7e1bbf7bb85b317cbc8f396177c38e4fec63a28b6ebbf7070bfR17-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a76281a1ccb3b7e1bbf7bb85b317cbc8f396177c38e4fec63a28b6ebbf7070bfR65-R78)

This pull request introduces a new Helm chart for the `questarr` application, enabling Kubernetes-based deployment and configuration. The chart includes templates for deployment, service, ingress, persistent storage, secrets management, and customizable values, providing a comprehensive and flexible way to run `questarr` in Kubernetes environments.

The most important changes are:

**Helm Chart Introduction and Structure:**

* Added a new Helm chart for `questarr` with all standard chart files, including `Chart.yaml` for metadata and `values.yaml` for configurable parameters. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e10c9a14f1dafb62f4ae415664f766abec0492b7b76187180341ce0669340ccbR1-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fa52ba424067134d2f71c0db0ee1db8ab3f80381c71fadd434261d3a25bf369bR1-R88)
* Added Helm chart helper templates in `_helpers.tpl` to standardize naming, labels, and secret references.

**Kubernetes Manifests:**

* Added deployment template (`deployment.yaml`) for managing the `questarr` application pods, with support for environment variables, probes, persistent storage, and secret injection.
* Added service template (`service.yaml`) for exposing the application within the cluster, and ingress template (`ingress.yaml`) for optional external access with TLS and host/path configuration. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c591d4e5a97742ecdfee18e054b2b3c6de072c972ac21e80670220695ab63ce0R1-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-521be713b50fd208001c6a0a397fd8500d4bc2bdf72dfb41acc5958ccb45e327R1-R35)
* Added PVC template (`pvc.yaml`) to manage persistent storage for application data, configurable via values.
* Added secret template (`secret.yaml`) for securely managing sensitive environment variables, with support for user-provided or auto-generated secrets.

**User Guidance and Quality-of-life:**

* Added a `NOTES.txt` template to provide post-install instructions and access information for users deploying the chart.
* Updated `.prettierignore` to exclude the `helm/` directory from formatting.

This pull request adds support for users to specify and manage "preferred release groups" for game downloads. Users can now prioritize downloads from specific release groups, both in the UI and in the automatic download logic. The implementation includes database schema changes, UI components for configuration, and backend logic to honor these preferences during searches and downloads.

**User Settings and Database Changes:**

- Added two new fields to the `user_settings` table and schema: `preferred_release_groups` (a JSON-encoded list of group names) and `filter_by_preferred_groups` (a boolean to enable/disable filtering by these groups). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-514180d05db7c2c8db48946c8092aabe2e8204fa3e010724a685bc85dd7fc0b4R1-R2) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-248adfc01eb4816dcacc7b777efec7f15df5a4c21da1eaa3f5214b3eb61e1e9aR37-R40)

**Frontend: User Interface for Preferred Groups:**

- Introduced a new `PreferredReleaseGroupsSettings` component in the settings page, allowing users to add, remove, and save preferred release groups, as well as toggle filtering. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c0178aa54074ad44832d93ef430f70281678e931923f85057363e43d26fd2acbR1-R216) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ef86b78ab3a2fcb20b1b2b6d4acb9f78241d5b4c4583ea386e82b788f4aa688aR42) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ef86b78ab3a2fcb20b1b2b6d4acb9f78241d5b4c4583ea386e82b788f4aa688aR107-R108) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ef86b78ab3a2fcb20b1b2b6d4acb9f78241d5b4c4583ea386e82b788f4aa688aR137-R146) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-ef86b78ab3a2fcb20b1b2b6d4acb9f78241d5b4c4583ea386e82b788f4aa688aR695-R700)
